KSU faculty, staff, and students can log into the platform using their NetID via the OwlTrain website . Required Training for KSU Employees Right to Know Global Harmonized System When : Prior to your New Employee Orientation and annually each fall semester. Required By : the "Public Employee Hazardous Chemical Protection and Right to Know Act of 1988” (O.C.G.A. 45-22-2). Instructions : Sign in to your OwlTrain account. Under “My Assignments,” select “Launch Compliance Training.” Select “Right to Know.” Complete the 30 minute course. Description : As an employee of the State of Georgia, you have the right to know about hazardous chemicals in the workplace. Along with your right to know, recent federal regulations now provide you the “right to understand” with an updated Hazard Communication Standard (HCS). This new standard makes it easier for you to understand labels on hazardous chemicals and information in safety data sheets. The course is a linear series of slides designed to familiarize you with the basics of the Right to Know law. For questions about the content of this course see contact information below. contact us Environmental Health and Safety New Employee Training When: All new hires including employees who have been absent from work for over one year must complete this course within 30 days of hire. Required By: Federal Occupational Safety and Health Training Standards, State and USG policy. Instructions: Sign in to your OwlTrain account . Under “My Assignments,” select “Launch Compliance Training.” Select “Environmental Health and Safety New Employee Training E-C-22-V1 (WBT).” Complete the training in its entirety. Complete all “Test Your Knowledge” activities to the best of your ability. At the end of the course, you will be prompted to download the New Employee Orientation Safety Training Checklist . This form should be reviewed, completed, and signed by both you and your supervisor to document completion of job-specific orientation provided by the department. Send the completed, signed form to EHS at ehs@kennesaw.edu . Description: This New Employee Safety Orientation covers general safety procedures at Kennesaw State University (KSU). The objective of this training session is to give you a comprehensive safety orientation to your workplace, including understanding your role in KSU’s health and safety program; where to get safety information; identifying, mitigating, and reporting hazards; preventing and responding to fires and emergencies; responding to and reporting incidents; and evacuating campus facilities safely. For questions about the content of this course or employee training, please contact us below. email USG Required Ethics Training When: Within 30 days of employment and periodically as instructed. All employees must complete the current refresher course by December 23, 2021. Required By: the University System of Georgia Ethics Policy. Instructions: Log in to Owltrain and go to "My Assignments" to complete this training. Watch the entire 18 minute course including all videos with no skipping. Answer all questions correctly. Failure to score 80% correct will require you to re-take the course. Answer the policy acknowledgement question in the affirmative or you will not pass the course. Close the training window after watching the videos and answering all questions. Description: The University System of Georgia (USG) is committed to the highest ethical and professional standards of conduct in pursuit of its mission to create a more educated Georgia. Accomplishing this mission demands integrity, good judgment, and dedication to public service from all members of the USG community. While the USG affirms each person’s accountability for individual actions, it also recognizes that the shared mission and the shared enterprise of its institutions require a shared set of core values and ethical conduct to which each member of the USG community must be held accountable. Furthermore, the USG acknowledges that an organizational culture grounded in trust is essential to supporting these core values and ethical conduct. View this link to access the USG Ethics Policy, which includes USG Core Values and Code of Conduct . For questions about the content of this course see contact information below. contact us KSU Conflict of Interest Training When: Within 30 days of employment and an annual refresher each fall semester. Required By: Kennesaw State University. Instructions: Log in to Owltrain and go to "My Assignments" to complete this training. Watch the entire 8 minute course including all videos with no skipping. Answer all questions correctly. Failure to score 2 out of 3 correct will require you to re-take the course. Close the training window after watching the videos and answering all questions. Then review and complete the Outside Activity & Conflict of Interest disclosure form. Description: All Kennesaw State University employees must avoid or manage real or perceived conflicts of interest regarding their KSU duties. To do so, employees must be able to recognize conflicts of interest, and they should know how to disclose those conflicts of interest. For questions about the content of this course please contact us below. email Clery Act Training When: Within 30 days of employment and an annual refresher each fall semester. Required By: the Clery Act Federal Statute 20 U.S.C. § 1092(f). Clery Act New Employee Training Instructions: Log in to Owltrain and go to "My Assignments" to complete this training. Watch the entire 20 minute course including all videos with no skipping. Answer all questions correctly. Failure to score 100% correct will require you to re-take the course. Close the training window after watching the videos and answering all questions. When the course is over complete and submit the CSA Acknowledgement form. Clery Act Annual Refresher Training Instructions: Log in to Owltrain and go to "My Assignments" to complete this training. Watch the entire 8 minute course including all videos with no skipping. Answer all questions correctly. Failure to score 100% correct will require you to re-take the course. Close the training window after watching the videos and answering all questions. When the course is over complete and submit an updated CSA Acknowledgement form. Description: This training will familiarize participants with the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act. The Jeanne Clery Act is a federal law that requires colleges and universities across the United States to disclose information about crime on and around their campuses. For questions about the content of this course please contact us below. email USG Cybersecurity Awareness Training When: Within 30 days of employment, new employees must complete the 10 minute “New Hire's Guide to Security Awareness” training available from the KSU KnowBe4 Cybersecurity Training Portal . In addition, the State of Georgia requires all employees to complete cybersecurity awareness training twice annually. These trainings are available beginning in April (for the Spring training) and October (for the Fall training) and you will have 30 days to complete the training after each training announcement email is received. Required By: USG IT Handbook Section 5.9.2 Instructions: Log in to the KnowBe4 Cybersecurity Training Portal . and go to "My Assignments" to complete this training. Watch the 10 minute video. Complete the, 5-question, post-assessment quiz with a score of 80% or higher. Click the “Exit Course” link in the training window to earn a completed status. Description: This short module covers the basics of security and provides a few helpful action items that every individual can quickly understand and apply to their day-to-day functions. For questions about the content of this course contact the Office of Cyber Security below. email Sexual Misconduct Prevention and Awareness Training When: Within 60 days of receiving the e-mail with registration and completion information and an annual refresher each fall semester. Required By: KSU and federal requirements under Title IX of the Education Amendments Act of 1972 and Section 304(a)(5) of the Violence Against Women Reauthorization Act of 2013 (known as the "Campus SaVE Act"). Faculty and Staff will receive a notice from Vector LMS <Kennesaw State University> with a link to their annually required Sexual Misconduct Prevention and Awareness Training. Click the link to complete the training. Note: this training is provided by an external vendor and will not show in your Owltrain learning plan or transcript. Using your web browser, go to the Vector LMS, Higher Education Edition website for Kennesaw State University Employees. Building Supportive Communities: Clery & Title IX New and returning employees will receive an email from Kennesaw State University Online Training < automated-message@everfi.net> with access to the course. Complete the 60 minute course and answer all questions. Building Supportive Communities: Clery & Title IX, is a web-based, interactive training program for faculty and staff that includes scenarios and examples you may face around sexual assault, domestic violence, dating violence, stalking and sexual harassment. This program will provide you and your colleagues with important skills and resources to help foster a safe, inclusive, and healthy campus environment. For login or technical issues, please visit Vector LMS learner support page . For questions about this course please contact the Office of Institutional Equity below. Please note: UITS does not provide technical support for these modules. For any technical assistance with the Vector LMS courses, please visit Vector LMS, Higher Education Edition contact page. email KSU Driver Qualification Program When: Prior to operating any vehicle on KSU business and annually on the anniversary of completion. Required By: Kennesaw State University Policy and Board of Regents Policy. Official Code of Georgia Section 50-19-1 through Section 50-19-9 and Section 50-5-141. DOAS Comprehensive Loss Control Program (CLCP). Level 1 - Motor Vehicle Operator Training Instructions: 1. Log in to Owltrain and go to "My Assignments" to complete this training. 2. Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the 16 minute long course Description: This program is to establish basic driver training required for ALL employees (full time, part time, student workers, occasional or temporary workers) of KSU who drive University owned or controlled vehicles, rental vehicles, personal vehicles for KSU business or low speed vehicles such as golf carts, Gators, Mules etc. This training is a requirement if an employee is travelling between campus locations, transporting of employees, students or guests, driving to meetings, driving to a conference or completing any University business that requires driving, regardless of vehicle ownership or driving frequency. This training is also an acknowledgement of State policies for driving. Level 2 - National Safety Council’s Defensive... Instructions: Go to: National Safety Council's Defensive Driving Course and log on with your NetID & Password. Select a session of the National Safety Council’s Defensive Driving Course. Attend and complete the Instructor Led Training Session for the date you selected. Description: Defensive Driving is required for all approved drivers who operate a state vehicle, rent a vehicle or drive their own personal vehicle for KSU Business. The goal of the National Safety Council’s (NSC) Defensive Driving Course is to provide drivers with knowledge and safe driving techniques to prevent collisions and violations. This State recognized, 6 hour course focuses on collision prevention though hazard recognition and the application of collision-avoidance techniques. In addition, the course addresses common driving violations that result in collisions and how to change driving habits to eliminate moving violations. **If it is determined that an employee will NEVER drive on behalf of KSU and claims exemption for any reason, the employee must complete the KSU Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) Exemption form. You will not be authorized to operate any vehicle for KSU business. Remember exemption from this program also excludes the employee from liability insurance coverage under the State Tort Claims Act, and you will not have the same immunity from personal liability as other State employees.** For questions about these courses course please contact us below. email Additional Courses May Be Required Depending on Job Duties and Exposure to Risk eProcurement and P-card training FERPA records privacy Travel Management (Concur) Position-specific Environmental Health & Safety training Programs Serving Minors View our HR Training Calendar Training & Professional Development Approval Form This form is required for certain training and professional development activities to ensure compliance with University System of Georgia (USG) requirements and proper documentation of employee development. Submit this form if you are: Creating or delivering internal training for a KSU audience. If a mandatory training request is submitted, it will be routed to the CHRO for approval. Requesting approval for individual professional development (such as certifications or specialized training) Presenting or facilitating training externally on behalf of KSU This form is not required for: Employees attending KSU-sponsored programs or internal training Conference attendance unless you are presenting on behalf of KSU Informal learning opportunities such as webinars or informational sessions Required Documentation Supporting materials such as agendas, course descriptions, presentations or certification information must be attached. Incomplete submissions may delay review. Processing Timeline Due to the volume of submissions, approval may take up to two (2) weeks from the date of submission. You will receive notification via the email provided once your request has been reviewed. If the request includes a certification, professional license, or specialized credentialing, then you will receive a second approval email from Financial Compliance. Training and Development Resources KSU Community and Professional Education KSU Community and Professional Education (KSU CPE) is committed to empowering lifelong learners to achieve their career and educational goals. To assist in that mission, KSU offers substantial discounts to current employees. The exact amount will vary based on the cost of course materials. For more information regarding this benefit, please review the discount guidelines or contact KSU Community and Professional Education. CPE CLASS REQUEST FORM Class Registration Benefits Employees who are also students at KSU may be eligible to register for classes during Early Registration which occurs at the very beginning of the normal Priority Registration period. Eligible employees may have their supervisor authorize the registrar's office to assign early registration status prior to each semester. Those employees excluded from the early registration benefit include transient students, those participating in the Tuition Assistance Program and those on academic probation. New students and students being readmitted must wait one term to become eligible for early registration benefits. For more information regarding early registration benefits, contact the Registrar's Office. This directory provide a clearer view of how departments and individuals are aligned across the university, improving visibility into organizational structure and reporting relationships. Student Access Now that the directory is live, all employees are encouraged to review their information and confirm that their work location is correct. Keeping this information up to date helps ensure the directory reflects KSU as it operates today and supports future planning, reporting, and operational improvements. Faculty/Staff Access How to Use the Employee Directory Resources 1-page reference sheet: How to make updates to the Employee Directory How to Submit the Employee Location Update Request in the KSU Facilities Portal How to Locate a Space for an Employee Using the KSU Facilities Portal How to Update a Mail Drop in the KSU Directory Departmental Hierarchy The departmental hierarchy is an important view of KSU’s organizational structure. It depicts the departmental reporting relationships and represents a clear view of the work being performed within the university. The hierarchy supports KSU’s mission by promoting transparency, facilitating communication, and clarifying decision-making pathways.​ There are 5 levels in the department hierarchy based upon the existing organization of university academic and administrative functions. Level 1: President ​ Level 2: Division (Cabinet level - directly reports to the President) ​ Level 3a: Academic College OR 3b: Business Unit​ Level 4: Department ( OR Research Center OR Institute) ​ Level 5: Ancillary Department ( OR Research Center OR Institute)​ Brief Definitions Academic College: A major academic unit led by a Dean, overseeing related departments and programs.​ Business Unit: A major administrative unit managing key operational functions. ​ Department: A specialized academic or administrative unit within a college, business unit, or division. It focuses on a specific discipline or function and is responsible for delivering programs, services, or operations aligned with its area of expertise. Departments are usually staffed by faculty or professional employees and have at least one physical location.​ Ancillary Department: A department recognized as providing support to the primary activities or operations within the scope assigned to a parent Department. ​ Research Center: Supports research and continuing education. Typically affiliated with a department and does not offer credit courses or degrees.​ Institute: More formalized structure and potentially autonomous. Our resources cover key aspects of managerial responsibilities, including strategies for enhancing employee engagement, approved training programs, a guide to the employee separation process, details on alternative work schedules, and information about the New Manager Orientation series. Explore these tools and process steps to better support your role in creating a positive and productive work environment at KSU! Manager Toolkits TITLE DESCRIPTION Dual Appointment Agreement (DAA) Toolkit Use this toolkit when submitting a DAA request. Employee Engagement Toolkit for Managers This toolkit was designed to empower KSU managers to improve employee engagement through teambuilding, recognition and appreciation. Modified Operations Frequently asked questions for campus closures vs. modified operations. Onboarding Toolkit As you onboard your new employees, please use this resource to make their departmental onboarding experience a remarkable extension of KSU Orientation. Separation of Employment Below are the steps for the Offboarding Process with instructions on how to process each type of employee separation at KSU. HR Offboarding Process Employee submits termination notice Manager creates MSS transaction HR starts the separation process KSU property is collected Exit interview is conducted Employee Separation Types Resignation (voluntary) Employee must give written notice to supervisor and a copy to Human Resources. The minimum notice is generally ten (10) working days. MSS Termination transaction should be submitted as soon as possible. The effective date should be one (1) calendar day after the last date worked or the last active date on payroll. Upon receipt of the submitted MSS Termination request, HR will send an email to the supervisor with a Manager Checklist for Separation . Managers should complete and send to your HR Coordinator. Reference KSU Employee Handbook , Section 1.8, Termination Guidelines for more information. Human Resource Coordinator will send an email to the separating employee’s personal email (not their KSU email) that will include the following: Separation Checklist for employees Exit Memorandum Information on benefits USG Exit Survey Instructions to schedule Exit Interview Department of Labor (DOL) Notice Your HR Coordinator will review the MSS termination transaction and request removal of the following accesses, if applicable: Door access Time clock Parking deductions Email access HR Coordinator will enter data for the Vacation Pay Out (VPO) if applicable, and compile separation documents to be sent to the employee’s personnel records. The institution is not obligated to allow an employee to rescind the resignation. The supervisor may designate an earlier final date of employment. Manager should send an email to terminate leaving employees access and responsibilities that their position required. Please email service@kennesaw.edu to transfer IT equipment to appropriate department or person. Request removal of employee’s access to any propriety software used by the department of group, such as SAS, Banner, Onbase, PeopleSoft,ePro,OwlPay, etc. Request transfer or close out of email resources account owned/managed by this employee. Involuntary/Termination Supervisors who are considering a suspension, demotion, or dismissal of an employee must contact Human Resources to ensure that all appropriate laws, regulations, and policies are observed. The effective date is immediate. Examples include: Violation of Rules Unsatisfactory Performance Probationary Period No Show Job Abandonment Gross Misconduct Failure to Return from leave No Work Authorization-NRA An employee affected by demotion, suspension, or dismissal will be informed in writing of the reasons for the action taken. The effective date of demotion or suspension shall be five (5) days following the notification. Employees affected by a demotion, suspension, or dismissal may appeal to the next level of authority within five (5) working days of the notification of the action. The employee will be entitled to a procedural protection of a hearing before a Board of Review (Grievance Policy). This request must be made within ten (10) working days following the documented adverse action. Grievance Policy is not applicable for employees terminated during KSU’s provisional period or temporary employees. Note: Before you move towards involuntary termination please be sure to contact your HR Business Partner to discuss first. Retirement Meet with your Human Resource Benefits Specialist to discuss your retirement date, timing and next steps. Meet with your ORP Retirement Advisor for a one on-one session to review your portfolio and request illustrations of your retirement distribution options. Meet with TRS or ERS to initiate the retirement process and confirm your date of retirement. Then, complete your retirement packet online. Confirm your retirement date with HR and announce dates to department chair/dean or supervisor. If you’re eligible and would like your Social Security benefits to begin at the time of retirement, apply at least six (6) months prior to your retirement date. Your TRS, ERS or ORP Retirement If you are a member of the Teachers Retirement System of Georgia (TRS), or Employees Retirement System of Georgia (ERS), schedule an appointment with TRS or ERS to discuss your eligibility to retire, your benefit amount at retirement, and how you plan to provide for your beneficiaries. Call your retirement system directly: TRS at 1-404-352-6500 or ERS at 1-404-350-6300. Create an online account by visiting www.trsga.com . Review the TRS retirement checklist online. If you are a member of the Optional Retirement Plan (ORP), schedule a financial counseling appointment with your retirement vendor to discuss your distribution options. Call them directly: AIG: 1-800-448-2542, Fidelity: 1-800-343-0860, or TIAA: 1-800-842-2252. Access your account(s) online by visiting AIG, Fidelity, and TIAA. If you currently participate in 403(b) or 457(b) you should start meeting with your plan advisor to discuss plan distribution options. If you’re not currently participating and would like additional information, please visit the 403(b) and 457(b) Plans page or call CAPTRUST for more information at 1-800-967-9948. Please note : Up to 360 hours of unused vacation time is paid out by the next pay period after your retirement. If you are a TRS retiree, unused sick time can count toward your retirement service time and is unlimited. Unused sick time does not apply toward ORP retirement. Contact TRS or visit the website for your conversion options. Transfer to Another Institution Internal Transfer – The shift of an employee from one position to another of the same classification or to one with comparable skills and in the same general pay range in the same institution. The employee who is affected by an internal transfer will continue all benefits uninterrupted. The employee will not restart the provisional period. External Transfer – The movement of an employee from a position at one institution within the University System to a position at another institution or to/from the University System Office. Since institutional compensation practices may differ due to market conditions, the transfer may be to a position at a different pay range, but the provisions of this transfer policy shall apply. In the event of an external transfer, accumulated sick leave, retirement benefits and service continuity will be transferred if the break in service does not exceed thirty (30) calendar days. When the external transfer occurs with no break in service, an employee must transfer accrued vacation leave of between one (1) and twenty (20) days. For employees with accrued vacation leave of greater than twenty (20) days, the employee may elect one of the following options: Transfer of the total accrued vacation balance, not to exceed forty-five (45) days. Payment by the institution from which the employee is moving of accrued vacation leave greater than twenty (20) days. The total accrued vacation leave for which the employee may be paid shall not exceed twenty-five (25) days. The transferring employee will restart the provisional period at the new location effective on the first day of employment and serve their first six (6) months in a provisional status, subject to all terms and conditions of the provisional period policy. When an employee terminates from one institution and is then hired by another System institution, this shall not constitute an external transfer. If the termination and subsequent hiring occurs with less than thirty (30) days between the actions, the Chief Human Resources Officer of new employer may choose to treat such an action as an external transfer under this policy at their sole discretion. This policy ensures consistency among institutions of the University System regarding the transfer of employees with the institution and from one University System institution to another, including the University System office. The policy also ensures consistency as necessary for meeting applicable reporting requirements while also affording the appropriate level of flexibility needed at the institutional level. Alternative Work Schedule and Telecommute Policy Kennesaw State University’s Teleworking and Alternative Work Schedule Policy outlines creative approaches for completing work while promoting balance between work life and personal life commitments. Options available under this policy include teleworking, flextime, and compressed work week schedules. Adoption of alternative work schedule arrangements requires the approval of the supervisor and must be in compliance with HR policies and practices. For more information regarding alternative work schedule options, follow the links listed below. Request Forms Alternative Work Schedule Request Telework Arrangement Request For further questions regarding the alternative work schedule policy, contact your HR Partner . OneUSG is a system-wide initiative to develop and implement a consistent approach to policies, procedures and technology solutions that benefit the University System of Georgia (USG), in an effort to reduce costs, streamline processes, and have uniform guidelines with centralized support. OneUSG Connect manages USG human resources activities, benefits and compensation including: Approving time and absence requests from your employees. Requesting an employee reporting change or location change. Submitting requests to transfer or separate an employee. Submitting requests for pay changes or one-time payments. Viewing or submit requests for position funding changes. Electronically Submitting requests formerly processed through paper Personnel Action Forms (PAF) and Faculty Status Change Forms. HAVE QUESTIONS OR WANT TO LEARN MORE? Contact the USG Shared Services Center at 877-251-2644, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., or by email: support@usg.edu There are Many Benefits for Using OneUSG Connect It’s easy to use and can automate some of the current manual hiring and onboarding processes such as: Handles job openings, job postings, applicants, resumes, interviews and offers. From ordering business cards and arranging travel through Concur to accessing team practice facilities and understanding compliance software like Jumpforward and Blackbaud, this guide covers everything you need to get started. Whether you're a coach or administrative staff, this onboarding guide will ensure a seamless integration into the KSU Athletics family. Athletics Business Office The Athletics Business Office at Kennesaw State supports staff with administrative tasks like ordering business cards and managing travel. Conference travel is handled through Concur, while other travel uses Anthony Travel or Blackbaud. Office supply needs can be coordinated through the office's purchasing process below. Business Department See Cara Gaskins cgaskin7@kennesaw.edu . Business Card See Office Manager ( kstep105@kennesaw.edu ) to order your business cards. Travel (Concur) i. KSU Facilities for Team Practice and Competition KSU's Athletics facilities provide top-tier venues for team practice and competition! From Stillwell Stadium to the Convocation Center, and specialized sites like the Sports Performance Facility and Athletics Rehabilitation Center, these state-of-the-art locations provide support for the success and development of KSU's student-athletes across all of our sports. Stillwell Stadium Convocation Center Practice Facility Sports & Entertainment Park Track Sports & Entertainment Park "The Perch" Sport & Entertainment Park Rugby Field Pinetree Golf Club Betty Siegel Courts Marietta Country Club Fifth Third Bank Stadium Bailey Park Golf Indoor Practice Facility Sports Performance Facility Student Athlete Success Services Athletics Rehabilitation Center Bobby Bailey Athletic Complex New KSU Owl Coaches Check out key tools available for our new KSU coaches, including access to athletics facilities like Marietta Country Club and Fifth Third Bank Stadium, and instructions on using compliance software like Jumpforward and Blackbaud. We hope to also provide in-depth guidance on handling away game contracts, ensuring that all requirements are met before submission. Jumpforward This is the compliance software used by coaches ONLY and compliance to track roster management, eligibility, financial aid and recruiting. Please see a Compliance staff member to get assigned to Jumpforward. Blackbaud System used for coaches (and staff) that travel for all purposes EXCEPT conferences (for conferences, see Concur). Away Game Contracts Checklist Receiving Away Game Contract When you receive an away game contract, check to verify that: The contracting party is The Kennesaw State University Athletic Association, Inc. No signatures are included (the contract is unsigned). Contract is in an editable form (a word document or unscanned PDF). If you receive a contract that meets the above requirements, upload the contract into the Contract Management System for approval. Contract That Does Not Meet Requirements If you receive a contract that does not meet the above requirements: Reach back out to the sender to request an updated document that meets the requirements; If you do not hear back from the sender within a few business days, forward the contract and last email received on the game to Breana Ware in the Division of Legal Affairs; Upload the contract into the Contract Management System with a note that you have attempted to contact the original sender. Campus Services Serving KSU by providing the essentials of campus life. Campus Services includes the departments listed below. The KSU Bookstore provides educational resources, spirit wear, technology from OwlTEC (an Apple-Authorized Campus Store) and more from their two convenient locations. Campus Postal Services manages the delivery, collection and processing of all interoffice and U.S. Postal Service mail on campus. Central Receiving and Distribution (CRD) processes delivery items, packages and freight orders to on-campus warehouses. Housing and Residence Life is responsible for 10 on-campus residence halls at KSU, and oversees all functions of the residential communities that serve 5,900 students who live on campus. Vending Services offers beverage and snack vending in convenient locations on campus Community and Professional Education Community and Professional Education offers courses for personal development and professional advancement in high-demand fields. CPE provides professional certificate programs in Business & Management, Computer-Aided Design, Culinary, Data Science and Analytics, Legal, Marketing, and many other areas of focus. CPE also offers personal enrichment classes in Art, Cooking, Finance, Health and Fitness, Photography, Travel and more through their Osher Lifelong Learning Institute (OLLI) program for adults 50+. In accordance with DOAS, CR&D facilitates identification, redistribution and disposal of KSU property including office furniture, equipment and supplies. The service team assists with interoffice or intercampus moves. Hours, Locations, and Contact Information Central Receiving Warehouse Hours: Monday - Friday from 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM Surplus Hours: Open Fridays 9:00 AM – 2:00 PM Kennesaw Warehouse Address: 3305 Busbee Dr., Suite 100, Kennesaw, GA 30144 Marietta Warehouse Address: 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060 KSU Surplus Warehouse Address: 3305 Busbee Drive, NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144 (Formerly Known as BrandsMart) Central Receiving Office Hours: Monday - Friday from 7:30 AM – 4:00 PM Phone: 470-578-3614 Email: centralrecanddistr@kennesaw.edu Receiving Freight orders must be coordinated ahead of delivery with CR&D staff and campus partners. Please contact us at 470-578-3614 or centralrecanddistr@kennesaw.edu to schedule delivery to the warehouse. Deliveries Kennesaw Warehouse Address: 3305 Busbee Dr., Suite 100, Kennesaw, GA 30144 Marietta Warehouse Address: 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060 A signature is required for all packages. CR&D cannot accept hazardous materials which include, but are not limited to, chemicals, radioactive waste, alcoholic beverages, oils/lubricants, batteries, lab specimens, live animals, perishables or refrigerated items. Items received by CR&D are distributed to customers as soon as possible. While you may receive a delivery notification from a carrier, your shipment will take 24-48 business hours for on-campus processing and delivery. Please note that IT equipment will take longer to process. Packages with accurate on-campus addresses should be delivered directly to campus customers. Campus Moves and Surplus Pick Ups and Deliveries To schedule a furniture or supply move, surplus pick up or surplus delivery, please submit a request to the KSU Facilities Portal. To schedule a move that includes IT equipment and furniture, please complete the Campus Moves form . Allow 7-10 business days for work order completion of non-IT requests.Please note: work order completion may exceed our normal time frame due to increased request volume, particularly from May to August. Campus partners will receive a phone call or email to schedule pick ups and deliveries. Service and Surplus cannot move or accept hazardous materials which include, but are not limited to chemicals, radioactive waste, oils/lubricants, batteries, lab specimens, live animals, perishables or refrigerated items. CR&D will reuse your moving boxes. Once your move is complete, please break down your boxes and submit an Facilities Portal request for pick up. Asset Transfers to Surplus Please complete an Asset Transfer form to transfer assets to surplus. Assets are defined as items or equipment with a value of $3,000 or more. Each asset must be listed on an asset transfer form and signed by a department representative or office manager. KSU Surplus Warehouse *Surplus items/equipment are for official KSU use only.* KSU Surplus Warehouse Address: 3305 Busbee Drive, NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144 (formerly known as BrandsMart) The KSU Surplus Warehouse is open to KSU faculty and staff only. Items are available on a first-come, first-serve basis. Before visiting, please measure your office space to ensure the items you select will fit in your space. Be sure to consider windows, doors and other structural features that may impede placement of new furniture. We cannot install furniture that violates ADA guidelines, interferes with egress, blocks a window or creates any other type of safety hazard. We accomplish this by offering thorough maintenance, repair, and installation services for essential building systems. Our team is committed to maintaining and improving the campus environment, ensuring all facilities are safe, functional, and efficient. We are proud to support the university’s mission by delivering exceptional services throughout KSU. Our Services Include: Carpentry Electrical Energy Management Engineering Mechanical (HVAC) Plumbing Emergency Procedure Call KSU Police Department for situations requiring – Police Department, Fire Department, Ambulance/EMS Call: 470-578-6666 or 911 Plant Operations Carpentry Builds, repairs and maintains campus structures to ensure safety, durability, and quality craftsmanship. Electrical Installs, repairs and maintains campus electrical systems to ensure reliable power and lighting. Energy Management Optimizes campus energy and water use while promoting sustainability through efficiency, innovation and engagement. Engineering Supports MEP systems and manages major repairs to ensure code compliance and campus reliability. Mechanical Maintains and repairs HVAC systems to ensure comfort, safety and efficient campus operations. Plumbing Maintains water and drainage systems to ensure reliable, efficient service across campus. Submitting a Work Request To submit a work request, please use the KSU Facilities Portal. What to do if you smell gas? This is a reminder that Kennesaw State University is served by natural gas. If you smell natural gas (rotten egg smell) or hear a hissing sound coming from piping while on campus, please leave the area immediately and call 470-578-6666 or 911 from a safe location. If you are inside a building, while exiting, do not turn on or off light switches. Do not use the telephone or do anything that may create a spark. Also, there should be no digging on campus without notifying Facilities Services first at 470-578-6224 , as damage to the natural gas pipeline may occur. Maintenance Related Emergencies Leaking Pipes and Overflowing Toilets Storm Damage, etc. Electrical Power Disruption Gas Leak Contact Us Normal hours of operation are Monday through Friday from 7:30 AM to 4 PM. Phone: 470-578-6224 Email: plantops@kennesaw.edu After Hours/Emergency: 470-578-6666 Carpentry The Carpentry Shop is responsible for the construction, repair, and maintenance of general structural components across campus. Skilled carpenters within the department manage a wide range of projects designed to support and enhance the structural integrity of university facilities. Electrical The Electrical Shop installs, maintains, and repairs electrical systems throughout the university. From lighting and power distribution to emergency backup systems, the department’s skilled electricians work diligently to ensure that campus facilities remain reliably powered and properly illuminated. Energy Management The Energy Management Department at Kennesaw State University employs a holistic and continuous strategy to improve energy and water efficiency, emphasizing equipment optimization and the reduction of utility consumption and costs. The department’s objective is to minimize resource use while supporting effective campus operations. In addition, it fosters a culture of mindfulness by encouraging students, faculty, and staff to engage in practices that promote the conservation of university resources. Internship Opportunity in Energy Management Each semester, Plant Operations offers internship opportunities in which students collaborate with the Energy Manager and the Plant Operations team to enhance operational efficiency across campus. Responsibilities may include analyzing utility data, generating reports using building automation systems (BAS) and energy management software (EMS), evaluating potential savings opportunities, and studying Kennesaw State University’s power grid. Interns gain practical, hands-on experience that expands their technical knowledge and supports their long-term professional development. Engineering The Engineering Department within Plant Operations provides comprehensive engineering support for the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems across all Kennesaw State University properties, ensuring compliance with applicable standards and code requirements. In addition to technical support, the department oversees the university’s Major Repair and Rehabilitation (MRR) program and manages capital renewal and MEP system modification projects. Services: Oversee the MRR program to support the capital renewal of campus facilities Provide engineering expertise and project management for Plant Operations departments Maintain and manage university-owned utility distribution systems on all campuses Collaborating with Planning, Design, and Construction and Environmental Health and Safety on projects involving existing MEP infrastructure Support university departments in addressing their MEP system needs Manage documentation related to building MEP systems and underground utility distribution systems across campus Mechanical The Mechanical Shop is responsible for the maintenance and repair of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems throughout the university. The department ensures that all mechanical equipment operates efficiently and reliably, supporting a comfortable and safe environment for students, faculty, and staff. Plumbing The Plumbing Shop manages the university’s water supply and drainage systems. The department handles routine maintenance as well as emergency repairs, ensuring that plumbing fixtures and systems operate effectively to support the daily needs of the campus community. Frequently Asked Questions What is the typical response time for a maintenance request? Your request will be acknowledged within 24 hours by an assigned technician. Response times vary based on the urgency of the request. Emergency issues are prioritized, while routine requests are addressed in the order received. What is the temperature setpoint in each building? Kennesaw State University’s temperature policy sets a minimum cooling temperature of 72°F and a maximum heating temperature of 70°F, with a comfortable range between 66°F and 76°F maintained to achieve energy savings. During extended unoccupied periods, building temperatures will be kept between 60°F and 80°F to further conserve energy. What is the difference between a work order and project request? Plant Operations will maintain existing conditions (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing & Carpentry). We do not install new services or modifications to buildings including building structure, walls, doors, floors, etc. These types of modifications must go through Planning, Design, and Construction and require submission of a project form and approval of department funding How do I request custodial services for my area? Please submit a work order through KSU Facilities Portal. What should I do during a building power outage? In case of a power outage, please report the issue immediately. Backup power systems will activate in critical areas. KSU is dedicated to providing a safe and healthy environment for those who participate, volunteer and work in University sponsored programs, or programs operated by third parties held on University facilities. In conjunction with BOR Policy - Programs Serving Minors Kennesaw State University established KSU Programs Serving Minors Policy on May 1, 2017. This policy governs all KSU programs involving minors to ensure compliance with federal and state laws and the BOR/USG policies. Key areas of focus under this policy are registration, education and compliance. KSU staff, faculty and sponsoring departments of programs that involve minors should review the Program Serving Minors website, training and resources to become familiar with the policies, procedures and requirements needed to comply with both BOR and KSU policies. KSU Policies Relating to Minors on Campus KSU Programs Serving Minors Policy The purpose of the KSU Programs Serving Minors Policy is to provide guidance to the campus community and ensure compliance with federal and state laws and the BOR/USG policies and procedures. This policy was presented to KSU governance bodies for feedback in November/December, 2016. On December 13, 2016 the KSU President approved this policy to post on the Policy at KSU website and to submit to the BOR as required by January 1, 2017. The effective date for this policy is Monday, May 1, 2017. KSU Employee Handbook 5.4.5 Children in the Workplace The KSU Employee Handbook 5.2.12 Children in the Workplace governs employees and their children on KSU campuses and states: "The University cannot accommodate children of employees and students on campus during normal operating hours. Children are welcome to make brief visits and to attend scheduled events. KSU Institutional Review Board (IRB) The KSU Institutional Review Board (IRB) regulates all research activities involving human subjects on the campus of Kennesaw State University, including research activities involving minors. KSU requires prior review and approval from the IRB for all research involving human participants. KSU University Handbook Policy 5.2.13 Visits by Children KSU University Handbook Policy 5.3.3 Visits by Children governs visits by children on KSU campuses and states: "The university cannot accommodate children of the faculty, staff, and students on campus during normal operating hours; i.e., 8:00 a.m. - 10:30 p.m., Monday through Thursday, and 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m., Friday. Children are welcome to attend scheduled events and to make brief visits when accompanied by a parent or other adult." Upload a Photo and Government ID for Your Mobile Talon Card Psst... DO THIS NOW! Take a passport-style photo facing forward on a white background without any moulding, corners or ceiling showing. For the best user experience, please follow these instructions on your mobile device using the Transact eAccounts app to upload a new photo: Select “Kennesaw State University” from the list of schools. Sign in with your KSU Net ID — make sure you have set up Multifactor Authentication (MFA), it is required to submit your photo. Click the Settings tool and select “Submit ID Photo” and “Get Started.” Read and agree to the Terms and Conditions. Review the Photo Requirements and tap to upload your photo (or take a photo). Once you have added your photo, tap where prompted to upload a photo of your ID document (current US driver’s license, current passport, current government ID). Tap “Submit & Sign Out.” You will receive confirmation on your screen as well as through your KSU email. Once your photo has been approved by KSU Talon One Service Center staff, you will receive additional instructions for accessing your Mobile Talon Card via KSU email. More Photo Guidelines Purchase a Parking Permit Spring 2027 Spring Permit Selection will open in early January. Visit the Parking Permit website for permit selection dates, permit details, and more! Student Parking Areas Tip: One of the statements you will agree to is that you've reviewed our rules and regulations , so be sure you indeed read them! Visit the KSU Bookstore Purchasing your course materials is easy! If your professor has selected Day One Access (D1A) course, the materials can be accessed on the first day of class through D2L Brightspace . Your student account will be charged after you register for a class. If you choose to opt-out or leave the class during the drop/add period, your account will be credited back the cost. All other course materials can be purchased by visiting the KSU Bookstore website . Select the term, department and course section, then click "View Your Materials." When purchasing other books, login using SSO to view the complete booklist. Stop by the KSU Bookstore or shop online to show your school spirit with KSU branded apparel and take advantage of your educational discount on technology purchases from OwlTEC. Personalize Your Meal Plan KSU's dining program is one of the best in the nation. Whether you live on campus or commute, we have a Meal Plan to fit your needs. Our dining program offers a wide variety of restaurants and dining locations across both campuses. Purchase or upgrade your Meal Plan today to save before classes start! Meal Plans Housing Spring 2027 We are currently on a waitlist for all populations for Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 Housing. If you would like to join the Housing waitlist, please visit Housing’s Waitlist Webpage. 2027-28 Housing If you are interested in living on campus for the 2027-28 academic year, the First-Year Housing Application will open Tuesday, December 1, 2026, and the Upper Class Housing Application will open Wednesday, January 13, 2027. Visit the Housing website to learn more about Housing Applications. Housing Application Connect With Us! Check your student email account often for important information from Campus Services, and stay in the know about all of our departments by following us on Instagram and Facebook. To accommodate our guests as conveniently as possible, Parking and Transportation provides contactless parking payment through the ParkMobile app for visitors at both of our campuses. A $0.35 transaction fee will be added when using ParkMobile for payment. Pay-per-Plate kiosks are also available in each Visitor parking area. Parking Door Access Copier Services Dining Kennesaw Campus Lot A Visitor Parking (located near the Clendenin building on Kennesaw State University Road) | Zone number 35104 Chastain Pointe (located at the end of 200 Building) | Zone number 35108 Lot V2 (located outside of the Central Deck off of Parliament Garden Way) | Zone number 35101 Lot J (located off of Parliament Garden Way) | Zone number 35105 Lot L (located near Jolley Lodge on Canton Place NW) | Zone Number 35106 Kennesaw Campus Parking Map Marietta Campus Visitor Parking Lot (located off of Rossbacher Way) | Zone number 35103 Visitor Parking Lot (located off Walter Kelly Road) | Zone number 35107 West Deck on the second level in the spaces marked for visitor use | Zone number 35102 Marietta Campus Parking Map Once you park, please follow these steps: Download the ParkMobile app . Enter the zone number for the parking area using the number listed above, lot signage or the map in the app. Select the duration of time you want to park. Confirm your information and start your parking section. Monitor your session and extend time remotely if needed. Visitor Parking Rates Under 30 minute – $1 31 minutes to 1 hour – $3 1 hour to 2 hours – $6 2 hours to 3 hours – $8 3 hours to 4 hours – $10 Each additional 30 minutes – $1 Maximum Daily Rate – $12 Visitor Coupon Codes: If you are hosting a meeting or event for off-campus guests and would like to purchase a Coupon Code, please complete the Parking E-Coupon Code Request Form . Coupon code pricing aligns with visitor rates. The cost will be determined based on the parking timeframe your guest(s) select. Parking and Transportation provides a 50% discount for KSU departments. Disability Visitor Parking Accessible parking is available in all designated visitor parking areas for a fee. Visitors displaying the appropriate state-issued license plate or placard may park in any ADA designated parking space. Parking options for Visitors with a valid state-issued disability hang tag or license plate: Park at a KSU defined disability space on campus in a visitor lot and pay the hourly or daily parking fee. Purchase a temporary KSU permit for Long Term Visitors, Emeritus and Alumni. Emeritus Parking Emeritus Faculty are eligible for a parking permit that will allow them to access the faculty/staff parking locations on the Kennesaw and Marietta Campuses. This permit is offered free of charge. Emeritus Faculty are encouraged to visit the Talon One Service Center to register their vehicle information. In order to complete set up for this permit, you will ned to bring: A valid (not expired), government-issued photo ID Your vehicle's license plate number, make, model and color Retiree Parking Retirees of the university who are enrolled in the Retirees Association are welcome to park in the visitor parking areas on the Kennesaw and the Marietta Campuses free of charge. Retirees are to display their Association Card on their dash while parking in the visitor lots. Retirees not part of the Association are welcome to pay to park in the visitor lots. Alumni Parking Kennesaw State University encourages alumni to remain active within the KSU community. Alumni can pay for hourly or daily parking in the Visitor parking lots. Alternatively, alumni frequently on campus can purchase an Alumni parking permit, which costs $23 per month and is valid in any Visitor parking area on the Kennesaw or Marietta Campus. Please note, alumni permits are not available to students actively registered for classes at KSU. Purchasing an Alumni Permit Please visit the Talon One Service Center located at the Student Center on both campuses and bring the following: A valid (not expired), government-issued photo ID A credit card for payment Your vehicle's license plate number, make, model and color All citations and other unpaid fees due to Parking and Transportation must be paid prior to applying for and Alumni parking permit. Event Parking Parking and Transportation has the right to reserve lots for event parking on campus. Lot restrictions for an event will be posted at the entrance to the lot. Alumni permits are not valid for event parking. Event parking may be sold in advance or at the entrance on a first-come, first-served basis. Parking and Transportation has the authority to close a lot for construction, maintenance or safety issues. Lot closures will be posted at the entrance to the lot. On-campus parking is coordinated through Parking and Transportation. All visitors to campus should be instructed to park at one of the pay-per-plate visitor parking areas. Learn more about our current event parking information and policy. Visitor Parking Citations and Appeals Citation Payments Visitor citations may be paid online at parkingportal.kennesaw.edu . If a vehicle is not linked to a KSU student or employee, the registered vehicle owner is ultimately responsible for a parking citation, including lost, stolen or damaged citations, whether or not the owner was operating the vehicle at the time the citation was issued. Appeals All visitor appeals may be appealed through the Parking Portal within 7 days of citation issuance. If a citation is appealed within 7 days, any associated fines will be frozen until the appeal is adjudicated. Fines will not come due during this period of review. After 7 days, the citation may no longer be appealed. Appeal Approved : The associated citation will be voided and any associated fines will be reduced to $0. Appeal Denied : The associated citation stands, and the initial fine remains the responsibility of the registered vehicle owner. Citation Violation Types Click here to view violation description and costs . Citation Collections and Vehicle Tracing All unpaid citations are subject to collections and/or University policies. Citations for vehicles not found in the KSU Parking Database shall be traced through the appropriate state's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) or Department of Drivers Services (DDS). Owner's addresses will be obtained for collection purposes. Any corresponding fees associated with tracing vehicles will be passed along to the respective vehicle owner. Visitor Dining University Dining welcomes campus guests and we want to ensure that all of our diners have an exceptional dining experience in all of our campus eateries. Entry to The Commons or Stingers dining halls costs $10.50 per person for breakfast and $14 per person for lunch or dinner. Students who have an Access Plan, can use their entries for guests. Alternatively, they can pay $9.25 Dining Dollars for breakfast or $11.50 Dining Dollars for lunch or dinner for each guest meal. Kennesaw State students must present their Talon Card (KSU ID) at the time of the transaction. All guests will also be asked to show identification. Please note that visiting groups of more than ten people will need to fill out the Dining Group Reservation Request Form. Registered Visitor Services Departments need to obtain HR approval for non-directly affiliated personnel (not paid or not paid by Kennesaw State University) before Campus Services can grant access to various KSU services and facilities. Complete the Registered Visitor Job Aid linked under “Visitor Services.” This form includes instructions for requesting a NetID and related services for individuals and groups. Door Access After your Registered Visitor’s account is active, your sponsor (KSU Faculty/Staff) will need to email dooraccess@kennesaw.edu with your name, KSU ID number, and details about what door access you need, including a date for removal. When you receive confirmation that door access has been granted, present your Talon Card to a HotSpot and wait until the flashing and beeping stop to update your card. You will need to do this every seven days. Parking Once you have been granted Registered Visitor status, you can stop by the Talon One Service Center at the Kennesaw or Marietta Campus to obtain an assigned parking pass. By clicking the link below you are agreeing to set up either a recurring monthly payment or to pay the monthly equivalent to your tenure at KSU in full, upfront. Economy parking is not available to long-term visitors at this time. Talon Card Once your Registered Visitor’s account has been activated, contact the Talon One Service Center at (470) 578-8663 or email talonone@kennesaw.edu to set up an appointment to obtain your Talon Card. You will use your card to access doors and more on campus. Copier Services Our off-campus visitors may use guest cards that can be purchased for $2 from any of the KCash machines on both campuses. Guest cards allow visitors to print at the following locations: G109B Horace W. Sturgis Library (Kennesaw Campus) 117A Lawrence V. Through a one-day training, participants explore career readiness trends, learn about key campus resources, and discover ways to integrate career readiness into their courses and student interactions. Our goal is to build a campus-wide network of faculty champions who help students prepare for their futures and make career readiness part of the KSU experience. If you're interested in becoming a Faculty Career Champion, fill out the interest form so a member of our team can follow up with you. Faculty Career Champion Interest Form Program Details Classroom Assignments FAQ Why Become a Faculty Career Champion? As a Faculty Career Champion, you'll learn about current career readiness trends and student outcomes, and gain awareness of the career resources available to your students. You'll discover practical ways to connect academics and careers, and join a network of faculty committed to student success. Along the way, you'll earn recognition as a Career Champion. What You'll Learn Career readiness competencies National and employer hiring trends Internship and experiential learning insights Career outcomes and student success data KSU career resources and referrals Strategies for embedding career readiness into coursework Benefits Professional development opportunity Recognition as a Faculty Career Champion Access to career readiness resources and materials Connection to a cross-campus network of colleagues Regular updates from the Department of Career Planning and Development Available Tools Career readiness competencies Syllabus statements Classroom activity ideas Career resource guide Employer trends reports Referral information Hear from Current Faculty Career Champions "The workshop was a great introduction… the best part was the D2L course with assignment examples." Stay up to date on new developments, events, and the job fair cycle by connecting there. To be added reach out to Anthony Holmes . Career Exploration Career Fair Career-Related Event Elevator Pitch Career Foundations Badge Informational Interview LinkedIn Profile Mock Interview Resume Assignment Frequently Asked Questions Who can participate? Any Kennesaw State University faculty member may participate, regardless of rank or appointment type, including lecturers, assistant professors, associate professors, full professors, and adjunct faculty. How long is the training? The Faculty Career Champions training is approximately three hours in length. How often is training offered? The Faculty Career Champions training is offered at least twice each semester, with at least one session available online to provide greater flexibility and accessibility for faculty participants. What is expected after training? There are no formal requirements following completion of the program. Faculty Champions are encouraged to incorporate what they learn into their courses and interactions with students, utilize career readiness resources, and help connect students with relevant opportunities and support services when appropriate. This framework outlines clear, approachable steps you can take each year to explore your interests, gain experience, and prepare for your future. Let these milestones guide you to make informed decisions throughout your college experience – guiding your path from the nest to what’s next. Key Resources Detailed Milestones Your Four-Year Career Plan Nest to Next is a four-year roadmap that empowers students to take intentional steps each year at KSU. Whether you want a quick next step or a detailed plan, you’ve got options. Use the quick links for key career resources, or dive into the milestones for a deeper look at what to focus on each year. First Year (Freshman) Second Year (Sophomore) Third Year (Junior) Fourth Year (Senior) Key Resources by Academic Year Not sure where to start? This collection of resources connects you to the right tools at the right time. Each resource is organized by year and links you directly to what will best support your four-year career journey — helping you take confident, intentional steps from your first year through graduation. Year One Explore Focus2Career Steppingblocks OwlTrek Site Visits OwlAdvising Career Exploration Advising Prepare Handshake OwlSwap Career Guidebook KSU Tutoring Academic Success Coaching Connect OwlLife FLIGHT Program Mentoring Program Follow Our Instagram Year Two Explore Career Advising Study Abroad Research Opportunities Occupational Outlook Handbook Prepare LinkedIn Profile Template BigInterview Informational Interview Questions Resume Examples Connect Career & Internship Fairs GivePulse Student Groups & On-Campus Engagement Year Three Explore What Can I Do With This Major? Writing Center DoubleOwl Program Prepare Creating an Elevator Pitch Experiential Learning - Co-ops & Internships Career Development Workshops Connect Career & Internship Fairs Handshake Events OwlLife - Student Groups for Professional Development Year Four Explore Career Advising Graduate School Interest Community & Professional Education Prepare Writing Center ePortfolio Interview Tips Standard Interview Questions Salary Negotiation Connect Career Fairs Handshake Events Engage Alumni Stay Informed on Linkedin Share Your Next Steps Detailed Milestones Year One Goal: Build a foundation for your future by forming meaningful connections and engaging in self-discovery to find the major that aligns with your goals and strengths. Explore Begin with self-assessment: Identify your strengths, interests, and values using tools like the Focus2 career assessment . Utilize our additional Key Resources to learn more about potential majors and career paths. Receive your custom personality report: SteppingBlocks is a unique resource that provides a custom personality report and data on your major and career matches. Meet with a Career Consultant: Attend a career exploration appointment for personalized guidance to clarify your goals, review your self-assessment results, and explore majors. Explore beyond the Classroom: Go on an Owl Trek Site Visit or participate in field experiences to see careers and workplaces in action. Map your path: If you are undeclared, meet with OwlAdvising to ensure you are registered for the right courses. Prepare Establish your online presence: Create a Handshake account, and use this to explore companies, jobs, and organizations in your fields of interest. Review all of your social media profiles to ensure your online presence reflects your professional goals. Craft a Resume and Cover Letter: Begin developing a resume/ cover letter and use the Career Guidebook to guide you through the writing process. Build your professional wardrobe: Start assembling versatile, career-ready attire to prepare for interviews, networking events, and career fairs. OwlSwap provides free professional clothing to KSU students. Focus on academic success: Your GPA may impact acceptance into academic programs at KSU, internships, and job eligibility—develop strong study habits and utilize campus-resources focused on helping you succeed: Academic Success Coaching and KSU tutoring . Connect Get involved: Attend programs, workshops, and events through OwlLife . This is a great way to explore your interests and make connections! Engage with your KSU Community: Connect with your class-year community and explore events and opportunities through the FLIGHT program . Begin Networking: Seek out conversations with professors and potential mentors to discuss your major and career interests. Seek advice and build relationships through programs like the KSU Odyssey Peer Mentoring Program open to all first year and transfer students. Stay informed: Follow our Instagram and LinkedIn to keep up with career events and announcements! Year Two Goal: Narrow your career interests, choose or confirm a major, and begin building skills and experiences aligned with your goals. Explore Reflect on your Freshman Year: Did you enjoy your courses? Did you struggle in class? Have your interests shifted? Are you thinking of changing your major? Meet with a Career Consultant to ensure that you feel confident in your choice of major and career direction. Gain new experiences: Consider participating in a study abroad program or research opportunity to expand your knowledge, perspective, and make connections. Research Careers: Use the Occupational Outlook Handbook to learn about careers, job outlook, salary expectations, and the education needed to reach your goals. Prepare Build your professional profile: Create a LinkedIn account utilizing our LinkedIn Profile Template. Begin connecting with individuals in areas of interest, interact with posts, and browse job opportunities. Practice your interview skills: Conduct mock interviews with a mentor and/or career advisor to build your confidence and improve your communication skills. Use the BigInterview platform to practice your interview skills through industry specific example questions. Conduct informational interviews: Gain firsthand insight into careers by talking with professionals in industries of interest. Use this collection of questions as a guide: Informational Interview Questions. Update and refine your resume and cover letter: Tailor your documents to reflect new skills, experiences, and career interests. Use our database of Resume examples to create the right document for your major, and seek feedback in a resume review appointment. Connect Attend a Career and Internship Fair: Begin making connections with employers through networking events. View our current fair schedule and uncover the range of opportunities available in your areas of interest: Career and Internship Fairs. Volunteer: Utilize GivePulse to view volunteer and service opportunities that can expand your network and help you to gain real-world experience that looks great on your resume! Stay involved on campus: Continue participating in programs, clubs, and events that connect you with peers and professionals: KSU student groups. Year Three Goal: Gain hands-on experience, strengthen professional skills, and prepare for internships, graduate school, or full-time work. Explore Refine your Career Direction: Use What Can I Do With This Major? to discover career focus areas and the many opportunities available within your major. Identify at least 3 specific roles of interest and reflect on how those roles align with your skills, interests, and long-term goals. Prepare for graduate or professional school: If you are planning to attend graduate school, explore which entrance exams you will need to prepare for (GRE, MCAT, LSAT, GMAT, etc.), seek recommendations from professors early, and use campus resources such as the KSU Writing Center to strengthen application materials. Develop a focused job search strategy: Identify preferred job boards, review job descriptions, and clarify the qualifications, skills, and experiences employers are seeking. Accelerate Your Education: Explore Double Owl Pathways to see if your major offers an accelerated path to a graduate degree. Prepare Practice telling your story: Continue to participate in mock interviews and work on developing an elevator pitch to confidently communicate your interests, experiences, and goals in professional settings. Expand Your Career Knowledge: Attend workshops throughout the year to explore careers, build professional skills, and prepare for your next opportunity. Refine your Resume and Cover Letter: Ensure application materials are kept up-to date with your most recent projects, courses, and experience. Tailor these documents to the company and roles you are applying to, you may have several versions of your resume. Gain relevant experience & seek academic credit for this work: Apply to internships, research, part-time work, volunteering, or summer experiences that align with your career interests and major. Meet with an Experiential Education Advisor to learn more about the process of getting academic credit before you start your new role. Connect Engage with employers: Participate in career fairs on campus and in the community, attend employer information sessions, research organizations, and attend college-specific career events (Diamond Day, Coles Career Fairs). Use Handshake strategically: Log in regularly to explore internships, part-time roles, and events with companies of interests. RSVP for Career Planning and Development Events (Employer panels, workshops, and fairs) through Handshake. Turn involvement into experience: Use OwlLife to step into leadership roles, organize events, and gain experiences you can highlight in interviews and on your résumé. Year Four Goal: Turn your college experiences into a clear next step by securing a job, internship, or graduate school plan after graduation. Explore Finalize your post-graduation direction: Confirm whether you are pursuing employment, graduate/professional school, or another pathway—and map out next steps. Meet with a Career Consultant if you need assistance exploring job opportunities and how to best prepare yourself to submit applications. Research employers and programs intentionally: Review company websites, graduate programs , and industry trends to ensure your applications align with your interests, values, and long-term goals before you apply! Expand your qualifications: Explore certificates in areas like business, technology, healthcare, project management, and more to strengthen your résumé and support your career goals: Community and Professional Education. Prepare Use a structured plan and prepare references: Create a spreadsheet to track each position for which you applied, remember interview schedules, and coordinate follow-up communications. This will keep you organized as you apply. Confirm 3–5 professional and/or academic references, provide them with your résumé, and maintain communication throughout the process. Complete graduate school applications (if applicable): Take required entrance exams, submit applications on time, request transcripts, and have essays reviewed by the Writing Center. Consider building an ePortfolio: Create a professional portfolio that showcases your projects, experiences, and accomplishments: ePortfolio Resources. Strengthen and practice interview skills: Review practical interview tips and review examples of frequently asked interview questions to prepare thoughtful responses: Interview Tips & Standard Interview Questions . Negotiate with confidence: Learn strategies for researching salaries, evaluating job offers, and professionally discussing compensation and benefits: Salary Negotiation Guide . Connect Engage directly with employers & alumni: Make connections through career fairs , Handshake events , and alumni pages . Stay connected after graduation: Follow Career Planning and Development on LinkedIn to stay informed about career events, alumni resources, networking opportunities, and professional development available to KSU graduates. Finish strong and celebrate: Stay involved in campus organizations, share your next steps , earn your degree, and confidently transition into your next chapter. You did it! Whether you're hiring for open roles or building brand awareness, our team is here to support your recruiting goals. All recruiting activities begin in Handshake, where you can manage job postings and event requests. Some options may only appear after you've connected with our team—reach out if you don’t see what you’re looking for. Recruiting Periods: Spring : Late January – End of April Summer : Mid May – Late July Fall : Late August – Mid November Handshake Employer Resource Page Recruitment Tables Information Sessions On-Campus Interviews Other Recruiting Options Key Guidelines for On-Campus Recruiting These guidelines apply to all recruiting activities facilitated by the Department of Career Planning & Development: Active Job Posting Required Employers must have a current job or internship posting in Handshake before submitting a recruiting request. Equal Opportunity Employers Only KSU facilities may only be used by employers who comply with Equal Opportunity Employment standards. Advance Notice Required Submit requests at least 4 weeks in advance to allow time for space reservation and event promotion. Scheduling Restrictions Recruiting activities cannot be scheduled during: The first two weeks of the semester Student holidays or university closings The final two weeks of the semester Please review our Important Dates before submitting a request. Compensation Transparency If a position includes commission-only pay, base plus commission, or start-up costs to the employee, signage must clearly disclose this information during the event. Professional Conduct Students participating in interviews are expected to wear professional attire. Employers must limit promotion to recruiting opportunities only—product or service solicitation is not permitted. Rescheduling If you need to change your event date, a new request must be submitted with at least 4 weeks’ notice. Recruitment Tables Recruitment Tables are designed for employers actively hiring KSU students for current internship or full-time opportunities. These structured tabling days provide a targeted way to connect with candidates who are ready to apply. Recruitment Tables are offered on select days based on hiring focus: Tuesdays: Internship Recruitment Thursdays: Career (Full-Time) Recruitment Details: $75 per table Intended for employers with active, immediate hiring needs Focused on connecting with students for specific open roles If your goal is to build brand awareness or engage more broadly with students, we encourage you to host a free Information Session instead. Reruitment Table Options To find and register for a recruitment table, go to Fairs and search "not a career fair". Locations: Kennesaw Campus - Lobby of ALC, Burruss, Social Sciences, & Prillaman (Prillaman is Thursday only) Marietta Campus - Lobby of Atrium, ETC, and Student Center Available Dates: (18 internship and 19 career recruitment opportunities each month) Tuesday Dates (Internship Recruitment) Thursday Dates (Full-Time Recruitment) September 8 September 10 Septmber 15 Septmber 17 September 22 September 24 October 13 October 8 October 20 October 22 October 27 October 29 November 3 November 5 November 10 November 12 Campus Information Sessions & Presentations These one-hour sessions allow employers to share hiring processes and opportunities with students in a more formal setting. Sessions are typically held on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, or Thursdays between 12–2 PM or 4–6 PM. Space is limited and offered at no cost. Interviewing KSU Candidates Employers can conduct interviews with students and alumni through several scheduling formats: At Your Location / Virtual: Coordinate interviews directly with candidates. Preselect Schedule: Review applications and select candidates; interviews are scheduled through Handshake. Open Schedule: Qualified candidates can select interview slots immediately after applying. Build Your Own / Room Only: Interview candidates identified through prior recruiting; employers manage scheduling.
