We're glad you've decided to apply to live with us on campus. To begin your Housing Application, you must set up Microsoft Authenticator multi-factor authentication . Housing Application Process The First-Year Housing Application is comprised of three steps. The first step, the Housing Application, and the third step, Room Selection, are required for all first-year residents who want to live on campus. The second step, Roommate Selection, is optional. We recommend saving the dates below in your calendar so you're prepared to complete each step of the application as soon as it opens. Please note, your time ticket for steps two and three are dependent on the date and time you complete the initial application. Step 1: Housing Application Opens Monday, December 1, 2025 at 10:00 AM Step 2: Roommate Selection Begins Monday, March 23, 2026 Step 3: Room Selection Begins Monday, April 20, 2026 Step 1: Housing Application The first step of the Housing Application for First-Year students opens on Monday, December 1, 2025, at 10:00 AM EST. Please note that you must be accepted to the University before you can apply to live on campus. To complete this step, fill out all the required fields in the application and submit. While the $200 nonrefundable Application Initiation Fee is not needed to finish the application, it must be paid to proceed to Step 2 and 3. Students are encouraged to apply for housing as soon as possible to increase their likelihood of receiving housing. Students must be fully admitted to Kennesaw State University before they can apply for on-campus housing. Please contact the Talon One Service Center at 470-578-8663 (T-ONE) or ksuhousing@kennesaw.edu for specific information. Click to View the Step 1 Guide Housing Application Frequently Asked Questions Renter's Insurance Is Renter's Insurance required to live on campus? How much does it cost and how do I pay for it? Renter’s insurance is optional but highly encouraged; this will protect you from paying out-of-pocket costs if there is damage to your personal property or Housing and Residence Life’s property while living on campus. Housing and Residence Life has a partnership with GradGuard to provide renter’s insurance to on-campus residents for $139 per year. In Step 1 of the Housing Application, students can indicate interest in this service. GradGuard will communicate directly with students when it is time to enroll. Payment is made directly to GradGuard; students are unable to pay using financial aid. Watch our Keys to On-Campus Living: First-Year Housing Application video for all the details you need to know to complete Step 1! Step 2: Roommate Selection On Monday, March 16, 2026, students can see their time tickets for the second step of the application process, Roommate Selection. This is an optional step when students can select one preferred roommate after their time ticket opens. Time tickets are based on when students complete Step 1 of the application. The Roommate Selection process opens on Monday, March 23, 2026, and closes on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 5:00 PM EST.​ Click to View the Step 2 Guide View the Link Guide Roommate Selection Frequently Asked Questions Time Tickets Where can I find my time ticket for Roommate Selection? You can find your time ticket for Roommate Selection in the Housing Portal starting Monday, March 16, 2026. Once logged in, you will see a notification box that shows you your time ticket. You can also select the "2026-27 Application" tab in the gold menu, and you will see a green box with your time ticket. How are the time tickets assigned for Roommate Selection and Room Selection? Time tickets are assigned based on the completion date of your Housing Application (Step 1). Please ensure you have paid the $200 nonrefundable Application Initiation Fee or you will not be able to access these steps. When does Roommate Selection close? The Roommate Selection process closes on Friday, April 10, 2026 at 5:00 PM. What happens if I do not pick a roommate by April 10 at 5:00 PM? If you do not select a roommate by April 10 at 5:00 PM, you will move forward with the room selection process without a preferred roommate. Roommate Selection and Roommate Pairs Do I have to select a roommate? No, this step is optional. What if I don't know who I want to room with? If you do not know who you want to room with, you can see a pool of “Recommended Roommate Matches” based on your answers to the questions asked when you created your profile. Can First-Year students live with Upper Class students? No, students must live with other students of their same classification and gender. Can students in Honors Housing room with students not living in Honors Housing? No, students participating in Honors Housing can only room with other students who are in Honors Housing and are of the same classification and gender. How do I create a Roommate Pair? To create a Roommate Pair, one person in the pair must begin this step by selecting "create the group,” giving the group a name and setting a password. The person that creates the Roommate Pair is the Roommate Pair Leader. Once the pair is created, the Roommate Pair Leader can invite potential roommates to join the pair. If you have been invited to a Roommate Pair, you can accept or decline the invitation within seven (7) days of receiving it. How many people can I have in my Roommate Pair? You can have a maximum of two people in a pair, including you and one other person. If I have more than two people that I want to live with (3-4 people), how does the process work? Roommate Pairs are a maximum of two people. If you want to live with more than one other person, you and the other Roommate Pair or people you wish to live with will need to communicate early and often with one another. Before Room Selection opens, designate the person with the earliest time ticket as the Roommate Pair Leader in the Housing Portal . Once Room Selection opens, the two leaders will need to tell each other what unit and beds you are picking. We recommend that you enter the Housing Portal at the same time, if possible. Please note, we cannot guarantee that there will be units available with 3-4 open beds as Room Selection is based upon availability when the time ticket opens for the Roommate Pair Leader. Roommate Pair Leaders What is the responsibility of the Roommate Pair Leader? The Roommate Pair Leader is responsible for placing themselves and their roommate in their unit and bed when Room Selection opens. Communicating With Roommates How can I communicate with potential roommates? You can communicate with potential roommates via the messaging feature on the Housing Portal or by reaching out to them directly if they chose to share their cell phone number, email address or social media handles. If you do not see contact information listed in the portal, we cannot share it with you due to privacy, and you will need to message them through the Housing Portal. Step 3: Room Selection Time tickets for the final step of the Housing Application, Room Selection, release on Monday, April 13, 2026. Room Selection begins on Monday, April 20, 2026 for First-Year students. During this step, students will select a room once their time ticket opens. Time tickets are based on when students completed Step 1 of the application . To complete this step, you must pay the nonrefundable $75 Room Booking Fee and sign the License Agreement. Click to View the Step 3 Guide Anti-Bullying Policy Housing and Residence Life will not tolerate bullying or cyber bullying, harassment or threatening behaviors from students during the Room Selection process. If you experience any of these behaviors during or after Room Selection from students who are pressuring you to cancel your room assignment, please complete this form , so Housing and Residence Life can get involved. Harassing and/or bullying another student is a violation of the KSU Code of Conduct, which all accepted KSU students are responsible for upholding upon admission into the University. Students who are found responsible for inappropriate conduct during the Room Selection process may be moved to another room assignment, could possibly lose their opportunity to live on campus, and/or could face conduct charges with the Department of Student Conduct and Academic Integrity . Important Documents License Agreement Housing Fees Cancellation Fee Schedule Room Selection Frequently Asked Questions Time Tickets Where can I find my Room Selection time ticket? You can find your Room Selection time ticket in the Housing Portal starting Monday, April 20, 2026. Once logged in, you will see a notification box that shows you your time ticket. You can also select the "2026-27 Application" tab in the gold menu, and you will see a green box with your time ticket. When do time tickets open for First-Year students? Time tickets for First-Year students begin on April 13, and span into the month of May. Time tickets open in 20-minute intervals during business hours Monday through Friday. Time tickets are determined based on when students signed their License Agreement during the first step of the Housing Application. Each student has been assigned a specific time when they may begin Room Selection. As a reminder, First-Year and Upper Class students are not able to live in the same communities and will only be able to see the available units for their classification whenever their time ticket begins. My Room Selection time ticket doesn't open until later. What should I do in the meantime to set my Roommate Pair up for success? Before Room Selection, we recommend that you visit our website and carefully explore each community. Review the virtual tours, community and room amenities, and pricing of each option. Communicate with your preferred roommate (if applicable) and make a list of your top three community choices before Room Selection begins, so you know what to look for in the Housing Portal . Also, make sure the group member with the earliest time ticket is selected as your Roommate Pair Leader. This information is located in two places on the Housing Portal. The first place is on the main "Term Selector” page. Click on “Roommate & Room Selection,” and you will see a summary of your pair. It is also listed on the “Roommate Pair” page. Roommate Pairs Am I guaranteed a room if I have a roommate? Unfortunately, we cannot guarantee that there will be a room available when your time ticket for Room Selection begins. We encourage each Roommate Pair Leader to log in to the Housing Portal when their time ticket opens to pick rooms from what we have available at that time. Remember if you are in a Roommate Pair, only your Roommate Pair Leader is able to select rooms. How do I know who my Roommate Pair Leader is? This information is located in two places on the Housing Portal . The first place is on the main "Term Selector" page. Click on "Roommate & Room Selection," and you will see a summary of your group there. It is also listed on the "Roommate Pairs" page. The Roommate Pair Leader may pass their leader role to the other roommate in the "Pair Management" page any time before their Room Selection time ticket begins. How can I change the Roommate Pair Leader? Log in to the Housing Portal . Click on "Roommate & Room Selection" in the gold menu bar. Click "Continue" on the Term Selector page. Once inside the process, look for the "Roommate Pair Management" page. This page will be available before and after Room Selection opens. Once on the Roommate Pair Management page, the Roommate Pair Leader can see the Room Selection timeslots for all group members. If a pair member has an earlier time ticket, they can make that person the Roommate Pair Leader by clicking the "Make Leader" button on this page. Once this button is clicked, the Roommate Pair Leader responsibilities will be passed to the other member. The new Roommate Pair Leader is responsible for going into the Housing Portal when their time ticket opens to place both roommates into rooms. If I'm not the Roommate Pair Leader, can I select a bed? No, only Roommate Pair Leaders can select beds for the group. This is why it is very important to communicate with your Roommate Pair Leader about your plans and preferred living locations. My Roommate Pair Leader Forgot to place me in a bed. What should we do? The Roommate Pair Leader cannot move forward with Room Selection without placing both people in a room. How will I know what other students select beds in my unit if they were not part of my Roommate Pair? Once you select a room and pay the Room Booking Fee, you will be able to see the other students who selected that unit before you in the Room Selection Summary page on the Housing Portal . You will not receive a notification when other students select beds within your unit after you, but you may log in to the Housing Portal at any time to check. We encourage you to use each student's information provided on the Room Selection summary page to contact your roommates and coordinate who is bringing what shared items before Move-In Day. Selecting a Room Without a Roommate Pair I was not able to pick a roommate before Roommate Selection ended. Am I still able to select a preferred roommate? Unfortunately, you cannot create a Roommate Pair after Roommate Selection ends, but you can coordinate with other students on your own if you wish to live with someone you know. When your time tickets for Room Selection open, you can attempt to find rooms in the same unit or on the same hallway, depending on what is available. We cannot guarantee this will happen, but with coordination, it is possible. What should I do if I didn't match up with a preferred roommate during Roommate Selection? Roommate Selection is not a mandatory step. If you did not match up with someone, you will select a bed for yourself during Room Selection, and you will live with the other students who also select beds within your unit. Room Selection for Special Interest Housing How does Room Selection work for students who are participating in an Honors Housing? The Room Selection process is the same. The only difference is that Honors Housing students will only be able to select rooms from those reserved for Honors Housing. For more information about Honors Housing and to see which communities it can be found, please visit our Special Interest Housing webpage . What should I do if I am on the Honors Housing waitlist? If you are on a waitlist for Honors Housing and have not yet received an offer, you have two choices. Option 1: You may wait for an Honors Housing offer, which we cannot guarantee you will receive, and forgo your time ticket to begin Room Selection. Option 2: You may begin Room Selection according to your time ticket, which will automatically remove you from the Honors Housing waitlist. If you choose Option 1, you may potentially miss the opportunity to find a room on campus. If you choose Option 2, you will miss the opportunity to live in Honors Housing. If you have questions about Honors Housing, please email ksuhousing@kennesaw.edu . Room Selection for Other Special Interest Housing Room Selection for The Academy, Ascend and The Outfit is managed by the programs or departments overseeing these housing types. Eligibility for these accommodations is determined solely by each program's specific criteria. Visit our Special Interest Housing webpage for more information. What if I’m not accepted into Special Interest Housing? If you are not accepted, you will proceed with the general Room Selection process according to your assigned time ticket. Living With 3-4 People If I want to live with 3 or 4 people, how will Room Selection work? No more than two people can be in a Roommate Pair, including you and one other person. If you are attempting to match up with someone outside of your Roommate Pair, you will need to communicate early and often with one another. You may try to live together by communicating which units you have selected to live in so when their time ticket opens, they can attempt to select that same unit. If another student chooses the other rooms in your selected unit, it is unacceptable to ask them to cancel their room booking to accommodate your friends. Room Selection is based on a time ticket system determined by how soon a student completes the first step of the Housing Application. It is unfair to ask someone to give up their current booking to accommodate another student with a later time ticket. If I want to live with another Roommate Pair, should I wait to book a room until the other Roommate Pair Leader's time ticket opens? Since our housing options are limited and space will fill quickly, we advise you to prioritize finding a room on campus above attempting to live with others outside your Roommate Pair. We cannot guarantee that there will be units available for groups of 3 to 4 people when your time tickets open. Room Selection is based upon availability, and we have a high demand for housing but cannot accommodate everyone who wishes to live on campus. Bed and Room Availability Are the floor plans on the website exact? Our floor plans are useful guides to give you an idea about what your space will look like, but they are not exact. For example, in some units, the bedrooms may be flipped depending on the orientation of the rooms. You may view a virtual tour of each floor plan in our Housing Options section . Can roommates within the same unit switch beds? Some of our rooms in The Summit, University Village and Hornet Village have double occupancy bedrooms, which means there are two beds in one bedroom. We ask Roommate Group Leaders to assign beds (either bed A or B, or the top or bottom bed) during Room Selection to prevent disagreements on Move-In Day. What happens if I don't select a bed? If you don’t select a bed and we run out of available rooms, you will need to place yourself waitlist. You will not be guaranteed a bed if you do not select one during Room Selection. What happens if there are no rooms available? If we no longer have rooms available for your gender, classification or campus, we will open a waitlist. Students may add themselves to the waitlist; Housing and Residence Life does not place students on a waitlist automatically. There is no cost to add yourself to the waitlist. If a room becomes available, a Housing staff member will reach out to you via phone or email with an offer for the next available bed. You have 48 hours to accept the offer. Campus Assignment Can I choose a room on either campus? If you are a First-Year student, you will only be able to select rooms from the available options for your classification on your assigned campus. Your assigned campus is based on the major you declared when you applied to attend KSU. If you wish to change your major, you can do so in Owl Express. Please allow 5 to 10 business days for your major change to be processed. How do I change my room selection? If you have not paid the Room Booking Fee, you are able to change your room selection in the Housing Portal. Watch our Keys to On-Campus Living: First-Year Room Selection video to learn how.​ Room Booking Fee When do I have to pay the Room Booking Fee? Students who have a Roommate Pair Leader place them into a room and students who are not in a Roommate Pair have 48 hours after selecting or being placed into a room to pay their $75 Room Booking Fee. If you do not pay this fee within 48 hours, your reservation will be dropped, and your room will go back into the available room pool. We encourage you to pay this fee as soon as possible. Room Booking Cancellation I added a room to my cart and confirmed my booking. Can I cancel this booking to pick a different room? To cancel your existing booking in an attempt to book a different room, please email talonone@kennesaw.edu from your KSU student email account with your request. You will be asked to complete a form indicating your acceptance of the terms for canceling your existing booking. If you are part of a Roommate Pair, making this request will dissolve your Roommate Pair, and you will NOT be able to join or create another one. Please note that the room you hope to select may not be available once your booking is canceled and you are able to log back in to select a new room. Marietta Live-On Requirement Living on campus in your first year improves your likelihood of success in college and beyond. Living on campus makes it easier to meet people, helps you transition from high school to college, and can help you achieve academic success and graduate on time. Housing and Residence Life at Kennesaw State University is committed to supporting First-Year students in their academic pursuits. The Marietta Campus has a First-Year, live-on requirement for students pursuing majors based on the Marietta Campus. Kennesaw State University believes it is in the best interest of these students to live in close proximity to their peers and primary course instruction for the first year of college. For specific information on majors based in Marietta, use this resource to find your campus by your degree . If you are 21 or will be before the first day of class for the fall, reside with your parents or legal guardian, are married, have dependent children, serve in the Armed Forces, or are transferring into KSU with more than 30 credit hours, you may qualify for an exemption to the Live-On Requirement. Complete the Live-On Exemption Request form if you believe you qualify. The Upper Class Housing Application is comprised of two steps, which are both required to reserve your room on campus. We recommend saving the dates below in your calendar so you're prepared to complete each step of the application as soon as it opens. Upper Class Housing is limited, so it is important to complete the housing application as soon as possible. Step 1: Housing Application Opens Wednesday, January 14, 2026 at 10:00 AM Step 2: Room Selection Begins Monday, March 2, 2026 What Type of Upper Class Student Are You? Renewing : Students who are able to renew their current room assignment for another year Returning : Students who are returning to live on campus but are not able to renew their same room New Upper Class : Students who have never lived on campus Transfer : Students who are coming to Kennesaw State University from another institution Step 1: Housing Application The Housing Application for Upper Class students opens on January 14, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST . Please note that you must be fully accepted to the University before you can apply to live on campus. Students are encouraged to apply for housing as soon as possible to increase the likelihood that they will receive housing as Upper Class Housing is limited. Students must be admitted to Kennesaw State University before they can apply for housing. Please contact the Talon One Service Center at 470-578-8663 (T-ONE) or ksuhousing@kennesaw.edu for specific information. Current Upper Class Residents Only (Renewals): Current residents in Upper Class Housing are eligible to renew their room for the 2026-27 academic year. Renew your room starting January 12, 2026 until February 13, 2026 in the Housing Portal . If you don’t want to renew but still want to live on campus during the 2026-27 academic year, please apply for Upper Class Housing via the Housing Portal on January 14, 2026 at 10 a.m. However, since we have limited Upper Class housing, we cannot guarantee another room assignment. If you are applying for KSU Housing for the first time, please review the Step 1 Guide below. You will follow the same steps to complete the Upper Class Housing Application. Step-by-Step Guide Step 2: Room Selection Time tickets for the final step of the Housing Application, Room Selection, will be available on Monday, February 23, 2026 . Room Selection begins on Monday, March 2, 2026, for Upper Class students. During this step, students will select a room once their time ticket opens. To complete this step, you must sign the License Agreement and pay the non-refundable $75 Room Booking Fee. Step-by-Step Room Selection Guide Anti-Bullying Policy Housing and Residence Life will not tolerate bullying or cyber bullying, harassment or threatening behaviors from students during the Room Selection process. If you experience any of these behaviors during or after Room Selection from students who are pressuring you to cancel your room assignment, please complete this form , so Housing and Residence Life can get involved. Harassing and/or bullying another student is a violation of the KSU Code of Conduct, which all accepted KSU students are responsible for upholding upon admission into the University. Students who are found responsible for inappropriate conduct during the Room Selection process may be moved to another room assignment, could possibly lose their opportunity to live on campus, and/or could face conduct charges with the Department of Student Conduct and Academic Integrity . Important Documents License Agreement Housing Fees Cancellation Fee Schedule Room Selection Frequently Asked Questions Time Tickets Where can I find my Room Selection time ticket? You can find your Room Selection time ticket in the Housing Portal starting Monday, February 23, 2026. Once logged in, you will see a notification box that shows you your time ticket. You can also select the "2026-27 Application" tab in the gold menu, and you will see a green box with your time ticket. When do time tickets open for Upper Class students? Time tickets for Upper Class students begin on March 2, 2026. Time tickets open in 20-minute intervals during business hours Monday through Friday. Time tickets are determined based on when students signed their License Agreement during the first step of the Housing Application. Each student has been assigned a specific time when they may begin Room Selection. As a reminder, First-Year and Upper Class students are not able to live in the same communities and will only be able to see the available units for their classification whenever their time ticket begins. My Room Selection time ticket doesn't open until later. What should I do in the meantime to set myself up for success? Before Room Selection, we recommend that you visit our website and carefully explore each community. Review the virtual tours, community and room amenities, and pricing of each option. Communicate with your preferred roommate (if applicable) and make a list of your top three community choices before Room Selection begins, so you know what to look for in the Housing Portal . Bed and Room Availability Are the floor plans on the website exact? Our floor plans are useful guides to give you an idea about what your space will look like, but they are not exact. For example, in some units, the bedrooms may be flipped depending on the orientation of the rooms. You may view a virtual tour of each floor plan in our Housing Options section . What happens if I don't select a bed? If you don’t select a bed and we run out of available rooms, you will need to place yourself waitlist. You will not be guaranteed a bed if you do not select one during Room Selection. What happens if there are no rooms available? If we no longer have rooms available for your gender, classification or campus, we will open a waitlist. Students may add themselves to the waitlist; Housing and Residence Life does not place students on a waitlist automatically. There is no cost to add yourself to the waitlist. If a room becomes available, a Housing staff member will reach out to you via phone or email with an offer for the next available bed. You have 48 hours to accept the offer. Campus Assignment Can I choose a room on either campus? If you are an Upper Class student, you can see available Upper Class beds on either campus. Can I choose my roommates? Upper Class students are not able to choose their roommate because of the limited availability of rooms and the unlikely chance of finding a room pair after current Upper Class students renew. Room Booking Fee When do I have to pay the Room Booking Fee? Students have 48 hours after selecting or being placed into a room to pay their $75 Room Booking Fee. If you do not pay this fee within 48 hours, your reservation will be dropped, and your room will go back into the available room pool. We encourage you to pay this fee as soon as possible. Room Booking Cancellation I added a room to my cart and confirmed my booking. Can I cancel this booking to pick a different room? To cancel your existing booking in an attempt to book a different room, please email your request to talonone@kennesaw.edu from your KSU student email account. You will be asked to complete a form indicating your acceptance of the terms for cancelling your existing booking. Please note that the room you hope to select may not be available once your booking is cancelled and you are able to log back in to select a new room. Kennesaw Campus First-Year Males - Marietta Campus Adding Yourself to the Waitlist Here are the three steps you need to take if you wish to add yourself to this waitlist. If you are in a roommate pair, you will need to break the pair in order for each student to add themselves to a waitlist. Log in to the Housing Portal . After you complete the Housing Application, click on "Roommate & Room Selection First-Year students will only be able to see a waitlist based on their classification, campus and gender. Upper Class students will be able to see both the Kennesaw and Marietta Upper Class waitlists but can only add themselves to one. Please remember that we do not place students on a waitlist; you must place yourself if you wish to be added to the waitlist for your population. Select your waitlist population or the one shown and you will be placed on the waitlist automatically. Take note of what number you are. You can check your place on the waitlist any time by returning to the front page of the Housing Portal. This number will decrease as we place students from the waitlist. Be prepared to receive a call and/or an email at your KSU student email address with an on-campus housing offer. Make sure you have a voicemail box that can receive voicemails so we can get in touch with you when it is your turn to receive a room. You will have 48 hours to accept a room booking before we offer the assignment to the next person on the waitlist. Frequently Asked Questions How do I join the waitlist? After you complete the Housing Application, you will see “Roommate & Room Selection” appear in the gold menu bar of the Housing Portal. Click there to add yourself to a waitlist. First-Year Students: You will only see one waitlist based on your classification, campus and gender. Upper Class Students: You must place yourself on either the Kennesaw or Marietta Campus waitlist. You cannot add yourself to both. When will you stop adding students to the waitlist? We will place students from the waitlist throughout the summer until the end of July. At that time, we will pause placements until after Move-In, and begin placing again starting the first week of classes. We encourage you to be patient as we move through cancellations. Is there a cost to add myself to the waitlist? No, you do not have to pay any fees to add yourself to the waitlist. In the event we can offer an on-campus room to you, you will be prompted to pay a $275 application and room booking fee to reserve your room. Will I receive a refund for the $200 application initiation fee I paid during the Housing Application process? If you are a First-Year or new KSU student, you paid a $200 non-refundable application initiation fee at the start of the Housing Application. That non-refundable fee is not a deposit and does not guarantee students a room. I do not want to add myself to the waitlist. How do I cancel my Housing Application? If you are no longer interested in living on campus and do not wish to keep your place on the waitlist, please fill out the cancellation form on our website to cancel your Housing Application. If you change your mind after cancelling, you will need to reapply for housing and add yourself to the end of the waitlist. How do I break my Roommate Pair? (First-Year Students Only) If you are the Group Leader, follow these steps: Log in to the Housing Portal and click on “Roommate & Room Selection” in the gold menu bar. Click “Continue” to enter this portion of the application. Navigate to the “Roommate Pair Management” page. Click the gold “Delete Group” button to leave your group and search for rooms on your own. Please note: if you leave a group, we cannot help you re-create or re-join your group. To view your individual time ticket if you have not started Room Selection, click “2026-27 Application” tab in the gold menu. You will see a green box with your time ticket. If you are a Group Member, follow these steps: (You only need to leave a group if the Group Leader has not deleted the group.) Log in to the Housing Portal and click on “Roommate & Room Selection” in the gold menu bar. Click “Continue” to enter this portion of the application. Navigate to the “Roommate Pair Management” page. Click the gold “Leave This Pair” button to leave your group and search for rooms on your own. Please note: if you leave a group, we cannot help you re-create or re-join your group. To view your individual time ticket if you have not started Room Selection, click “2026-27 Application” tab in the gold menu. You will see a green box with your time ticket. When will you stop placing students from the waitlist? We will continue placing students from the waitlist until we have no more rooms to offer. Traditionally, this occurs the first or second week of September. Do I get to pick my bed option if I am on the waitlist? No, if you are offered a bed from the waitlist, it will be the first bed that becomes available for your gender and classification. I am on the Marietta waitlist but I want to change to the Kennesaw waitlist. How do I do that? To switch from the Marietta waitlist to the Kennesaw waitlist, you must first remove yourself from your current waitlist. In the Housing Portal, go to the Waitlist Status page and click “Delete” to leave the Marietta waitlist. You can then add yourself to the Kennesaw waitlist. Please note that you will be placed at the bottom of the new list, and this action cannot be undone. A student with an Academic Year License Agreement would move in during our August Move-In and move out after final exams in May. We encourage you to get involved and make the most of your time on campus. With new activities every week and month, there’s always something to enrich your campus experience. Take advantage of these opportunities to connect, learn and grow! Learn More About the Residential Engagement Model Residential Safety & Guest Policy BE SAFE All housing communities are protected by 24-hour video surveillance. Below are some precautions you can follow to help keep our communities safe for everyone: Be alert and take responsibility for the safety of your community. Do not allow strangers into your room/unit or community. Be sure to check that no one is following behind you (i.e. tailgating when entering buildings, propping open community doors, etc.). Always ensure your entryways are working effectively and notify RAs or CCs if you notice any failing equipment or security breaches. Report any suspicious persons or activities immediately, including those of your peers or roommates. GUEST POLICY When hosting a guest on campus, you must always accompany them. As the host, you are responsible for their behavior and may be held accountable for any misconduct. Residents may host guests of any gender expression in their room or unit with the consent of all roommates. Guests may include other KSU students, both residential and non-residential, or non-students. An overnight guest is defined as anyone who remains in the room or unit after 3:00 AM. The following is prohibited: Having guests without the consent of all assigned roommates in the apartment, suite, or room. Using another resident's bedroom or bathroom without that resident's prior consent. Hosting overnight guests (including other KSU students) in a resident's apartment, suite, or room for more than three consecutive nights or more than three nights within a seven-day period. Hosting overnight guests for more than the maximum allowable number of nights (12 nights per semester). Failing to escort guests at all times within the residential community. Providing access to a guest by lending or copying a key, Talon Card, or other access card. Hosting minors who are not enrolled KSU students unless they are accompanied at all times by both a parent or guardian and the host, or allowing minors to stay overnight without advance permission from the Executive Director of Housing and Residence Life or their designee. Hosting a gathering in an on-campus apartment, suite, or room where the total number of people present exceeds four people per bedroom (e.g., 16 people in a four-bedroom apartment, eight people in a two-bedroom apartment, or four people in a single-room apartment). Failing to comply with general occupancy guidelines established by building management and/or the fire marshal for overnight guests. General occupancy is limited to two people per bedroom (e.g., a four-bedroom apartment or suite has a maximum occupancy of eight people at any given time). Violating any additional posted guest or visitation policy or any term of a roommate agreement signed by all residents of an apartment, suite, or room. Read more about the Guest Policy in the Student Code of Conduct (page 17). SAFETY AND SECURITY Download the LiveSafe app for information on keeping yourself safe on campus at KSU. Please call the University Police at 470-578-6666 for emergency situations. Dialing 911 will cause a delay in response time as 911 will receive the call and forward it on to the University Police. In non-emergency situations, you can still contact the University Police at 470-578-6206. Housing and Residence Life has para-professional and professional staff on-call 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. If you need help, please call your Resident Assistant. RA On-Call Phone Numbers E-Scooter and Micromobility Policy E-Scooters and other micromobility devices are strictly prohibited inside all Kennesaw State University owned or operated buildings, including housing communities. The University reserves the right to temporarily immobilize any micromobility device found in violation of the Micromobility Rules and Regulations. Housing and Residence Life (HRL) will enforce the following actions if a micromobility device is discovered in a residential facility: First Violation: An HRL staff member or Resident Assistant will issue an official warning, and the incident will be formally documented. Second Violation or Further: The matter will be referred to Student Conduct and Academic Integrity and may result in a $150 fine. For more information, visit the Parking and Transportation website at the button below: Micromobility Policy Well-Being Resources If you are experiencing social anxiety, academic or financial stress, physical health concerns or any other challenges that may be affecting your mental health and well-being, we encourage you to take advantage of the these on-campus resources: Counseling & Psychological Services Counseling and Psychological Services aims to help students develop skills to manage emotions, navigate relationships and address mental wellness concerns, including psychiatric medication evaluation and treatment. Learn More Financial Assistance The Emergency Assistance Program provides emergency financial assistance to ALL degree seeking KSU students to help overcome unforeseen hardships that may hinder their successful academic progress. Learn More Academic Resources Our Undergraduate Academic Advisors are here to assist you with planning your course schedule, reviewing major requirements and offering guidance on academic success strategies. They aim to help you thrive academically during your time at KSU. Find Your Advisor CARE Services Campus Awareness, Resource & Empowerment (CARE) Services’ priority is to provide access to food, temporary housing and other supportive services for fostering students to realize a healthy, stable and dignified life academically and professionally. Learn More Student Health Services Kennesaw State University’s Student Health Services staff of board-certified physicians and advanced practice providers deliver comprehensive primary care services year-round. Learn More Office of Institutional Equity The Office of Institutional Equity (OIE) is responsible for ensuring the KSU campus community complies with all applicable laws and policies regarding Title IX and discrimination. Learn More Addiction & Recovery The Center for Addiction Recovery, Prevention & Education (CARPE) supports and encourages recovery and wellness by providing recovery-based programs, a peer recovery community and education to help those impacted by addiction. Learn More Student Disability Services Student Disability Services (SDS) is the first point of contact for students with disabilities to arrange academic and programmatic accommodations and to locate campus and community resources. Learn More SAFE Center SAFE Center specializes in working with individuals who experience domestic/dating violence, sexual assault and stalking. SAFE Center staff are highly trained in providing trauma-informed advocacy support, medical care, counseling, support groups and workshops. Available 24/7, they assist with both emergency and non-emergency matters. To receive any mail from common carriers, please use the address below. Kennesaw Campus [FULL NAME] [CAMPUS MAILBOX NUMBER] 1200 Chastain Road Suite 204 Kennesaw, GA 30144 Marietta Campus [FULL NAME] [CAMPUS MAILBOX NUMBER] 1100 South Marietta Parkway Marietta, GA 30060 To find your Campus Mailbox Number, log in to the Housing Portal and select the "Personal Info" tab in the top gold menu bar. Do not mail packages to the Student Centers, your community’s Housing Office, or your residence hall. Student mail addressed without a Campus Mailbox Number will not receive an email notifying them of a package. Students will also not receive an email for items when addressed to a nickname, a parent or items shipped in care of a second party. To learn more about Campus Postal Services, visit their website. Do not list the Student Center, Housing Offices, or your residence hall as the delivery address. Please note: Meal kit services such as HelloFresh and other subscription-based meal delivery services typically do not offer scheduled, on-demand deliveries and may not align with our designated food delivery process. For convenient, on-campus dining, residents are encouraged to utilize their Meal Plan whenever possible. Kennesaw Food Delivery Pick-up Locations (PDF) Marietta Food Delivery Pick-up Locations (PDF) Electronic Locks How to Operate Your Electronic Bedroom Lock Your electronic bedroom lock features Toggle Mode, which allows you to leave your bedroom door unlocked or locked when closed. To engage Toggle Mode and unlock your door, hold your Mobile Talon Card up to the middle of the reader at the top of the lock. When the green light flashes three times, turn the handle to open the door. Your bedroom door will remain unlocked until you disengage Toggle Mode. To disengage Toggle Mode and lock your door, hold your Mobile Talon Card up to the middle of the reader at the top of the lock. When the light flashes red twice, the door will be locked. In case Housing and Residence Life staff needs to enter your room for any reason, such as health and safety inspections or maintenance requests, the staff member will lock the door when they leave. Maintenance How-To Guide Once you submit a Maintenance Request, you will receive email updates regarding the status of your work order. Please check your KSUMail inbox regularly for updates. When maintenance staff arrive at your unit, they will knock and announce themselves before entering. Adhesives and Wall Hangings Residents are responsible for protecting university-provided walls, doors, floors, and furniture from damage. Please follow these guidelines when decorating your room: Prohibited Adhesive LED light strips are strictly prohibited in all campus residence halls, regardless of the surface to which they are applied. Wallpaper, wallpaper borders, and contact paper may not be used on walls, doors, or bathroom surfaces. Mountable curtain rods are not permitted. Only tension rods may be used to hang curtains. Adhesives of any kind may not be applied to University-provided furniture. Nails, screws, and staples may not be used on walls, doors, or furniture. Gummy or gel stickers, regular stickers, and other small adhesive items are not permitted, as they may cause paint damage or discoloration. Permitted Straight pins and thumbtacks may be used on drywall surfaces only. Improper use may still result in damage charges. Drywall-safe products, such as 3M Command Strips and painter’s tape, are permitted. These products must be used according to the manufacturer’s instructions and removed carefully within a few weeks of application. Improper use or leaving products in place for an extended period may result in damage fees. Read more in the Residential Handbook or find the Adhesives Agreement in the Housing Portal . Mold and Mildew Mold and mildew can be prevented by following a few simple tips for keeping your unit, suite and communities clean and safe. If you see the following issues in your room, please immediately submit a work order via the Housing Portal. If you feel a draft near the exterior door or window frames where outside air is coming inside If you see light peeking through your exterior doorframe on the side when it's closed If you see damp or wet spots or discoloration on your walls, ceilings or floors If you believe you have mold in your residence hall room that cannot be treated by household cleaners Maintenance Emergencies Maintenance emergencies include flooding, fire, AC outage in extreme temperatures and safety hazards. Resident Assistants (RAs) develop leadership skills while creating a safe, fun and vibrant community for their residents. The RA role is a gateway to campus engagement and meaningful connections with other students. An RA’s primary responsibility is cultivating one-on-one relationships with 15–70 residents, enriching their campus living experience with valuable insights. Our RAs also encourage campus involvement by crafting and supporting hall programs, major events and university initiatives. RAs contribute to resident safety and a secure campus by promptly reporting issues and managing minor incidents. Candidate Requirements Full-Time Enrollment: RAs must be registered as full-time KSU students with a course load of at least 12 credit hours (undergraduate) for Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 and must have completed at least one semester of enrollment at KSU by the start date. GPA: Must maintain a 2.0 KSU cumulative and term GPA at the time of appointment and throughout the term of employment. Summer session GPAs are reviewed with Fall GPAs. Student Conduct: Must be in good conduct standing at the time of appointment and throughout the term of employment. For more information, view the 2027-28 RA Agreement. Criminal Background Screening: RAs will be subject to a criminal background screening conducted by KSU’s Human Resources, which they must complete successfully. Housing Commitment: RAs are required to sign a housing contract and pay the housing activity fee to reside on campus, ensuring their availability throughout the academic year and breaks for RA responsibilities. Open Halls: All applicants must attend at least one (1) Open Hall to be eligible for the position. Open Hall Sessions Open Hall sessions are your opportunity to learn more about the RA role, the application process, and what to expect throughout recruitment. RAs and HRL staff will be available to answer your questions and share what it’s really like to be an RA. Come learn more, ask questions, and see if becoming an RA is right for you! Attending an Open Hall is required for all RA applicants. You must tap in within the first 15 minutes of the session to receive attendance credit. If you arrive more than 15 minutes after the session begins, you will be asked to attend a different Open Hall session to receive credit. Kennesaw Campus Tuesday, September 29 | 6:15 PM | University Village Center (UV 6000) Tuesday, September 29 | 7:30 PM | University Village Center (UV 6000) Friday, October 2 | 3:00 PM | KP Cave (UV 6000) Friday, October 16 | 10:30 AM | ALC 1100 Friday, October 23 | 10:30 AM | ALC 1100 Marietta Campus Tuesday, September 29 | 8:30 PM | Q202 Tuesday, October 6 | 8:30 PM | J1122 Friday, October 16 | 1:00 PM | Shore Innovation Center 1115 Friday, October 23 | 1:00 PM | Shore Innovation Center 1115 How to Apply Step 1: Log in to the Employment Portal. Step 2: Use the STUDENT SSO LOGIN at the bottom of the page (DUO). Step 3: Select "RA Application" in the gold menu bar. Step 4: Begin your RA Application by selecting "Apply." Position Description Resident Assistants are student leaders within the Department of Housing and Residence Life (HRL), leaving a legacy by building personal connections with residents and enhancing their campus experience.taking center stage in building personal connections with residents and enhancing their campus experience. RAs also support HRL and campus initiatives and events for residents, host individual programs, serve as the first level of Housing’s On-Call (Emergency Response) structure and complete administrative tasks throughout the year to support their community. A great RA is a problem solver, campus resource, roommate mediator and one of your first friends on your floor. Please review the 2027-2028 RA Agreement for a full look into what the Resident Assistant Position entails. 2026-2027 RA Agreement I applied to be an RA because I enjoy helping others and giving them the resources they need to be successful. This job also helps me strengthen my skills in leadership and management. My favorite part about being an RA is talking with my residents, learning new things about them and knowing I am being a good resource for them Brianna Senior I applied to be a Resident Assistant because of the influence my junior year RA, Brandon, had on me. My favorite part about being an RA is the opportunity I have to be a mentor and coach in a similar fashion. Sean Junior I applied to be an RA because as a resident my RAs are what made living on campus feel like home. My favorite part of being an RA is being able to create events that residents can come to and meet new people. I enjoy seeing them meet other residents and find their "clique" because that's what I wanted when I was a resident. Josh Sophomore Questions? The answers to many of your questions about the RA position can be found on this website or during our Open Hall series. If you have any additional questions, please email RASelection@kennesaw.edu. I missed one of the requirements before the application deadline. Can I make it up? No, there are no make-up opportunities. We have a strict deadline, and incomplete applications won’t be considered. When are grade, conduct and Title IX checks done for the RA position? The HRL team will review grades, conduct, and Title IX compliance at the end of the Fall and Spring semesters. If you don’t meet the requirements, you’ll be removed from the selection process. What is the RA interview format? The 2026-27 RA Selection process involves a video format application and one (1) in-person interview conducted by HRL professional staff and current RAs. Detailed information will be sent to applicants throughout the interview process. Can I pick my room when I am hired? No, the HRL team will select your community and room during the recruitment process. Rooms are assigned based on candidate interview and community needs. If an accommodation is required, please submit the necessary paperwork through the Office of Student Disability Services and add that information to your application. Additional support can be provided upon hire. Who can I ask for more information about the RA role? HRL will be hosting Open Halls within each community for candidates to ask questions to professional staff and current RAs. If you want to learn more about the role, look for our RA Street Team around campus or connect with a current RA. For specific application questions, please email RASelection@kennesaw.edu . What is REM? The Residential Engagement Model (REM) serves as the cornerstone for all engagement efforts targeting residential students at KSU. Our approach to engagement is comprehensive, involving students, student leaders and professional staff in fostering a more interconnected housing community. Self-Discovery Self-Discovery indicates the ability for residents to discuss their personal values, identities and goals using campus resources and opportunities provided by Housing and Residence Life staff. Life Skills Life Skills are essential for managing one’s personal matters related to conflict resolution, personal well-being and independent living. Residents will learn to think critically, practice necessary skills for adult life and understand how their choices affect themselves and their community. Community Awareness Community Awareness is the ability for residents to build meaningful relationships, positively contribute to their communities and develop an awareness of social, cultural and interpersonal differences in order to promote positive community interactions. We positively impact our students through engagement! How We Do It Programming (REM Traditions) Dedicated to building on campus traditions, REM Traditions are large-scale events intended to guide our residential population into their next steps of adulthood. Tip: Reach out to your RA for all events in your community! OwlChats We believe in connecting with you and this is how we connect! Share with your RA to find resources and support for managing your living experience. Residential Care Team (RCT) The Residential Care Team serves as a specialized layer of support for residential students who need prolonged outreach to manage challenging situations. The RCT works in connection with the Behavioral Response Team to ensure that our residential students thrive during their time living at KSU. HOOTCREW What is the HOOTCREW? The HOOTCREW is a dedicated group of students currently residing with Housing and Residence Life who are dedicated to planning, hosting and promoting our designated REM Traditions! Purchase an Apple TV, Roku, or Amazon Fire Stick to make streaming digital content as easy as possible. We recommend using devices that come with a remote control included since the new WiFi network does not allow wireless devices to operate in sync. Leave ethernet cords and routers at home since you will not need them. Leave coax cable cords at home since you will also not need them. Based on feedback received from residential students, cable was an amenity not regularly used since students choose to use their own streaming accounts (YouTube, Netflix, Hulu, etc.). As such, cable is no longer provided as an amenity. Always connect to My Resnet-5G network for faster, uninterrupted wireless connectivity. Update your laptop driver to ensure optimal performance. Wireless printers cause wireless interference. It is recommended that wireless printers be added to your additional device list or connected directly via a USB cable. Don’t forget that you can use the on-campus printers around campus! All residential students have access to the residential WiFi network, MyResNet. This network allows students to use up to ten (10) devices at one time without seeing a decrease in internet speeds. How to Connect to MyResNet Open your device settings and select “Wi-Fi.” Choose the “MyResNet-Start-Here” network to connect. This will take you directly to the kennesaw.hed.boldyn.com portal. Create a new account by entering an email address (KSU email preferred) and creating a unique password. Finish setting up your account and you’re connected! Housing accommodations are done through partnerships with different programs in coordination with the Housing team. If students are interested in living in SIH, they need to reach out to the departments and apply via their specific process. Honors This community requires acceptance to the Honors College and the Honors Housing (via demonstrating interest in the Housing Application) in order to reside in the community. Honors Application or Honors Experience Questions: honors@kennesaw.edu Housing Questions: ksuhousing@kennesaw.edu When you decide to live in the Honors community at Kennesaw State, you are choosing to live in a community of dedicated scholars, just like yourself. The Honors community is a collaborative effort between the Honors College and the Department of Housing and Residence Life. By residing in this living-learning environment, students are able to live with others who thrive on an academically rigorous curriculum. While living together, residents are able to share similar experiences and rely on each other for academic and personal support. In the Honors community, our residence halls are truly an extension of the classroom with a dedicated space to study and interact in the building. University Village Suites Hornet Village Academy for Inclusive Learning The Academy is a 2-year college experience allowing students with different intellectual or developmental abilities, who do not meet the University requirements for admission, to learn beside degree-seeking students and live in the residence halls at the same time. Visit the Academy for Inclusive Learning and Social Growth website to learn more about the program. Location: University Village Suites Contact: academyadmissions@kennesaw.edu Requires approval from the Academy for Inclusive Learning and Social Growth (WellStar College of Health and Human Services) to reside in the community. ASCEND The ASCEND SIH is the on-campus living option for KSU CARE students who were homeless and/or in foster care during their K-12 education. Participants must be Kennesaw State University students who are pursuing their first bachelor's degree. They must also meet at least one of the following criteria: Verified as an Unaccompanied Homeless Youth status based upon the McKinney-Vento Act provided by their High School Homeless Liaison Eligible for an Education and Training Voucher (EVT) Program funded by the Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS), Independent Living Program (ILP) of the Georgia Foster Care Unit or eligibility otherwise determined by CARE Case Manager or Program Coordinator Depending on room availability, and if the eligibility requirements above are met, these students live together as a community so they can build stronger, hopefully life-long, relationships with students of similar life experiences. The Outfit The Outfit is housing provided by the Center for Addiction Recovery, Prevention & Education's (CARPE) Collegiate Recovery Program. It is for KSU students that are in recovery from substance use disorders and/or addictive behaviors that want to maintain a recovery lifestyle while living on campus alongside a tight-knit community of students that are a part of CARPE. Students accepted to the Collegiate Recovery Program with at least six months of continuous recovery from any substances and addictive behavior are eligible to apply to reside in The Outfit at Kennesaw State University. The Outfit Questions: bschnei9@kennesaw.edu Housing Questions: ksuhousing@kennesaw.edu Requires approval from the Center for Addiction Recovery, Prevention & Education to reside in the community. Please contact CARPE regarding the process to live in this community. Kennesaw Campus | August 19 – 21, 2026 Marietta Campus | August 20 and 21, 2026 Pre-Arrival Checklist Move-In Process Move-In Maps Frequently Asked Questions We are very excited you have chosen to live on campus for Fall 2026! Students can see their designated Move-In arrival time ticket in the Housing Portal. When your time ticket opens, you can select a Move-In arrival day and time. Your Guide to Move-In Success Pre-Arrival Checklist To make your Move-In process as smooth as possible, please familiarize yourself with the Move-In Pre-Arrival Checklist below. Each item on this list must be completed by your Move-In Day. Select Your Move-In Day and Time Select a Move-In day and time in the Housing Portal when your time ticket opens. Time tickets will open on Monday, July 13. To select your Move-In Arrival Time, you must acknowledge the Adhesives Agreement. If interested, you can upgrade your default Residential Meal Plan in the Housing Portal. Meal Plans will become active on August 19, 2026. Obtain Your Mobile Talon Card To upload a photo for your Talon Card, follow the instructions provided here . Once approved, you will receive an email to your KSU account with details on how to add your Talon Card to your device's digital wallet. This must be completed by August 3, 2026. Create Your 6-Digit Lock Access PIN This PIN is necessary to enter your room. Please see this document for information on how to set up and change your 6-digit Lock Access PIN. We recommend students set up their PIN after they register for classes. Submit Your Immunization Record Submit your immunization record (including Meningitis) online or in person at the Enrollment Customer Service Center. Pay Your Fall 2026 Tuition and Fees Pay your Fall 2026 semester tuition and fees by the payment deadline at 4:00 PM on August 28, 2026, which includes on-campus living fees for the semester. Use our Payment Plan Guide to help you sign up for a payment plan with the Bursar's Office . The Payment Plan information is available online. Visit the Bursar’s website for more information. Purchase a Residential Parking Permit! Permit Selection for all residential students opens in the Parking Portal on Monday, August 10, at 10 a.m. All residential students must have a Fall 2026 parking permit before coming to campus for Move-In starting August 19. Visit Parking's website for a full list of permit types and costs, parking maps, and more. KSU Parking Portal KSU Parking Website Packing Tips Here are some helpful tips for when you start packing: View our Packing List so you know exactly what to bring and what not to bring on your Move-In day. Unbox your purchases and leave packing materials at home! Make the most of your bin and vehicle space by recycling cardboard boxes and Styrofoam at home before you arrive. This helps reduce the number of trips to recycling stations and dumpsters. Bin carts will be provided at check-in but consider bringing your own wagons and dollies day of. No U-Hauls or moving trucks please! Save time moving in and pre-build small accent furniture you plan to bring to campus. We do not have tools available. Click to View Packing List Move-In Day Process We can't wait to see you on campus! Move-In day is one of the most exciting days of the year. As you and your guests prepare to make your way to campus, here are a few tips to make your day as smoothe as possible. Rescheduling Your Move-In Arrival Time To reschedule your Move-In arrival time, follow these instructions: Log in to the Housing Portal Select the "Schedule My Arrival" tab in the gold menu bar. Click the blue "Continue" button. Select the "Cancel button next to your Move-In arrival time. You will receive an email confirming this cancellation. You may now select a new arrival time. Check-In Arrive at your check-in location during your selected Move-In arrival time. Use the Move-In maps to find the correct place. If you are traveling in a separate vehicle from your parent/guest, follow the "student" route to your check-in location. Your parent/guest should drive directly to your community's unloading zone by following the "parent" route. If you are traveling in one vehicle, follow the "student" route to your check-in location before going to your community's unloading zone. All students should be ready to present their Mobile Talon Card on their device during Check-In. Unloading and Moving In Once you are checked in, follow the signs from your check-in location to your community's unloading zone. Review the How to Open Your Door Flyer you received at check-in BEFORE going to your unit. Unload your vehicle(s) as quickly as possible. Moving bins are provided, but we encourage you to bring wagons and dollies to make moving easier. Kindly limit your bin use to one hour. Please move your vehicle as soon as you finish unloading to make room for other residents who are arriving. If you need assistance, find a staff member or RA in a Move-In shirt. If you have questions throughout the day, stop by one of the Information Tents located in The Summit Lobby, Outside the North Housing Office or in front of Hornet Village 100 and 200. In Your Room Once you arrive at your unit, enter your 6-digit Lock Access PIN and then present your Talon Card to your lock to enter your room. You will find a magnet in your unit with emergency contact information. Visit the Welcome webpage for important information to get you acclimated to campus living. If you forget something, don't worry! Visit The Market on the Kennesaw Campus or the KSU Bookstore on each campus for any last-minute essentials. Trash and Recycling Join KSU in our sustainability efforts to divert waste from the landfill! Recycling is available at University Village Apartments / Suites, The Summit, Hornet Village and Howell Hall. Please recycle your cardboard and plastic film (e.g., plastic grocery bags, stretchy plastic bags in appliance boxes, etc.). Please flatten all cardboard boxes and remove all personal items, trash, packaging, Styrofoam and packing peanuts. Check out your community's Move-in Map for locations. Landfill dumpsters are available for regular trash. Please tie and secure all trash bags. Check out your community's Move-In Map for locations. The Summit Unloading Due to the construction of The Summit II, Move-In for The Summit residents will look a little different this year. Please follow these steps carefully on your Move-In Day: Review The Summit Move-In Map Be sure to look over The Summit Move-In Map before arriving on campus. Check-In Process Students: Go to the Central Deck for Check-In. Parents/Supporters : If driving separately from your student, go directly to the Unloading Zone in Lot A, located in front of the Clendenin Building on Kennesaw State University Road. Unloading Zone After going through Check-In, head to The Summit Unloading Zone in Lot A, located in front of the Clendenin Building on Kennesaw State University Road. When you arrive to Lot A, you will receive a parking slip. Place the slip on your vehicle’s dashboard. Bin Check-Out Located in Lot A. Students must be present to check out a bin. Parents/supporters cannot do this alone. Loading Assistance A housing staff member or Move-In volunteer will help load your items into the bin Unloading Time Limit You will have one (1) hour to unload in the Unloading Zone. After unloading, move your vehicle(s) to the West Deck. Directional signs along the road will guide you. Frequently Asked Questions How many guests am I allowed to have with me on Move-In Day? We kindly ask that students bring no more than 2-3 people to help them move in. While we know this is an exciting event for the whole family, our hallways can get a little cramped, and we want to make sure you have a pleasant Move-In experience. How many vehicles may I bring to Move-In Day? To make the Move-In process as smooth as possible, we ask that you please bring no more than one car for the resident and one car for their guest(s)—two (2) vehicles total. Please do not bring U-Hauls or moving trucks; they will not fit in our unloading zones and are not allowed. If the student is not bringing a separate car, what map should we follow? If you are only planning to bring one car on Move-In Day, please follow the student route to ensure that you complete the check-in process. Can I move in early? Unfortunately, Housing and Residence Life cannot accommodate any Early Move-In requests unless you are in a special population, including but not limited to “The Marching Owls”. Students who are participating in these groups received Early Move-In communications. See the corresponding Early Move-In web pages for more information related to Move-In for these groups. Can I move in late? To maintain a smooth flow of our Move-In operations, we cannot allow residents to check in outside of the 30-minute window they selected for their Move-In arrival time. If you need to reschedule, you can do so through the Housing Portal up to 48 hours before your scheduled Move-In arrival time. Is the 30-minute arrival time window how long I have to move in? No, the 30-minute window is the time you need to arrive to check in. How do I contact my roommate(s)? You can reach your roommate(s) through the Housing Portal . Here is how: Log in to the Housing Portal Click on "Roommate and Room Selection" in the gold menu bar Click on "Academic Year 2026/27" and click "Continue" Navigate to the last available page titled "Housing Process Complete" On this page, you will see a summary of the roommates you are living with. Click on "Send Message" next to their name to send a secure message through the Housing Portal. Your roommate(s) may have also chosen to share their contact information, such as cell phone number and social media handles. You can also use these to reach out to them. If they have chosen not to share it through the portal, we cannot share it either. Will there be moving bins? We will have a limited number of bins available to use on Move-In Day. We recommend that you bring your own dolly or wagon. Can I change my room on Move-In Day? We do not accept Room Change Request Forms until after the first two weeks of each semester. If you need immediate assistance in your living situation, please contact your Resident Assistant or visit the Housing Office. There is a $200 room change fee if your request is approved. What is my mailing address? Kennesaw Campus Full Name Campus Mailbox Number 1200 Chastain Road - Ste. 204 Kennesaw, GA 30144 Marietta Campus Full Name Campus Mailbox Number 1100 South Marietta Parkway Marietta, GA 30060 To find your Campus Mailbox Number, log in to the Housing Portal and select the "Personal Info" tab in the top gold menu bar. Who do I call if I have additional Move-In questions? Please contact the Talon One Service Center at 470-578-8663 (T-ONE).
