We provide comfortable housing on both our Marietta and Kennesaw campuses to fit your lifestyle and location. The Marietta Campus, near I-285 and I-75, is ideal for easy access to the city. Hornet Village features double beds and shared bathrooms in a community-style setting. For those working farther north on I-75 or seeking apartment-style living, University Village on the Kennesaw Campus offers fully furnished four-bedroom, four-bath apartments with full kitchens, in-unit laundry, and optional dining services. Located just 30 minutes north of Downtown Atlanta, Kennesaw delivers premium, affordable lodging that exceeds the value of independent rentals. Key Dates First Check-In Date: May 19, 2026 Last Check-Out Date: August 7, 2026 Check-Ins and Check-Outs are only scheduled on select Saturdays from 10:00 AM - 2:00 PM and weekdays from 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM. Guests must move out no later than 12:00 PM on August 7, if applicable. Intern and Short Stay Lodging Inquiry Portal submit a contact request through our portal Advantages Affordability Experience the comfort and convenience of KSU’s fully furnished housing—an affordable alternative to traditional rentals. With easy access to major interstates, you’ll have everything you need to make the most of your summer without breaking the bank. Modern Lodging Experience modern and comfortable living at our secure campus community, with a range of fully furnished suite-style, apartment-style and traditional housing options. Location Enjoy the perfect balance of work and relaxation at KSU, a quiet retreat just 15 miles from downtown Atlanta. With easy access to I-285 and I-75, our campus offers a peaceful stay while keeping you connected to the city. Lodging Kennesaw Campus University Village $45 per night Located on the north side of the Kennesaw Campus and just a short walk across the pedestrian bridge to the main part of campus, University Village is a community of apartment-style units. Each premium apartment is equipped with a full kitchen with appliances, a washer/dryer, dishwasher and fully furnished living rooms. Floor Plan Virtual Tour Marietta Campus Hornet Village $41 per night Hornet Village is one of two suite-style communities on the Marietta Campus. Both phases of Hornet Village offer spacious, double bedroom floor plans. In this building, you are close to many of the Marietta Campus offerings such as Stingers and the multi-use field at the center of campus. Floor Plan Virtual Tour Amenities University Village Bedroom Amenities Private bathroom Keyed entry for individual bedroom Full-size bed 4-drawer dresser Built-in desk with bookshelves Closet Apartment Amenities Microwave Dishwasher Full-size refrigerator Stove with range Washer and dryer Pantry Sofa Coffee table and end table Hornet Village Bedroom Amenities Extra-long Twin-size bed Electronic keyed entry for individual bedroom 4-drawer dresser Computer desk with chair Bathroom and shower inside each suite shared with 3 people WiFi Community Amenities Elevator Access Large lounge on the first floor with couches and a TV Multipurpose rooms on each floor for small gatherings Laundry Center on first floor What should I bring for my stay? When packing for your summer internship, remember that you’ll be sharing a space with three other interns who may or may not be part of your program. The apartment is furnished but does not include personal items. Below is a list of recommended items to bring for your stay at Kennesaw. What to Bring - Suggested Items All rooms are fully furnished with dressers, desks with chairs and a Twin-size XL* or Full-size XL bed. *Bed sizes are listed under the amenities section for each community. Bedding Towels Shower curtain and hooks Toiletries (including hand soap) Toilet paper Laundry detergent Dishes and silverware Dishwasher detergent and dish soap Trash can and trash bags Prescribed medication Please review our Housing Policies for items that are not allowed in our residential spaces. What are things to do? Staying in the Kennesaw or Marietta area offers a great central location with easy access to various attractions and destinations in the surrounding areas such as the North Georgia Mountains and Chattanooga, Tennessee. For the Foodie Marietta Square Downtown Woodstock Downtown Kennesaw Atlanta Beltline Ponce City market Krog Street Market Colony Square The Battery Atlanta Westside provisions East Atlanta Village The Vortex OK Café The Varsity For the Outdoor Explorer Lake Lanier Lake Allatoona Float the Chattahoochee River Red Top Mountain Kennesaw Mountain Stone Mountain Silver Comet Trail For the Urban Explorer Downtown Atlanta Midtown Atlanta Inman Park Little Five Points World of Coca-Cola Georgia Aquarium Atlanta Botanical Gardens Atlanta National History Museum Civil Rights Museum Atlanta Atlanta Zoo High Museum of Art For the Night Owl Buckhead The Tabernacle The Masquerade The Coca-Cola Roxy - The Battery Atlanta MadLife Stage and Studios Starlight Drive-In Theater 10th and Piedmont For a Day-Trip or Weekend Excursion Dahlonega, GA Helen, GA Athens, GA Senoia, GA Chattanooga, TN Rates & Registration Rate per person/per night includes: Parking Taxes and Fees Utilities Wi-Fi Application Requirements: Headshot or photo of intern Proof of internship or employment Payment of $500 non-refundable deposit due at the signing of KSU Housing License Agreement. Emergency contact All placements are based on availability. Approved interns must sign a short-term housing contract. Housing Policies No alcohol or drugs may be consumed or brought onto the Licensed Premises. No smoking or tobacco use is permitted in any room or apartment or in KSU’s buildings. No firearms, weapons, ammunition (except as specifically allowed by applicable federal or state law), fireworks, explosives or highly flammable materials are permitted within KSU’s buildings or on KSU’s property. Except for service animals, no animals are permitted in rooms or apartments or in KSU’s buildings without prior written permission from Housing and Residence Life (HRL). No hot plates or cooking appliances are permitted in rooms or apartments. Cooking may be allowed in kitchen areas only (if applicable). No remodeling or renovating of rooms or furniture will be permitted, including, but not limited to, tampering with electrical or mechanical fixtures, placing of antennas or appliances out of windows or removing or adding furniture without permission from HRL. No alterations whatsoever of the rooms or apartments are permitted, including attaching any objects with adhesives, nails or screws without permission from HRL. No tampering with or removal of windows or window screens from any part of any building within the Licensed Premises is permitted. No tampering with the fire system or firefighting equipment is permitted. No removal of lounge or common area furniture into individual rooms or apartments without permission from HRL. No gambling or solicitation in any form is permitted. No parking in the service or fire lanes adjacent to KSU’s buildings is permitted. The Housing Policies are a subset of the KSU Codes of Conduct and applies to all clients and guests utilizing Kennesaw State University facilities. Please know that this is not an exhaustive list of policies; however, all clients and guests shall abide by the rules and regulations found in the Residential Handbook and the KSU Codes of Conduct. Dining Savor the flavor at our campus dining spots, each designed with your cravings in mind. On the Kennesaw Campus, The Commons dining hall offers nine stations to explore. On the Marietta Campus, enjoy a more intimate setting with six distinct stations, each providing a unique culinary experience. From gluten-free to vegan options, we've got your preferences covered with clear allergen labels for worry-free dining. Don’t forget to quench your thirst with our Coca-Cola Freestyle machines — they have the perfect sip for every mood. Hours of Operation Daily Menu Guest Meal Plans Enjoy your meals at our award-winning dining halls, The Commons (Kennesaw) and Stingers (Marietta), with Access Plan Entries. Each plan provides full access to all dining stations within our facilities, providing a variety of delicious options. Guest Entry Plan Rates Retail Locations Explore 17 unique dining options across both KSU campuses, from quick bites to sit-down meals. Convenient, cashless transactions are available at all locations using debit or credit cards.* *Some retail locations close during the summer. Kennesaw Campus Marietta Campus Recreation Make the most of your stay with our top-tier sports and recreation facilities on both campuses. From fitness programs to recreational sports and activities, we offer everything you need to stay active, have fun and feel your best during your time here. Purchase a Membership $10 per week or $30 per month To purchase a membership while on campus, visit the Administration Office at the Dr. Betty L. Siegel Student Recreation and Activities Center, Kennesaw Campus, during business hours. We accept debit/credit cards and Apple/Google Pay. A valid government-issued photo ID is required. Once your membership is processed, you’ll receive full access to both facilities with your guest Talon Card. The Perks Membership provides full access to services at both recreational activity centers, including: Weight and conditioning areas Four-court gymnasium for basketball, volleyball, badminton, pickleball, etc. Three (3) racquetball courts Indoor track Three (3) Fitness studios 8-lane 25 yard indoor pool Outdoor pool with whirlpool XP Power Performance room Personal Training office Outdoor Adventures Suite Bike Shop Climbing Gym Equipment Issue 8-Court tennis complex with hitting wall Two (2) sand volleyball courts Outdoor basketball court Locker/Changing rooms FAQs Details and Requirements What are the age requirements for the Intern and Short Stay Lodging program? Applicants must be 18 years old to apply. How can I prove my age, if requested? Providing a copy of your driver’s license, birth certificate or passport are acceptable ways to confirm your age. What is an acceptable proof of internship or employment? All applicants must submit proof of internship or employment. This documentation should be a letter from the applicant’s supervisor or Human Resources department and must be included with the application. Is there a pre-payment? Yes, you need to pay $500 when you accept the online contract. This amount is non-refundable but will be credited towards your total bill. When is the rent due? Full rent is due one (1) business day before you check in. The exact amount and due dates will be in your customer portal. Can I pay rent in installments? Yes, you can pay installments based on the number of nights and your expected check in date. Intern and S hort Stay Lodging Payment Schedule May check-in: $500 non-refundable deposit due at signing 50% of the remaining balance due June 1 Final payment due June 30 June check-in: $500 non-refundable deposit due at signing Final payment due June 30 July check-in: $500 non-refundable deposit due at signing Final payment due upon check-in Can I get a refund if I cancel? Except for the pre-payment, you can get a refund if you cancel at least 48 hours before check-in by emailing overnightexperiences@kennesaw.edu. Check-In and Check-Out Information When is the earliest check-in date? Tuesday, May 19, 2026, at 12:00 PM Where do I check in? You will get this information via email based on your lodging assignment. What are the Check-In hours? Staff is available from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Friday, with some flexible hours on weekends. Please coordinate your arrival time before you arrive. When is the latest Check-Out day? Friday, August 7, 2026, at 12:00 PM. You must check out by noon. Where do I check out? You will check out with an Overnight Experiences Team Member. Specific instructions will be provided in your welcome guide. Lodging Will I have a roommate? Bedrooms are single occupancy. You might share an apartment or suite with others, but not a bedroom. Room assignments are made by the Overnight Experiences Program. Can I live with people I am interning with? Yes, but both you AND your roommate MUST request each other on your applications. Only requests from roommates of the same gender will be honored. Will housekeeping clean my room and provide toilet paper? No, you must provide your own toilet paper and are responsible for the cleanliness of your unit, bathroom and bedroom. Trash receptacles are located near the residence halls. Are your facilities ADA accessible? Yes, please let the Overnight Experience Team know of any special requirements in your application. Is internet and parking available on campus? Yes, there is a designated parking area, and wireless Internet is included in your rent. More information will be in your welcome guide. What if I have further questions? If you have more questions, please call 470-585-3554 and tell the representative you have questions about the Intern Housing Program. You can also email overnightexperiences@kennesaw.edu . Campus Postal Kennesaw State University’s Campus Postal Services provides the University with convenient access to mailing services. Campus Postal Services process and distribute interoffice mail as well as all incoming and outgoing mail for the university. Additionally, United States Postal Service express mail, priority mail and tracking services are provided. Kennesaw Campus The correct address format for mail and common carriers is as follows: Full Name: UV – [Room Number] 1200 Chastain Road - Ste. 204 Kennesaw, GA 30144 You will receive an email notification when mail is received at the email address listed in your application. Mail can be retrieved at the student mail office on the second floor of the Carmichael Student Center . The office is open Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. Marietta Campus The correct address format for mail and common carriers is as follows: Full Name: HV – [Room Number] 1100 South Marietta Parkway Marietta, GA 30060 You will receive an email notification when mail is received at the email address listed in your application. Mail can be retrieved at the student mail office on the second floor of the Joe Mack Wilson Student Center . The office is open Monday through Friday, 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m. Amazon Lockers Campus guests who shop through Amazon.com can have their items conveniently shipped to our campus Amazon Hub Lockers — " Doughnut " at the Kennesaw Campus and " Dugout " at the Marietta Campus. When you check out, choose one of these convenient Amazon Hub Locker locations. When your package is ready to be picked up, you will receive an email notification from Amazon with a shipment tracking ID and a unique pick-up barcode. You can access the lockers anytime the Student Centers are open. To open the locker, scan your barcode or enter the tracking ID on the Amazon Hub Locker screen. You have three (3) days to pick up your package. If you do not pick up your package, it will be returned for a full refund. KSU Safety Kennesaw State University’s Department of Public Safety and University Police is dedicated to ensuring a safe campus environment for residents, students and guests. All exterior doors, unit doors and room doors are equipped with electronic locks to enhance security during your stay. Emergency Dispatch (to request an officer): 470-578-6666 or 770-423-6666 If the campus VoIP phone system is not working properly, dial 770-423-6666 to call and request an officer. Non-Emergency Administrative: 470-578-6206 Text Line: 770-356-3866* *Use the text line number to text message us only if you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability; or if a voice call might otherwise be dangerous or impossible. If you need a police, fire and/or EMS response to an emergency or other urgent incident and are able to make a voice call, you should always make a voice call if possible. Non-Emergency E-mail: police@kennesaw.edu To Report a Tip Anonymously (non-emergency): Call our administrative number (470-578-6206) and tell the person who answers your phone call that you would like to leave an anonymous tip. The Act requires that public records be open and available for inspection by a requesting party within a reasonable amount of time after the receipt of the request, unless the records are those exempted by law from disclosure (e.g., student educational records) . The Act also requires an initial response within three (3) business days to all Open Records Act requests received by a university official (faculty, staff or administrator). Failure to do so may result in penalties for the university official under the provisions of the law. There are some exceptions to the Open Records Act, including medical records and student academic records. Kennesaw State University has designated the General Counsel as the Open Records Officer for the University, and is the official to whom all Open Records Act requests should be made. Please send all Open Records requests to asklegal@kennesaw.edu or to: Kennesaw State University Division of Legal Affairs MD #9115, Town Point, Suite 3400 3391 Town Point Dr NW Kennesaw, GA 30144 Any Open Records requests must be forwarded immediately upon receipt to the KSU Office of Legal Affairs for initial response on behalf of the University. The Office of Legal Affairs will also be responsible for collecting documents that are responsive to the Open Records request (if any), and will provide the documents for review to the requesting party at a mutually convenient time. In order to avoid delay and to have sufficient time to respond before the 3-day deadline, Open Records requests received by University personnel must be faxed, e-mailed, or delivered in person to the Office of Legal Affairs. We empower our students to become thought leaders, lifelong learners, and informed global citizens by cultivating an inclusive environment that encourages free expression and civil discourse. Kennesaw State will achieve national prominence as a public university known for education, research, and community programs that foster inquiry and advance society. University Libraries The KSU Libraries are committed to supporting and furthering Kennesaw State University’s mission of being a student-centered, research-driven, and nationally prominent R2 university. The University Libraries carefully cultivate resources, services, and spaces that enhance teaching, learning, scholarship, and creative endeavors for our users. The KSU Libraries advance student success, lifelong learning, and research through teaching, outreach, access to and discovery of academic resources in a welcoming environment. Academic Distinction Statement (MARBL) Museums, Archives & Rare Books, and University Libraries (MARBL) is a welcoming, accessible, and inclusive unit that collaborates with academic colleges and support units to foster research and academic success for KSU students, staff, faculty, and researchers. MARBL is uniquely positioned to serve not only the KSU campus community, but also the greater metro Atlanta area and beyond through outreach, programming, instruction, and academic resources. We employ creative solutions to develop and enhance collections, facilities, services, and operational efficiencies. Welcome from the Associate Vice Provost, Dr. Catherine Lewis Welcome to the University Libraries at Kennesaw State University. If you haven't had the chance to get to know Kennesaw State University yet, now is the perfect time. Situated on two suburban campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta, northwest of metro Atlanta, KSU is a comprehensive university that is rapidly gaining recognition. With over 51,000 students enrolled in over 190 undergraduate, master's, doctoral degree, and certificate programs, we are proud to be the third largest university in Georgia. KSU is one of the most dynamic and innovative universities in the nation, and the University Libraries play a critical role in our mission. The University Libraries are committed to supporting and furthering KSU’s mission of being a student-centered, research-driven, and nationally prominent R2 university. The University Libraries carefully cultivate resources, services, and spaces that enhance teaching, learning, scholarship, and creative endeavors for our users. We recently completed a major reorganization and have welcomed new faculty and staff to this dynamic and innovative team. I believe that the best academic libraries are more than just repositories of information. They are . . . Hubs for interdisciplinary partnerships Hives of activity where students and faculty conduct and showcase research in a meaningful way Nests where students, staff, and faculty feel comfortable, supported, and confident that they will get the help they need The University Libraries’ team brings a range of expertise to their roles and values collaboration and innovation. We offer a supportive work environment, professional development opportunities, and a chance to make a real difference in the lives of our students, staff, faculty, and community. We welcome you to the University Libraries – whether in person or virtually – and invite you to take advantage of all we have to offer as you make a lasting impact on the academic community and beyond. Computing Visitors to KSU can use a guest computer in each of our libraries (2 hour limit). All other computers are for current KSU student use and require student log-in. Guests cannot access library resources from off-campus. Borrowing Privileges Residents of Georgia over the age of 18 may request a community borrower's card which provides limited borrowing privileges to the general collection. These privileges DO NOT include remote access to electronic resources OR borrowing services such as Interlibrary Loan (ILL) and GIL Express. Ask your local public library about requesting materials through their ILL service. ILL allows current KSU faculty, staff, and students to access articles not held by KSU and books not available at KSU or through GIL Express at no cost. For more information, visit our Research Guide or contact the ILL office at illoan@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6002. How to Request an Interlibrary Loan Log In: To request an interlibrary loan, please log in to the ILL system using your KSU NetID and password. Submit a Request: Once logged in, you can submit a request for the materials you need. Provide as much detail as possible to help us locate the item quickly. Log In to Your Library Location To log in and submit your interlibrary loan request, please click on the link for your home library location. This is the campus library where your physical items will be delivered: Log In to Sturgis Library (Kennesaw) Log In to Johnson Library (Marietta) Important: If you want to change your home library, please contact the ILL office at illoan@kennesaw or 470-578-6002. Accessing Delivered Items You will receive an email when your request has been delivered. Books and Other Physical Materials will be delivered to your designated home library. Please bring your TalonOne card to pick up items at the check out desk. Articles and Book Chapters will be delivered electronically to your ILLiad account. These files will be deleted after 30 days of delivery so please save or print for future use. Need Help? Exhibits on Display in the Sturgis Library Ground Floor We the People: The Documents That Made Our Nation On display: Now through September 2026 This 10-panel traveling exhibit premiered in September 2024 during Constitution Week as a companion piece to our newly restored 1843 facsimile of the Declaration of Independence. The exhibit, curated by MARB & Libraries Associate Vice Provost Catherine Lewis and Rare Books Curator JoyEllen Williams, underscores the enduring power of print in shaping our nation’s history and freedom struggles. Athenaeum Gallery, Second Floor Cobb County Commemorates the Revolution On display: June through September 2026 This America250 exhibit was installed at the end of June and was curated by KSU history major and Williams Rare Book Museum Mattord Scholar Andrew Bramlett. This exhibit looks at how Cobb County residents celebrated July 4 in the years 1876, 1926, and 1976, along with how our school celebrated the Bicentennial. Items from both the University Archives and the Williams Rare Book Museum are displayed, along with a collection of library books that focus on revolutionary era topics and people. Hear Ye! Hear Ye! American Independence in the News On display: Early September through May 2027 The former colonists who broke from Great Britain quickly learned that gaining freedom and creating a government were very different things. This exhibit, developed by MARB team members Catherine Lewis, Kate Matheny, and Mad Dworschak, examines how these debates unfolded in print – from broadsides to pamphlets to newspapers – as the founders sought to create a new nation. The panels tell the story of the creation and ratification of the U.S. Constitution and are supplemented by display cases featuring the tools of late 18th century printing and sample documents from the period. Memorializing the Adams Family On display: Early September through November 2026 The MARB Curatorial Affairs team worked with the Adams Memorial Foundation (AMF) to develop a traveling exhibit focused on the Adams family, including President John Adams, First Lady Abigail Adams, President John Quincy Adams, and First Lady Louisa Adams. That exhibit will travel across the country to increase awareness for the proposed Adams memorial in Washington, D.C. We are pleased to have our own version of the exhibit on display this fall to help us commemorate this special anniversary year. Read more in this press release from the Museums, Archives and Rare Book department. Constitution Week Events Designing for Democracy Faculty Panel Monday, Sept. 14 • 12:15-1:30 pm Willson Student Center, Marietta Campus Join us for a conversation on how architecture and design can promote inclusion, accessibility, and civic participation. Together, we'll explore how thoughtfully designed spaces can create greater opportunitiesfor everyone to connect, participate, and have a voice in our community. Panelists Michael Carroll, Architecture Keif Schleifer, Architecture SGIA Faculty Panel & Voter Registration Day Tuesday, Sept. 15 • 12:30-1:30 pm The Nest, First Floor, Sturgis Library (Kennesaw) In partnership with the School of Government and International Affairs and the Department of Student Leadership, the University Libraries are kicking off Constitution Week on the Kennesaw campus by hosting our annual SGIA faculty panel, "Recovering Political Goodwill: The Constitution and Strengthening Positive Political Norms." Panelists from the School of Government and International Affairs (SGIA) will examine how constitutional principles and design can help restore goodwill amidst current political polarization by reinforcing positive norms such as civility, mutual respect, deliberation, and compromise. The panel will utilize concepts from political science, conflict management, and related subfields to find ways to revitalize democratic discourse even as society addresses the needs of its individual members. This year's panelists include Dr. Maureen Wilson, Dr. Carter Harmon, Dr. Hayden Proborowski, and Dr. Carl Snook. A Corgi’s Take on the Constitution Wednesdays, September 16 • 1:30 – 3:00 pm Outside Sturgis Library (Kennesaw) Wednesday, September 23 • 1:30 – 3:00 pm Outside Johnson Library (Marietta) Back by popular demand, the University Libraries’ therapy Corgi, Summer, and her little brother Winston (therapy Corgi in training) will visit both campuses to give students a chance to ponder the Constitution from a dog’s perspective. There will be snacks, sticker surveys, stickers, and a chance to check your voter registration status and location. All are welcome to stop by for some sweet snuggles and interesting conversations. The Adams Family Remembered (Constitution Day) Thursday, September 17 • 1:00 – 2:00 pm The Athenaeum, First Floor, Sturgis Library (Kennesaw) Partnering with the Department of History and Philosophy , History Professor & Adams Scholar Marianne Holdzkom will deliver an insightful presentation about John and Abigail Adams and how they shaped the nation’s founding. Holdzkom will discuss her role on the curatorial team that developed the Adams Family exhibit in our Athenaeum Gallery as well as her book, Remembering John Adams, which explores Adams in scholarship, public memory, and pop culture. Revolutionary Recipes Monday, September 21 • 11:00 am – 12:00 pm The Nest, First Floor, Sturgis Library (Kennesaw) In celebration of our country’s 250th year, the Williams Rare Book Museum and the Department of History and Philosophy are partnering with Dining Services to showcase colonial recipes and cookbooks. Join a lively conversation with Dr. Tom Okie talking about colonial foodways, Dr. Catherine Lewis talking about colonial women in the kitchen, and Dr. Kate Matheny showcasing the Williams' rare colonial cookbook collection. The Commons culinary team will talk about how they brought one of these historic recipes to life for the KSU community to sample. After the program, we encourage everyone to visit The Commons to purchase a full serving of the special revolutionary recipe at the Globe Trotters station during their lunch service. Experts on DIY Publishing Series | September - November The KSU Libraries’ Scholarly Publishing and Research team invites you to attend our webinar series "Experts on DIY Publishing." We'll hear from KSU experts on the history of zines, the evolution of the book, and using zines as tools for teaching and learning. If you're interested but unable to attend, register to receive a recording. Experts on DIY Publishing: History of Zines (+ Free Speech) Zines have long been a powerful medium for sharing ideas, building communities, and subverting traditional publishing. Participants will gain insights into what zines are, how they’ve evolved over time, and how they remain a tool for free speech. When: Wednesday, September 2 at 2:00PM Register for the History of Zines webinar Experts on DIY Publishing: Remixing the Book Scrolls, codices, zines, ebooks—the book has taken many forms and is still evolving. This panel will consider the book’s physical history and form, books in digital environments, and the future of the book. When: Wednesday, September 30 at 2:00PM Register for the Remixing the Book Webinar Experts on DIY Publishing: Teaching with Zines How can zines transform the classroom into a space for hands-on, personalized learning? This webinar will explore the potential of zines as a teaching tool and opportunity for open pedagogy. Panelists will discuss their experiences using and creating zines in the classroom and ways DIY publishing can deepen student engagement. When: Wednesday, October 14 at 2:00PM Register for the Teaching with Zines Webinar Zine Party: A Making Day Join us for a Zine Fest in the Nest! We’ll have zines, hands-on crafts, hands-on event with zines, crafts, and open access. Hear welcome remarks from our keynote speaker Andrew Zonneveld, co-founder of On Our Own Authority! publishing house and the ATL Radical Book Fair. You’ll get the chance to dabble in different aspects of DIY publishing at stations around the Nest—walk around at your leisure, create, and learn! When: Wednesday, November 4 from 2:00-5:00PM Where: The Nest, Sturgis Library - First Floor, Kennesaw Campus No registration required. Open Access Week | October 19-23 Celebrate Open Access Week 2026 with the KSU Libraries! Open Access Week is an annual international event that celebrates the free and immediate online access to research, articles, books, and more worldwide. Visit the ground floor of Sturgis library during October 19-23 to view Our Open Story, a visual representation of how the Scholarly Publishing and Research team supports the Open Movements on campus. We’re also hosting events to promote the benefits of open access research. Attend and help the university advance the open access movement! In Conversation with Open Advocates: An Open Access Week Panel When: October 20 at 11:00AM Where: Virtual Event Who supports open access at your institution? Attend this virtual panel as we discuss the value of open access and the burgeoning open ecosystem we’ve created at Kennesaw State University (KSU) and within the University System of Georgia (USG). You’ll hear perspectives from open access advocates at the faculty, administrative, and university system level. Register for the Open Access Week Panel Digital Commons Drive-Thru When: October 20 from 1:00-4:00PM Where: Sturgis and Johnson Libraries Want to increase your work’s impact with a global audience? KSU Libraries’ Scholarly Publishing and Research team invites you to our Digital Commons Drive-Thru! Our team will review your CV for eligible works to share with the institutional repository. We’ll help you identify copyright considerations, upload your eligible publications to the appropriate collection, and ensure that you receive monthly metric reports to track your impact. Visit us at your convenience at either the Kennesaw or Marietta campus. Bring a paper copy of your CV and any questions you have. No registration required. Undergraduate Research Award 2026 The Undergraduate Research Award is open and accepting applications. Undergraduate students may submit one of their best papers and a separate project detailing how they used library and MARB resources. The grand prize includes: $500 in cash recognition at the Symposium of Student Scholars publication in the Kennesaw Journal of Undergraduate Research Review the detailed submission instructions and apply by December 4, 2026. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences College of Science & Mathematics Graduate College KSU Journey Honors College Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering & Engineering Technology Wellstar College of Health & Human Services Offices & Services Offices & Services University Registrar Parking & Transportation Student Affairs Housing & Residence Life Event & Venue Management University Information Technology Services Fiscal Services University Libraries Academic Advising Campus Operations Strategic Communications & Marketing Policies & Governance Policy Resources University Handbooks Institutional Policies Complaints & Appeals Conflict of Interest General Data Protection Regulation Protecting Minors Public Forum FERPA Governance University Council Administrators Council Staff Senate Faculty Senate Student Government A-Z Index KSU Home Open Access Publishing Fund University Libraries faculty Open Access Publishing Fund University Libraries Home Borrow & Request Research Support Get Library Help Space & Technology Faculty Resources About the Libraries Funding Guidelines The University Libraries, in conjunction with the Office of Research, supports Kennesaw State University faculty authors with the cost of open access manuscript publication through the Faculty Open Access Publishing Fund. Open access publishing assistance will be considered for publication or production costs (for example, Article Processing Charges) of peer-reviewed open access publications (like those indexed in the Directory of Open Access Journals or the Directory of Open Access Books ). Award Conditions The primary author should be a KSU faculty or staff member. Co-authors may be affiliated with other institutions. Requests should not exceed $3,000 . Funds will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. Multiple requests may be made, but individual authors will be restricted to one award per fiscal year. Authors should only apply after they have been accepted for publication. Awards will be paid directly to the publisher, not to the author(s). We prioritize funding gold open access journals. Hybrid open access journals are considered on a case-by-case basis. Learn more about gold vs. hybrid open access on our Open Access Research Guide . Open access funds are not available for applicants who are non-compliant with Institutional Review Board requirements. Authors will receive a response to their submission within 2 weeks. Authors must deposit an appropriate version of the funded manuscript in the institutional repository. Authors must include the University Libraries and the Office of Research in the acknowledgment section of their manuscript. Exclusions The following are not eligible for open access publishing funding: Requests in excess of $3,000 Anthologies Author’s comments Book indexing Book reviews Conference proceedings Fees for accelerated publication Fees for pre-acceptance Letters to the editor Manuscripts with mandatory embargoes Predatory journals Reprint costs of articles in professional journals Table of content production Translations Where else can I get funding? Authors who know they will need open access publishing funding in excess of $3,000 should explore outside funding options as soon as possible and make every effort to obtain funding from a variety of sources: Author’s college or department Internal funding opportunities External funding opportunities Before you submit, have the following information Proof of acceptance (for example, a letter or email from the publisher) Invoice from publisher in USD with the balance due clearly stated Confirmation that your manuscript will be made fully available open access at the time of publication Apply Now Apply For Funding Questions about this fund can be sent to its manager: Chelsee Dickson , Assistant Director for Scholarly Publishing and Research. Additional Resources For information on Open Access, visit our Open Access Research Guide. For information on publishing, visit our Publishing Research Guide. For information on author’s rights, visit our Copyright Research Guide . If you need further assistance, contact Chelsee Dickson , Assistant Director for Scholarly Publishing and Research. Access The New York Times New Resources Evidence-Based Acquisition (EBA) eBook Collections We have renewed our Evidence-Based Acquisition (EBA) eBook programs with Project MUSE and Wiley and added new programs from Cambridge University Press and Oxford University Press. These programs give the KSU community access to thousands of eBooks across many subject areas and disciplines, greatly expanding the number of titles available to students and faculty. At the end of the access period, we select titles for permanent purchase based on campus use, helping us build collections around demonstrated interest and need. Titles are available through the publisher's eBook platforms and can also be discovered through the library catalog and discovery system. Taylor and Francis Ebook Collections We added several Taylor & Francis eBook collections with permanent access. These collections are available through the Taylor & Francis eBooks platform and in the library catalog & SuperSearch. They support research and teaching across the social sciences and humanities. New collections include resources in areas such as social welfare, poverty studies, ethics and public life, diversity and inclusion, and the 2026 Anthropology ebook collection . Readex Primary Source Collections We now have access to several new Readex collections. These resources provide historical newspapers, archival materials, and primary source content useful for research in history, political science, sociology, public policy, and related disciplines. The collections can be searched together through Readex AllSearch or explored individually (links below). Printing and Copying Where are the printers? Once you print your document, you can release your job at any printer/copier on campus. Sturgis (Kennesaw) Library Ground Floor: Printers moved to first floor temporarily for summer renovation 2 Black/White & Color printers Black/White Student & Guest Printer 1st Floor (Owl Space Study Area) - near the South stairway Black/White & Color printer 2nd Floor - near the restrooms and South stairway Black/White & Color printer Johnson (Marietta) Library Main Floor (Hive Computer Lab): Next to the circular stairs on the main floor Black/White printer Color printer with guest printing function How much does printing cost? Black and White pages: $0.12 per side Color pages: $0.56 per side How do I pay for printing? The printers do not accept cash for printing. In order to print or copy, you must have KCash loaded on your Talon card or purchase a guest card. You can add money at any KCash machine on campus, or online using the KCash Manager . KCash machines can take bills in any denomination, but they cannot accept change. Please note: the Check Out Desk is unable to make change. There is a $5.00 minimum for credit/debit cards at the KCash machine. KCash machines accept Visa, MasterCard, and American Express cards. Mobile pay is not accepted at KCash machines. There are KCash machines in both libraries. Sturgis (Kennesaw) Library - located on the ground floor next to the self-check-out kiosk and across from the Research Help Desk. Temporarily moved to the first floor for summer renovation Johnson (Marietta) Library - located on the brick wall next to the Ricoh printers/copiers on main level. The KCash Manager requires a minimum deposit amount of $10.00. It may take a few minutes for KCash to appear on your account when using the KCash Manager. *Library guests must use a guest card to print. KCash guest cards can be purchased for $2 at a KCash machine prior to adding funds and printing. The locations of KCash machines on campus can be found here . Can I get a refund for pages that did not print correctly? If you experience an issue that results in the loss of funds or unusable pages, please contact KSU Printing Services for a refund. Front desk staff at the library cannot give refunds. How to Print From Computer Labs (KSU students) Log on to a computer with your NetID and password. When you are ready to print, select Student-Print-BW for black and white print jobs ($0.12 per side) or Student-Print-Color for color print jobs ($0.56 per side). Go to any Ricoh copier/printer.If you are printing black and white, you can use any machine. For color, you must use a color machine. Signs at the machines indicate BW or color. Tap your Talon card on the SmartCard Reader on the side of printer. Select the print job(s) you wish to print. Press the [Print] button. Tap your Talon card on the SmartCard Reader to log out. From Laptops Visit KSU Print or https://ksuprint.kennesaw.edu . Log in with your NetID and password. Select [Upload], find/select your file and select [open]. Check the box next to the uploaded document to specify printing options (ie , how many copies, color or BW). Please note: print jobs with any color content that are sent to the color printer will be charged for color. Tap your talon card on the SmartCard Reader on the side of printer. Select the print job(s) you wish to print. Press the [Print] button on the screen. Tap your talon card on the SmartCard Reader to log out. Guest Computers Before you can print or copy, you must purchase and activate a Guest Card for $2 and then add funds to the Guest Card for printing. Log on to a guest computer. There is no login information. When you are ready to print, select Guest-Print-BW for black and white print jobs ($0.12 per side) or Guest-Print-Color for color print jobs ($0.56 per side). Please note that Guest Printing is ONLY available in Black and White at Sturgis (Kennesaw). A pop-up should appear. Enter the Guest Card Number on the back of the Guest Card in the first field. Leave the password field blank and select “Print.” Go to the guest printer. Slide your Guest Card through the reader on the left side of printer. Select the print job(s) you wish to print. Press the [Print] button after selecting your print job(s). Slide your Guest Card through the card reader to log out. Award winners receive $500, recognition at the Symposium of Student Scholars, and publication in the Kennesaw Journal of Undergraduate Research (KJUR). Visit our collection that showcases the work of award winners and finalists. About the Award The KSU Libraries' Undergraduate Research Award is bestowed upon a currently enrolled (or recently graduated) undergraduate student who has demonstrated effective research processes and successful use of Museums, Archives, Rare Books, and Library (MARBL) resources and services. This includes utilization of at least one of the following: Online chat reference In-person or virtual research consultations Library databases Physical books and/or eBooks GIL Express to borrow materials from other University System of Georgia libraries Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Archives, Rare Books, or Special Collections One winner receives a $500 prize, which is awarded and disbursed by the KSU Libraries. The winner is guaranteed publication in the KJUR upon completion of the revision process. All runner-up articles will also be reviewed and considered for publication in the KJUR . The winner will receive their prize after they have revised and resubmitted their winning paper to the KJUR . Eligibility Requirements Applicants must be currently enrolled undergraduate students at KSU or recent graduates (within the last semester). Applicants must allow the KJUR to publish and share their research article and MARBL research project. Submission Requirements Applicants must submit both a research article and a project demonstrating their use of MARBL resources. For the research article , submit a current research paper you have recently written on any topic or subject and for any class. There are no minimum or maximum length requirements. Most submissions are 5-15 pages, double spaced. For the MARBL research project , select one of the following project options which highlights MARBL's role in supporting the creation of your research article: Option One: Application Essay Describe how MARBL resources and/or services (see options in About the Award section) were used in the research process and writing of the research article, and how they can improve undergraduate research. Applicants must refer to their research article within the application essay. Essays should follow a standard format including a title and structured paragraphs. Length: 500-700 words Acceptable formats: Word, RTF, or PDF Option Two: Marketing Video Videos must show how MARBL resources and/or services (see options in About the Award section) were used in the research process and writing of the research article, and how they can improve undergraduate research. Applicants must provide a link to their video or upload the video file. Videos must be formatted to YouTube or Instagram Reel. Applicants must refer to their research article within the video. Video must include a title slide/screen that includes the applicant’s name. Video length: 30 seconds – 2 minutes Contact Heather Hankins with any questions regarding video uploads. Application Evaluation Criteria The research article will be evaluated for clarity of writing, originality of ideas, use of MARBL resources, and thoughtful analysis of the research topic. The application essay or video will be evaluated for specific mention of MARBL resources and services used, as well as the role of MARBL in your research process. Submission Deadlines The submission portal is open until December 4, 2026. Finalists will be notified by January 13, 2027. The deadline to complete your revisions is February 12, 2027. FAQs Q: Who will judge the applications? A: Applications will be evaluated by a panel of KSU MARBL employees. Q: I recently graduated, but I conducted research and wrote a paper during my undergraduate education which I’d like to submit for publication. Am I eligible to apply for this award? A: Yes, but only if you have graduated within the last semester. Q: Can I submit more than one application per year? A: No, you may only submit one award application per year. However, you may submit multiple articles to the KJUR separately from this award. Q: If I've won the Undergraduate Research Award, can I apply again? A: No, if you have already won the Undergraduate Research Award, you cannot apply again. However, you are encouraged to pursue other awards and publication opportunities. Q: Will the award money impact my financial aid? A: Please contact the Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid with questions regarding any impact monetary awards might have on your specific financial aid situation. Q: What is the Digital Commons@Kennesaw State University? A: DigitalCommons@Kennesaw State University is a digital repository of the intellectual and creative output of the university community at KSU. This includes theses and dissertations, student work, faculty publications and books, journals, conference proceedings, and more. How to Apply Click here to begin the submission process . Create an account with the system. You will be redirected to the upload page. Complete the Article Submission Agreement, fill in the required information fields, and include metadata for your research article (i.e. title, abstract, keywords, etc.). Upload your research article. At the bottom of the upload form, attach your MARBL research project as a supplemental file. Submit your completed application. The manager of the Undergraduate Research Award will contact you if there are any issues with your submission. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences College of Science & Mathematics Graduate College KSU Journey Honors College Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering & Engineering Technology Wellstar College of Health & Human Services Offices & Services Offices & Services University Registrar Parking & Transportation Student Affairs Housing & Residence Life Event & Venue Management University Information Technology Services Fiscal Services University Libraries Academic Advising Campus Operations Strategic Communications & Marketing Policies & Governance Policy Resources University Handbooks Institutional Policies Complaints & Appeals Conflict of Interest General Data Protection Regulation Protecting Minors Public Forum FERPA Governance University Council Administrators Council Staff Senate Faculty Senate Student Government A-Z Index KSU Home Office of the Ombuds Visitor Information How We Can Help Contact Us Visitor Information The KSU Ombuds serve all members of the campus community and provides confidential, impartial, informal, and independent services to assist individuals with resolving problems or concerns. All members of the university community can seek assistance from an Ombuds at no cost. The Ombuds can help by listening as a sounding board, assisting in examining resolution options, suggesting possible referrals, making informal inquiries, or otherwise reviewing matters received. The response of the Ombuds is tailored to the dynamics of the situation and the visitor's concerns. All communication with the Ombuds Office is understood to be confidential. The Ombuds will not confirm communicating with any party or disclose information without that party's permission, except in cases where there is an imminent risk of harm to self or others. Please note that email and voicemail are not considered confidential. If you have an interest in ensuring the confidentiality of our communications, be mindful of what information you share via email or voicemail, and consider using the telephone or a face-to-face conversation instead. The Ombuds office is impartial, serving as neither advocate nor apologist for any members or offices of the KSU community. Hence the Ombuds assists visitors in finding ways to address their problems, rather than by prescribing or pursuing a particular solution for a visitor. The goal of the Ombuds is to empower a visitor with options, knowledge, consultation, information, and objective, non-binding advice. The Ombuds office operates informally, has no authority or role in any formal process on campus, and does not accept notice on behalf of KSU. The Ombuds functions independently of other campus processes and offices and has no vested interest or agenda, other than assisting visitors with reaching a satisfactory resolution to their concerns. We look forward to assisting you in exploring your options or gathering information to inform your decisions going forward. Meet Your Ombuds Dr. Luc Guglielmi The Office of the Ombuds is serviced by Dr. Luc Guglielmi. Dr. Luc D Guglielmi has been a professor at KSU since 2006. He has served as the Coordinator of the French program and as Director of a number of study abroad programs in Belgium and in France for the European Council of the University System of Georgia (now the University System of Georgia Goes Global) as well as at KSU. He has taught in multiple departments. How Ombuds Can Help An Ombuds can help by: Listening carefully to your concerns Answering questions and helping you analyze your situation Reviewing and explaining relevant university policies or regulations Helping you explore options Facilitating discussions Visitor feedback is appreciated! The following link provides the opportunity for you to give feedback on your experience with the Ombuds. The survey is anonymous and purely voluntary. Additional Resources Office of Institutional Equity Behavioral Response Team KSU Concern Submission Forms Human Resources Due to the confidential, neutral, informal, and independent function of the Ombuds Office, communication with this office does not constitute official notice to Kennesaw State University. Contact Us The KSU Ombuds serve all members of the campus community and can be contacted: Via Phone or Email: Contact the Ombuds by phone at 470-578-7773 or via email at ombuds@kennesaw.edu . Every attempt will be made to return all messages within 48 hours, or on Monday morning for messages received over the weekend. Explore New Routes Rapid 10: Take this route to travel between campuses, just like the Big Owl Bus Kennesaw/Marietta Route! From Kennesaw Campus: Board at the Frey Road CobbLinc stop. From Kennesaw Shuttle Lot: Board at the Busbee Park and Ride (3305 Busbee) From Marietta Campus: Board at Rossbacher Way (before East Lot 1). Route 40 & Route 45: These routes provide access to Town Center Mall, shopping areas along Barrett Parkway and Marietta Square. From Kennesaw Campus: Board at the Frey Road CobbLinc stop. From Marietta Campus: Walk about 15 minutes to the Marietta Transfer Center to catch the bus. Park in the Shuttle Lot. Ride to Marietta. Have a Shuttle Lot Permit? You can park in the Kennesaw Shuttle Lot and use the CobbLinc Rapid 10 to easily travel to the Marietta Campus. How to Get to Marietta Campus Step 1: Track your bus Download the MyStop mobile app to track CobbLinc buses in real time. Step 2: Head to Busbee Park and Ride From the Kennesaw Shuttle Lot, make your way to the Busbee Park and Ride. Step 3: Board the Rapid 10 Board the CobbLinc Rapid 10 and show your Mobile Talon Card to the driver. Step 4: Enjoy the ride! Sit back and relax while CobbLinc takes you directly to the Marietta Campus. Heading Back to Kennesaw? Catch the Rapid 10 from the CobbLinc stop on the Marietta Campus at Rossbacher Way, before East Lot 1. It’s that simple — park at the Shuttle Lot and let CobbLinc get you to Marietta! Did You Know? You can ride CobbLinc to Truist Park! Take the Rapid 10 route and once you arrive at the Cumberland Transfer Center, you can then take the free Circulator Blue route directly to The Battery Atlanta and Truist Park. From the Marietta Transfer Center, which is on all routes, you can transfer to other routes to explore even further! * *Transfers between CobbLinc routes are not included in this program. Check the CobbLinc website or download the myStop Mobile app to view stops, routes and other helpful information for your travel . CobbLinc Fares and Transfers Convenient Campus Travel Starting at the Busbee Park and Ride , the Rapid 10 provides an easier way to travel to the Marietta Campus for students who live in off-campus apartments including: Bixby Sova Parliament The Indy Copper Social Aldridge at Town Village MAA Milstead Why Choose CobbLinc? Closer Pickup Locations: Skip the long walk to campus bus stops! CobbLinc offers pick-up spots that are closer to where you live, so you can hop on right near your off-campus apartment. Convenience & Flexibility: With CobbLinc, you have more frequent pick-ups and routes that work better around your schedule. Later Route Times and Weekend Services: CobbLinc offers later routes and more routes during the week and on weekends! To view all CobbLinc hours of operations, visit their website. Download the myStop Mobile App The myStop Mobile App allows you to view when the CobbLinc buses will arrive at the Big Owl Bus Stops and to your desired location(s). Download from the App Store Download on Google Play CobbLinc Holiday Hours Please note that CobbLinc operates during special holiday hours that may affect route schedules. Be sure to check the CobbLinc website for updates on holiday service times and any route changes. Charter Request Form Charter Policy Charter Request Submission and Approval Requests must be submitted at least ten business days prior to the event. Approval or denial of service will be provided in an email within three to five business days of the request being received, and will provide a quote for the cost of the service being requested. The requester will then need to provide a confirmation email stating their acceptance of the service being offered, commitment to pay, and agreement of stated charter policies. We are unfortunately unable to fulfill all requests. Our ability to provide charters is based on availability of vehicles, drivers, and our primary academic obligation to serve our students, faculty and staff. Request Guidelines During the academic school year charters are subject to availability. Charters are subject to a 50-mile radius of the James V. Carmichael Student Center or the Joe Mack Wilson Student Center. We are unable to provide overnight charters. Charter requests may be for a maximum of 12 hours, eight of which may be drive time. Standing is not permitted on charter vehicles. Charter service to nightclubs and adult entertainment venues is prohibited. Unless exempt, applicable sales tax will still apply. Parking fees and tolls will be charged if encumbered during the service. Non-affiliated groups or individuals must provide a security deposit three business days prior to scheduled service. The security deposit is equal to half of the quoted cost of services requested. Checks should be written out to Kennesaw State University. While on Board No signage or markings of any kind may be placed on the window, vehicle door, exterior or the interior of the vehicle. The following are prohibited on Parking and Transportation vehicles: eating, drinking, glass containers, alcohol, weapons, tobacco products, e-cigarettes, illegal drugs, hazardous materials and animals (with the exception of registered service animals). Cancellations Cancellations and modifications are allowed up to 72 hours prior to time of service without penalty. These change requests must be submitted via email to talonone@kennesaw.edu . All cancellations received 72 hours prior to the time of service will be subject to a penalty equal to the minimum three hours of service for each vehicle being chartered. Modifications received less than 72 hours prior to the time of service will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Service modifications may not be requested of the driver on the day of service. Damage Fees A cleaning fee of $200 will be added to any charter if the vehicle is not returned in a reasonable condition. Costs for any damages caused by the chartering group will be billed to the responsible department, group or person. This option is only available for KSU Departments with a University speed chart number. Making an E-Coupon Request E-coupon codes must be requested online through the E-Coupon Request Form at least five business days prior to the event. Departments will be billed based on e-coupon usage after the event. Billing for coupon codes is half the price of the posted visitor parking rate for the lot requested. Standard rates are displayed at each hourly visitor parking area. Lots that are set up for validation are: Kennesaw Campus: the Visitor Lot near the Carmichael Student Center, Lot J, Lot V2 and the North Parking Deck. Marietta Campus: the Visitor Lot near Wilson Student Center (formerly Lot P2), Lot E (formerly P21) and the West Deck (formerly P60). The West Deck is a mixed-use deck and visitor parking in that area is marked with striping and signage. Upon a visitor’s arrival, they will be required to input their vehicle license plate number and coupon code at one of the designated pay stations. Rates for validated parking are determined based on the length of stay. Policy Restrictions Visitor must input license plate number at pay station and select the appropriate length of stay. Failure to do so may result in a citation. No refunds will be issued for E-coupon usage. E-coupon codes must be requested with a minimum of five business days’ notice prior to the event. If a code is requested with less than five days’ notice, Parking and Transportation reserves the right to decline the request. E-coupon codes are valid for a maximum of 60 days; after 60 days, a new code should be requested. The university is proud to be part of the greater Atlanta community and offers its facilities for private events and affairs to local groups, schools, and community functions. Parking and Transportation provides access to its parking facilities whenever possible. The favorable approach is to always have attendees pay the visitor parking fee. An alternative to this is to use parking e-coupons , which must be obtained from the department that is sponsoring the event. Small Event Parking (less than 20 vehicles) When a smaller event is planned on campus for a number of attendees that can be accommodated within visitor parking (less than 20 vehicles, depending on the campus traffic for the requested day), the process is to route attendees to visitor parking, where they will pay the parking fees: Structure Fee for the Kennesaw Campus $3 for the first hour Additional $1 every half hour thereafter Maximum $12 per day Structure Fee for the Marietta Campus $3 for the first hour Additional $1 every half hour thereafter Maximum $12 per day Or you can submit an online request for an e-coupon code and issue these to the attendees. Large Event Parking (more than 20 vehicles) To ensure the best experience possible for guests, events that involve larger groups with more than 20 vehicles expected is best served by our University Events department. Your event needs will be tracked and managed with the University with regards to logistics, parking, security, etc. Connect to the University Event Management System IMPORANT: If the event is for VIP’s and/or special guests of the University, it is advisable to contact University Events for assistance no matter the size of the event.
