Before you make a purchase, it's important to follow university guidelines to ensure a smooth and secure process. In accordance with USG policy, UITS reviews all new technology hardware and software prior to purchase or rental to ensure it: Fits within the technology environment at KSU Does not pose a security risk Does not duplicate technology already available at the University Standard Technology UITS offers a selection of standard computers, tablets, HP printers, cellular devices, and peripherals, such as monitors, keyboards, headsets, or webcams in our Product Catalog. View Product Catalog Cellular Devices & Plans Non-Standard Technology Non-standard technology will require a quote from the vendor and review from UITS to ensure the item can be supported by the University, fits within the technology environment at KSU, does not pose a security risk, and does not duplicate technology already available at the University. Non-standard technology requires: A vendor-provided quote A review by UITS to ensure compatibility and supportability Examples of non-standard technology includes: Software and subscriptions Web applications 3D printers IT professional services Point-of-sale (POS) devices Hardware not listed in KSU’s standard offerings Other technology-integrated equipment Request a Quote Do you have technology you would like to purchase? To request a quote, complete the Quote Request Form . After submission, you will typically receive a quote along with UITS approval via DocuSign within two to five business days. Request a Quote Did you obtain your own quote? Already have a quote? If you obtained your own quote, the next step is the pre-purchase technology review required by the USG. Please follow the steps on the Technology Approval Form . Technology Approval Form Next Steps After Receiving Approval After UITS has reviewed the technology and you have received approval, your department is ready to follow the procurement process to purchase the item. Once technology has undergone pre-purchase review and received approval from UITS, it has been verified to meet USG and KSU standards. Frequently Asked Questions What technology needs to be reviewed and approved by UITS? Per USG policy, UITS is required to conduct a pre-purchase review of and approve all technology not previously approved for purchase or rental at KSU, including all: Technology hardware, including (but not limited to) computers, printers, scanners, displays, headphones, wireless presenters, webcams, audio/visual equipment such as cameras and microphones, and other technology accessories. Software not already provided standard by KSU When should requests for pre-purchase review and approval be submitted? A request for technology pre-purchase review and approval must be requested after a quote has been received but before placing an order to purchase or rent technology. (See below for more information about technology quotes.) How should I request a technology pre-purchase review and approval? First, you will need a technology quote. Please complete this form: Quote Request Form . Once you have a quote, you should submit a request for UITS to review and approve the technology by completing the Technology Approval Form . Important: Once technology has undergone pre-purchase review and received approval from UITS, it has been verified to meet USG and KSU standards. However, technology approval is not budget approval. Because technology is ordered and paid for by an employee’s department, the employee must ensure they have budget approval from their supervisor and/or budget owner. All purchases must be made in accordance with KSU’s procurement guidelines . Resources like training sessions, guides for tools such as D2L Brightspace, and AV equipment support are available to enhance teaching effectiveness. Faculty and staff can access these resources or request specialized assistance to integrate technology into their instruction. Owl Express D2L Brightspace Additional Resources Employee & Student Information Portal: Owl Express Owl Express (Banner) is KSU’s employee and student information portal. All Employees Log in to Owl Express and select Employee Services to quickly access parking and vehicle information, update your preferred name, make sure you (and employees you manage) are up to date on required training, and more. Faculty Log in to Owl Express and select Faculty Services to view your course schedules and rosters for each class you teach (including photo rosters of your students). At the end of each term, this is where you will post students’ final grades. Please note that courses added to your roster by the registrar typically populate in Owl Express several weeks before they appear in D2L Brightspace. (For students, classes typically appear in D2L Brightspace on the day of the first class meeting.) Learning Management System: D2L Brightspace D2L Brightspace is the USG's Learning Management System. UITS supports faculty needs as you set up and manage course content on D2L Brightspace. Find detailed information about course availability, course-related requests (course shell, course reset, third party integration, enrollment), account access, and updates to the D2L Brightspace system and related technologies here: D2L Brightspace Information for Faculty and Staff . Using D2L Brightspace Kennesaw State University's D2L Brightspace is a comprehensive Learning Management System that supports the university's academic needs. This platform provides students, faculty, and staff with convenient access to course materials, assignments, and updates. Faculty and staff can find detailed guidance on managing courses, accessing technical support, and integrating third-party tools. Students can access their current and upcoming term courses, with additional resources available for eCore courses and course date modifications. How to Set Up Authenticator on a New Phone Get started in 3 easy steps: Visit mfa.kennesaw.edu from your computer. Download Microsoft Authenticator on your mobile device and complete setup. Update your Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) methods to ensure password recovery. Need more detailed instructions? Refer to this Knowledge Base article . You will use Microsoft Authenticator to verify your identity whenever you sign into KSUmail, D2L, and most other KSU services. Please note: We strongly recommend registering at least two devices with Microsoft Authenticator to ensure you can access your account if your primary device is lost or damaged. Receiving an Unexpected Microsoft Authenticator Prompt IMPORTANT: If you ever receive a Microsoft Authenticator notification at a time when you’re not signing in to a KSU application, deny the request and immediately reset your password at changepassword.kennesaw.edu . Change NetID Password How Can I Get Help With Microsoft Authenticator? Contact the IT Service Desk: Hours & Locations service@kennesaw.edu 470–578-6999 Frequently Asked Questions What is Microsoft Authenticator? Kennesaw State University uses Microsoft Authenticator as a multifactor authentication method to protect student and employee accounts when logging into applications like Owl Express, KSUmail, D2L Brightspace, and Virtual Machines. Can I register more than one device? Yes! In fact, we strongly recommend registering more than one device because this will ensure that you have easy access to multiple authentication methods in the event that you do not have access to your primary device. I don’t have a smartphone. Can I still authenticate? Yes. When prompted to install the app, select “I want to set up a different method” and choose Phone call. Enter your personal phone number. After setup, select the “I want to set up a different method” option again and choose Email, then enter your non-KSU email address. Can I set up Microsoft Authenticator using my phone only? Setup requires scanning a QR code with your phone’s camera, so while it's not impossible, it can be tricky. We recommend using a laptop or desktop for initial setup. What if I already have Microsoft Authenticator installed? You can add your KSU account to your existing app without reinstalling. Follow the guides for iPhone and Android . Can I use a token like I had with Duo? MFA tokens are available at the KSU Bookstore Why shouldn’t I use my Teams calling number for authentication? Do not use your Teams number. If you’re locked out, Teams won’t help you regain access. Also, calls may not go through during active calls or when Do Not Disturb is enabled. Use a personal phone number. Why didn’t I receive the Microsoft authentication call? If the call is blocked, add Microsoft’s number (470-578-2632) to your contacts and check your Focus/Do Not Disturb settings. Why am I prompted for my PIN or biometrics when opening Authenticator? App Lock is turned on. Learn how to turn this off here: How to turn off App Lock in the Microsoft Authenticator app What number will Microsoft Authenticator call me from? Authentication calls come from 470-578-2632. Save this number and adjust Focus/Do Not Disturb settings to ensure you receive calls. What data does Microsoft Authenticator collect? The app collects: Your username (NetID) Authentication success/failure Your phone’s operating system Your country (for location-based access control) This data is used solely for authentication and will only be shared as required by law or during institutional investigations. Does using the app make my personal device subject to open records? No. Microsoft Authenticator does not make your personal device subject to open records. Do students need to use Microsoft Authenticator for KSUmail and Microsoft 365? Yes. All students must use Microsoft Authenticator for KSUmail, Microsoft 365, and other campus applications. NetID is the username for centralized access to KSU campus resources. It is formatted as the first initial of your first name and a portion of your last name, often followed by numerals. For example, Scrappy Owl's NetID is sowl , and his full email address is sowl@kennesaw.edu . This username will be used to gain access to most campus-supported technologies. Your NetID password expires a year after the last date it was changed . You will receive email notifications 30 days before the expiration, and additional reminders as the expiration nears. You can change your password at changepassword.kennesaw.edu . To protect your account, KSU requires Multifactor Authentication (MFA) when signing in with your NetID. Learn more and set up MFA. Your KSU ID (eg.000192837) is a nine-digit number that is created when you apply to KSU. Your KSU ID is printed on your acceptance letter, and you can also look it up online: KSU Lookup. New to KSU? Forgot Your Password? Change Your Password NetID First-Time Users Welcome to KSU! Look up your KSU# and NetID and initial password. Navigate to the Multi-Factor Authentication login page and sign in using your NetID and initial password. Follow the prompts to reset your password and set up Microsoft Authenticator and Self-Service Password Recovery (SSPR) information. Once your account is activated, your password will be valid for 365 days after the activation date. Need help navigating through the process? Review this NetID and KSU ID instruction article. Forgot Your Password? Navigate to forgotpassword.kennesaw.edu and follow the prompts to reset your password. Password Tips Still need help? Call us at 470-578-6999. Changing Your NetID Password Did you receive an email notice stating that your password expires soon? Your NetID password expires a year after the last date it was changed. Please read this important information, and then navigate to changepassword.kennesaw.edu to change your password. *Before changing your password, set mobile devices to airplane mode and log out of Outlook. Updating Passwords on Mobile Device Email Before changing your NetID password, you must set your mobile devices to Airplane mode to prevent getting locked out of your accounts. iPhone/iPad To set Airplane Mode: Tap Settings Switch Airplane Mode to On setting To change Password: Tap Settings Tap Mail, Contacts, Calendars Locate your KSU Email account and select it Tap the field labeled Account Update the password Tap Done to close the Account window Tap Done to close the KSU email window Return to Airplane Mode and switch to Off Enter your new password when prompted to re-connect to the KSU Wi-Fi Note: Updating your NetID password does not in any way affect your Apple ID passwords, or third-party service passwords (Dropbox, GMail, etc.) so you do not need to change any of your iTunes, iCloud, or App Store passwords. Android To set Airplane Mode: Hold down the power button Tap Airplane Mode Tap OK to confirm, if prompted To change Password on Android 2.3.x: Tap Settings Tap Accounts Locate your KSU email account Update the password Return to Airplane Mode and switch to Off Reconnect to KSU Wi-Fi with new password To update password on Android 4.1.x: Tap Settings Tap Microsoft Exchange Active Sync under Accounts Tap Settings Locate and tap your KSU email account Scroll down and tap Exchange Server Settings Update the password Return to Airplane Mode by holding down the power button and switch to Off Tap Done Reconnect to KSU Wi-Fi with new password Password Requirements Must be at least 12 characters long At least one uppercase letter and at least one lowercase letter At least one special character: -!"#$%&()*./:;?@[\]^_{|}~+<= >` Cannot use l33t speak (substituting numbers or symbols for letters) Cannot reuse old passwords Cannot be found in compromised password databases Should be a strong passphrase instead of a single word What to Do After Your NetID Password Changes You may have software on your computer(s), which stores your NetID password in order to access various services. When you change your NetID password, you should also be sure to update any stored NetID password to reflect the new password and avoid being locked out of your account. Updating Stored Passwords on Macs Mac OS X Launch the Passwords application . Log in with your updated NetID password or biometric (ex. TouchID). Locate saved KSU account passwords by searching for your NetID. Click the account you would like to update the password for. Click the Edit button in the upper right corner. Highlight your previous password in the Password field. Press the delete or backspace key on your keyboard to clear the field. Type in your new NetID password. Get Help. With resources from academic assistance to health and emergencies, these resources will allow you to get the immediate help and assistance you need at KSU. See Something, Say Something. KSU seeks to foster a proactive climate of care that can only be achieved through cooperative input from the entire community. Through identification, we can connect concerns with the resources to succeed. Campus Maps Kennesaw State University includes two main campuses in Cobb County about 20-30 minutes north of Atlanta, GA. No matter where you choose to visit us, we hope you’ll love Kennesaw State University as much as we do. Student Success Possessing computer skills and feeling comfortable online does not necessarily ensure your success in an online course. A common theme in online courses is self-discipline and persistence. At Kennesaw State, we are committed to helping our online students achieving their academic best. Online Student Success Frequently Asked Questions What are the benefits of online learning? Online learning provides considerable freedom, allowing students to often choose when and where they'll participate in class activities. Save time and money spent commuting to a campus Continue working at your current job while you are taking classes Attend your class from anywhere as long as you have a high-speed Internet connection Learn at your own pace and study at your convenience Learn new technologies Interact on equal footing Students will have the same kinds of deadlines and structured responsibilities of a face-to-face class. In other words, flexibility must be balanced by responsibility. Like a face-to-face course, online courses require assignments be completed by due dates, your attendance (via logins to your course), involvement in online discussions, and sometimes group collaboration. Most students enjoy the active learning that online classes involve. What are the challenges of online learning? Self-motivation and discipline are required to succeed in distance learning courses. For many, distance learning offers access to education not previously available. It also provides a solution to flexibility needs, work and travel responsibilities, and family challenges. A successful experience in distance learning requires a basic familiarity with technology. Resources are available for students through University Information Technology Services for those interested in distance learning, but in need of a technology refresher. It is also strongly recommended that students have ready access to a computer or laptop with a high-speed Internet access, such as DSL or cable broadband. Online courses will require students to download and access course materials. Online learning success depends on preparation, motivation, dedication, and planning. What equipment and technology will I need to be successful at online learning? Online learners will need a computer, Internet access, basic software (such as Microsoft Office Suite, Windows Media Player, Quicktime movie player, anti-virus protection and a compatible browser), and auxiliary equipment (such as a webcam and microphone headset for video-based communication). Of course, technology needs will vary by course. But this list applies to the majority of courses. Computer: Online Learners will need reliable access to a desktop or laptop computer that has adequate memory and processing capabilities for large file downloads, video players, and synchronous meeting applications. Auxiliary Equipment: The Digital Learning Innovations team also strongly recommends a WebCam and Headset for video-based communication. Many newer laptop or monitor set-ups are pre-equipped. These items may be required by faculty on a course-by-course basis. Internet Access: Online courses at KSU use the web to deliver courses at a distance. So, to learn in an online course smoothly, you need a high-speed Internet connection (such as DSL, Broadband, etc). This is especially important to the online learning experience. Software: While this will vary by course, you will need a recent version of the Microsoft Office Suite. Access to MS Word, MS PowerPoint, and MS Excel are expected and necessary for viewing course material or completing assignments. Additional requirements include anti-virus protection, Windows Media Player, QuickTime movie player, and a compatible browser. Visit UITS Training for additional information on software training, compatibility, and available downloads. HAVE MORE QUESTIONS? Supplemental PP from 2.27.2020 Meeting (PDF) NCUR 2019 (PDF) Synergy Presentation (PDF) One USG Presentation (PDF) QEP Planning (PDF) CC Power Point (PDF) KSU R2 Roadmap to Success (PDF) Bylaws: Creating Effective Communication & Governance The Bylaws of the Administrators Council at Kennesaw State outline the structure, mission, and responsibilities of the Council, which is dedicated to fostering effective communication and shared governance within the University. It details the purpose, goals, membership criteria, officer roles, election procedures, and committee structures. These bylaws serve as a foundational guide for the Council’s operations and decision-making processes, ensuring that it fulfills its role in supporting administrators and contributing to the university's objectives. ARTICLE 1: NAME AND PURPOSE The purpose of the Administrators Council is to promote effective communication, collegiality and shared governance of the University in matters regarding the development of policy and to increase bi-directional communication about the implementation of policy. The Council reports to the Provost and is responsible for the implementation of shared governance decisions and policies among its constituents. In addition, the Administrators Council is also responsible for providing feedback on issues affecting administrators and their reports. ARTICLE 2: MISSION AND GOALS The mission of the Administrator’s Council is to act as a forum and advocate for administrators by providing leadership and guidance on issues which affect the interest of administrators, representing them to the University administration and keeping them informed on University initiatives and policies. The Council works to create a culture that promotes the fulfillment of overall university goals and objectives and provide an educational environment that promotes the growth and improvement of higher education and KSU. ARTICLE 3: MEMBERSHIP AND PARTICIPATION Section 1. Membership Requirements and Privileges A. Council membership is open to all administrators who meet the following criteria: Hold the Human Resource title/designation of Director or above Manage two or more direct reports Manage a budget Responsible for strategic planning Responsible for implementation of policy Approval of Supervisor B. Assistant Vice Presidents or their equivalents may serve on the Administrators Council or may delegate the responsibility to one or more individuals in order to represent major departments within his/her division. C. Member duties: Members are responsible for regularly attending Council meetings, participating in Council business and discussions, disseminating information, and soliciting feedback about new University policies, programs and initiatives. If a member cannot commit to the meeting schedule and therefore cannot carry out Administrative Council duties, he/she should inform his/her supervisor who should designate an alternate. D. Any member may be nominated or may self-nominate for elected officer positions. Section 2. Voting Privileges for Officer Elections Voting privileges for officer elections are open to all members of the Council. ARTICLE 4: OFFICERS Section 1. Chair The Chair is responsible for scheduling meetings of the Council and establishing an agenda for each meeting. The Chair represents the Administrators Council on the University Council and in discussions with other shared governance groups and committees. The Chair shall charge ad hoc committees as necessary. Section 2. Chair Elect The Chair Elect becomes the Chair after the incumbent Chair has completed his/her term. The Chair Elect shall serve instead of the Chair in the event the Chair is unable to perform his/her duties. Section 3. Past Chair Upon completion of his/her term, the Chair shall serve one year in the capacity of Past Chair. The Past Chair shall serve in an advisory capacity to the current Chair and Chair-Elect and assist in the transition of the Chair Elect to Chair Section 4. Recording Secretary The Secretary shall see that the minutes of each meeting are recorded and distributed to the Members within 15 calendar days of the meeting. Section 5. Removal of Officers Officers are required to attend all scheduled meetings of the Council; if circumstances prevent an Officer from attending, he/she must communicate the absence to the Chair. If an Officer fails to notify the Chair about an absence, it will be considered an unexcused absence. Officers with three (3) absences in one (1) year will be removed from the Executive Committee. The Chair or Chair Elect may call an election process at any time to elect an Officer to fill the remainder of the term. ARTICLE 5: ELECTIONS Section 1. Election Procedures The election of the Chair Elect and Secretary shall occur at the last Council meeting of the academic year. A simple majority is sufficient to elect Officers. Voting may be carried out either in person at meetings or electronically. All members of the Council are eligible to serve as Chair or Chair Elect. The Chair Elect will assume his/her responsibilities as Chair at the first Council meeting of the academic year. Section 2. Terms of Office Each officer shall serve a term of one year. Officers are eligible to serve second terms if so elected to a limit of three consecutive years. ARTICLE 6: COMMITTEES Section 1. The committees of the Administrators Council shall include an Executive Committee. Other committees may be established on an ad hoc basis. Section 2. The Executive Committee The Chair, Past Chair, Chair Elect and Recording Secretary will constitute the Executive Committee of the Administrators Council. The Executive Committee will serve as an advisory committee to the Chair. The Executive Committee shall advise the Chair about the agenda for the meetings of the Council and work together to facilitate initiatives and/or projects. Section 3. Standing and Ad Hoc Committees Standing and Ad Hoc committees of the Council shall consist of Council members who volunteer their services for one term. ARTICLE 7: MEETINGS Section 1. Quorum Requirement A simple majority of members shall constitute a quorum. A quorum is required for any vote taken by the Council but is not required for a meeting. The number of members shall be determined at the beginning of each academic year in fall for the purpose of determining a quorum. Section 2. Regular Meetings Schedule The Administrative Council shall meet no fewer than six (6) times per academic year during the fall and spring semesters. The Chair may call for meetings during the summer if necessary. Section 3. The Chair shall set the time and place of meetings and establish the agenda. ARTICLE 8: Operating Document Revisions Section 1. Proposed revisions to this operating document must be approved by two-thirds of voting members of the Administrator’s Council. AAUP@KSU is the largest AAUP chapter in the state of Georgia, and exists to protect academic freedom and promote shared governance between faculty, staff, administrators, and students at Kennesaw State. Ours is a vibrant chapter, with over seventy KSU faculty as members, representing every college in the university. In recent years we have helped create and implement the shared governance system at Kennesaw State, including the faculty senate, department and college faculty councils, and the administrative review process. We continue to represent faculty interests and to respond to concerns related to academic freedom, shared governance, and fair process. Please join us as we continue to advocate for equitable faculty compensation, transparent decision-making, and other important concerns. We hope you can participate in our monthly business meetings and faculty social hours. Follow the Meetings & Events link on the navigation bar to the left to find a full schedule of events. To see our bylaws and our goals for the year, follow the link to Chapter Business. We also have an external website: http://aaupkennesaw.org/ (opens in new window) Academic Freedom The History Academic freedom has been the central preoccupation of the American Association of University Professors since its founding in 1915. Academic tenure, with its protections against arbitrary dismissal for those with unpopular views, is a vital foundation of academic freedom. Here and Now It is tempting to think that the McCarthy era is long past, and the tradition of academic freedom is well established. In fact, Georgia, like many states, is currently considering legislation aimed at forcing professors to give ideas like Intelligent Design and hyper-patriotic versions of American history an “appropriate” place in the college classroom. Teachers and practitioners of the dramatic and visual arts have also seen their creative freedom inappropriately constrained owing to anxieties about local popular opinion. What the AAUP does The AAUP’s 1940 “Statement of Principles on Academic Freedom and Tenure” has been endorsed by the major academic organizations in every discipline of the academy. AAUP is generally recognized as the authoritative voice of the academic profession with respect to these issues. The AAUP’s Committee A investigates charges of violations of Academic Freedom, Tenure and Academic Due Process. Universities found guilty of “especially blameworthy” violations are places on AAUP’s Censure List. AAUP has led the response to the so-called "Academic Bill of Rights" campaign mounted by David Horowitz and other activists. See the AAUP assessment of the campaign and why it is a danger to the academy. The battle for Academic Freedom is far from over. Academic Freedom at Kennesaw State University One of the central roles of KSU@AAUP is to ensure that academic freedom and the tenure process are protected. Please see our Important Documents page for information about how KSU@AAUP has worked to improve and clarify the tenure and promotion process at Kennesaw State University. If you think that your academic freedom has been violated, or that your tenure process is not proceeding according to the Faculty Handbook or your department’s bylaws, please contact KSU@AAUP. This includes fundamental values of transparency and objectivity. USG employees are required to be honest, fair, and impartial in dealings with, and on behalf of, the USG. In accordance with USG policies, Kennesaw State University (KSU) employees are required to make every reasonable effort to avoid actual or apparent conflicts of interest. Please refer to the button below for the Board of Regents (BOR) Policy Manual for additional information. (BOR) Policy Manual Reporting and Disclosing Potential Conflict of Interests All faculty and staff have an ongoing responsibility to report and fully disclose any personal, professional, or financial interest, relationship, or activity that has the potential to create an actual or apparent conflict of interest with respect to the employee’s KSU duties, and obtain an approved management plan that properly defines and manages any actual and apparent conflicts of interest. Each KSU employee with a work commitment of 30 or more hours per week, and faculty members on contracts of nine months or more must obtain written approval prior to engaging in compensated outside activities that relate to the employee’s expertise or responsibilities as a KSU employee. Such activities include consulting, teaching, speaking, and participating in business, professional, or service enterprises. Employees who do not fall under these categories do not need written approval in advance of engaging in compensated outside activities so long as the outside activity does not create a conflict of interest or otherwise violate BOR policy. To submit a request to engage in an outside activity, or to disclose a conflict of interest, please access the Outside Activities and Conflicts of Interest Dashboard in Owl Express. The Dashboard is located under the Employee Services tab in Owl Express. Owl Express Using KSU Resources for Assistance Use of KSU Resources Generally, KSU resources may only be used in furtherance of authorized KSU business. However, KSU employees may request to use KSU resources through a written contract that provides that the university will be paid for the use of any KSU personnel, facilities, equipment, or materials at a rate which is at least the rate KSU charges to outside entities. Approval of such a contract must be obtained pursuant to KSU’s contracting policies and is in addition to the approval required to engage in the outside activity. Furthermore, such use shall be tightly controlled, and employees must be able to provide information as to the location of all KSU equipment and resource usage upon request. Required Statements 1. Any agreement for an outside activity executed between an outside entity and a KSU faculty or staff member must include the following statement: “The consultant has certain obligations to Kennesaw State University as a faculty member as described in the Intellectual Property Policy of Kennesaw State University (IP Policy). In the event that there is any conflict between the consultant’s obligations to the IP Policy and their obligations to the entity for whom they consult, the obligations to the IP Policy shall control.” 2. Any presentations or reports written, signed, or prepared by a KSU faculty or staff member for an outside entity as part of an outside activity must state: “This content represents the opinions of the consultant. It carries no endorsement by Kennesaw State University.” Contact Information Kennesaw Campus 1000 Chastain Road Kennesaw, GA 30144 Marietta Campus 1100 South Marietta Pkwy Marietta, GA 30060 Phone 470-KSU-INFO (470-578-4636) Campus Maps Parking Media Resources Campus A-Z Index Academic Calendar Campus News D2L Brightspace University Information Technology Services Related Links Libraries Housing Financial Aid Degrees, Majors & Programs Registrar Job Opportunities Campus Security Global Education Sustainability Accessibility © 2026 Kennesaw State University. This law was developed by the European Union and takes effect 25 May 2018. It applies to any organization that handles the personal information of any resident in the European Union (EU), regardless of where in the world that organization is located. GDPR requires organizations to maintain the privacy and security of any EU resident’s personal information. This website will serve to inform the University community on how to interpret and achieve compliance under GDPR. USG GDPR Memorandum GDPR Consent Form GDPR Policy Frequently Asked Questions What is the EU GDPR and When Does it Take Effect? The European Union General Data Protection Regulation (“EU GDPR”) is a new and more stringent regulation governing the use of personal data. It imposes new obligations on entities that control or process personal data about people who are located in the European Union. This regulation applies both inside the European Union (“EU”) and outside of the EU, and applies to data about anyone in the EU, regardless of whether they are a citizen or permanent resident of an EU country. The regulation takes effect on May 25, 2018. Who is Covered by the EU GDPR? The EU GDPR covers any entity that processes personal data about EU citizens or residents in connection with the offer of goods and services in the EU or the monitoring of behavior in the EU. Jurisdiction is therefore established digitally rather than physically. We can evaluate various factors in establishing coverage, including currencies and languages used, how a website references the individual and the profiling of the individual. What Countries Comprise the List of EU GDPR Member Nations? Austria Belgium Bulgaria Croatia Cyprus Czech Republic Denmark Estonia Finland Franc Germany Greece Hungary Ireland Italy Latvia Lithuania Luxembourg Malta Netherlands Poland Portugal Romania Slovakia Slovenia Spain Sweden United Kingdom What Information is Subject to the EU GDPR? The EU GDPR applies to the control or processing of ‘personal data,’ which is defined by the regulation as: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (the data subject); an identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, psychological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that natural person. Examples of identifiers include (but are not limited to): name, photo, email address, identification number such as KSU ID#, KSU Account (User ID), physical address or other location data; IP address, mobile device identifiers or geo-location data about a subject. Unique biometric data, such as fingerprints and retinal scans, and genetic data are also included. What are the Kennesaw State University Security Standards and Requirements for EU GDPR Data? All personal data and sensitive personal data collected or processed by any Kennesaw State University Unit under the scope of the EU General Data Protection Regulation Compliance Policy must comply with the security safeguards and process requirements defined therein. Does Kennesaw State University Have a Policy Concerning EU GDPR data? Yes. The Kennesaw State University EU General Data Protection Regulation Compliance Policy can be found in the university Policy Portal. If I Have Questions About My Personal Data That is Subject to the EU GDPR, Who Should I Talk to? Individuals with questions about their personal data collected and processed by Kennesaw State University that is subject to the EU GDPR should contact the Office of Legal Affairs at asklegal@kennesaw.edu . Does the University Require my Consent Before Collecting and Processing my Sensitive Personal Data? Individuals will be asked to sign a consent form by the department collecting their personal data. The form will be clear and easily understandable. Your consent must be freely given and is revocable at any time without detriment to you. If you should have any question about the form you should contact the Office of Legal Affairs. Where do I Find a Model Consent Form for the Collection and Processing of Sensitive Personal Data? GDPR-EU Model Consent Form Does the EU GDPR Apply to Kennesaw State University's Cooperative Organizations? Yes. If the Cooperative Organization process personal data of persons located in the EU, then the EU GDPR applies to those collection and processing activities. The Cooperative Organizations should follow their respective compliance policies in regard to this data. If I am Conducting Research Within the EU, What Special Precautions Should I Take? If you are planning a research project in any country in the EU the study must first be approved by the KSU IRB . Human subject research in the EU will now require two forms of consent, the KSU consent form and the GDPR consent form. The researcher is responsible for obtaining the required signatures and for the retention of both the IRB and EU consent forms. In addition, when conducting research abroad, the researcher must obtain permission to collect data from someone in a position of authority who can provide a letter to the IRB indicating that local permission has been granted ( e.g., the mayor, police chief, town official, etc ). Serving as an advisory body to the Provost, PAOC ensures compliance with NCAA regulations, maintains institutional control, and upholds academic integrity in athletics. The Council, comprising faculty, administrators, student-athletes, and community members, meets regularly to review policies, oversee strategic planning, and support student-athlete success. The Provost's Athletics Oversight Council (PAOC) assists the University Provost with: Maintaining Institutional Control of Athletics Assuring the Academic Integrity of Athletics' policies and practices Ensuring Compliance with NCAA Rules About the PAOC Approved by the Faculty Senate on April 9, 2007 Amended by the Council, November 14, 2012 Amendments approved by University Council, December 4, 2017 Name change and new bylaws adopted, April 30, 2020 Purpose of the PAOC The primary role of the KSU Provost's Athletics Oversight Council (PAOC) is to serve as an advisory group to the Provost concerning the intercollegiate athletics program, including providing oversight on strategic and budget planning and implementation, reviewing policies and practices of the department, and sustaining the academic integrity of the university. PAOC also reports, at least annually, to the University Council and to other university shared governance bodies as requested and as schedules permit. Rules of Operation A quorum of KSU PAOC and all its sub-committees shall consist of a simple majority of the voting members. If faculty members are in a minority at any meeting, the majority of faculty members present, as well as a majority of all members present, must support any motion for it. Beyond this provision to assure faculty consent, the Council and its sub-committees shall operate according to Robert’s Rules of Order, unless those rules are suspended by a two-thirds majority vote. Frequency of Meetings The Council will meet at least quarterly; additional meetings may be called by the Chair or by the Provost when necessary. A smoke/tobacco-free campus means that everyone, including guests, is free to travel and visit anywhere on campus without having to avoid potentially health-hazardous situations. How to Quit Current Campus Activities For more information about current campus cessation programs: Resources For Students On Campus KSU students are encouraged to schedule an appointment with the KSU Student Health Services to discuss their options for quitting with a qualified health professional. Schedule an appointment today or request more information by calling (470) 578-6644 or emailing studenthealthsvc@kennesaw.edu . Resources For Staff And Faculty On Campus For KSU employees receiving benefits, the USG provides coverage for all over-the-counter items and prescription smoking cessation products. There is a zero $ co-pay for these smoking cessation products. All over-the-counter smoking cessation products must be physician-prescribed in order to have a zero $ co-pay. For additional information, please visit the USG Tobacco and Smoke Free website . External Resources American Cancer Society’s Guide to Quitting Smoking American Cancer Society Great American Smokeout American Lung Association American Lung Association in Georgia Georgia Tobacco Quit Line Smoke Free Freedom from Smoking Cobb 2020 Tobacco Prevention Smile Ambassadors The Smile Approach: Smile and be friendly when approaching someone on campus smoking or using a tobacco product. Make the assumption that the person does not know about our policy. Inform the person about our policy and resources available on campus for quitting tobacco. Let them know about the policy again. Enforce by asking them to respect our policy and stop smoking or using tobacco on our campus. FAQs What is KSU's smoke-free and tobacco-free policy? KSU joins other University System of Georgia (USG) universities and colleges in creating a Smoke-Free and Tobacco-Free university. The University System of Georgia (USG) Tobacco and Smoke-Free Campus Policy, is effective on October 1, 2014. The proposed KSU Smoke-free and Tobacco-free Policy is currently under review with the University’s shared governance bodies and proposed effective date is October 1, 2014. When will the smoke-free and tobacco-free policy go into effect? October 1, 2014 Why did ksu decide to become a smoke-free and tobacco-free campus? In March 2014, the Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia adopted a tobacco and smoke-free campus policy to make USG 100 percent tobacco-free, effective October 1, 2014. The purpose of the policy is to create a health-supporting community for everyone, tobacco users and nonusers alike. The new policy also supports the right of all people on University System campuses to breathe smoke-free air. The simple reason for our policy is respect for each other and the environment. We hope that smokers who choose to continue smoking will respect our smoke-free environment out of concern for their fellow campus community members. Where can I find ksu's smoke-free and tobacco-free policy? Please visit this link for more information on the KSU policy: https://campus.kennesaw.edu/policies-governance/institutional-policies/ Which smoke-free and tobacco-free products are prohibited from campus? Cigarettes, cigars, pipes, all forms of smokeless tobacco, clove cigarettes and any other smoking devices that use tobacco such as hookahs or simulate the use of tobacco such as electronic cigarettes. How will the policy be enforced? Implementation, including enforcement, of a Smoke-Free and Tobacco-Free campus at KSU is phased as follows: Phase I: Implement Communications and Kick-off Activities: 08/14/2014 – 09/30/2014 Enforcement with a SMILE and no violation letters or tracking Phase II: Implement Communications and Cessation Activities: 10/01/2014 – 01/05/2015 Enforcement with a SMILE and no violation letters or tracking Phase III: Implement Full Enforcement of Violation and Enforcement Procedures: Effective 01/06/2015 01/06/2015: Enforcement with a SMILE for visitors, employees, and students continues. 01/06/2015: Online tool for public and internal (employee/student) reporting. 03/01/2015: Enforcement ticketing begins. ($25.00 ticket per violation from a KSU Police Officer). Fee assessments and collections will be processed similarly to parking tickets, with an equivalent appeal process. For additional information on enforcement procedures, please select "Procedures" on the menu bar of this page. What resources are available to those who are trying to quit smoking? For additional information on resources to quit smoking, select "How to Quit" on the menu bar of this page. How can I appeal a citation? The appeal process for tickets will be equivalent to the process for parking tickets and each appeal will go through a due-process by the respective student and/or faculty, staff, or visitors parking (and other citations) appeal panel(s). The following web pages provide more information on the appeals processes: Student Citation (Parking and Tobacco/Smoke) Appeals Faculty, Staff and Visitors Citations & Appeals Survey Results 2016 Campus Survey Results The survey was released to campus 03/17/2016—05/11/2016. Assign issues to the most appropriate governance body (or bodies), but with the understanding that other bodies may also comment if they wish. b. Assure that the appropriate governance bodies are consulted in the creation of any ad hoc committee or task force addressing issues of general importance, and, if desired, will have the opportunity a nominate members to such ad hoc committees or task forces. c. Assure that the appropriate governance bodies are given the opportunity to consider and offer formal comment on the final reports of any such ad hoc committee or task force. d. Report to the President and other UC members the results of deliberations in various bodies when issues or reports are considered by multiple bodies e. Seek to reconcile conflicting advisory opinions when different bodies have conflicting views. Governing Bodies Faculty Senate The Faculty Senate plays a key role in shaping policies that benefit our university. It fosters faculty involvement in decision-making, addresses issues affecting academic growth, and shares recommendations to enhance the institution. The Senate also serves as a vital communication link between faculty and university leadership, including the President, Provost, and other key stakeholders. It supports our vision by uniting staff, fostering shared governance, and enhancing campus-wide involvement. title: Celebrating Kia Redwine's GSMA Life Membership Award
text: Courses Professional Certificates & Courses Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business and Management Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Construction Fundamentals Culinary Arts Data Science and Analytics Drone Pilot Training Finance Healthcare Marketing Paralegal Patient Care Technology and Cybersecurity Online Courses Intensive English Program 50+ OLLI Program Coming Soon Professional Annual Catalog Summer Camps CPE Expo Advertise With Us Student Resources Career Development Resources Catalogs Financial Assistance Frequently Asked Questions About About CPE Blog Contact Give to CPE Instructor Application Login Login to Register Login to Moodle Search for: Courses Professional Certificates & Courses Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business and Management Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Construction Fundamentals Culinary Arts Data Science and Analytics Drone Pilot Training Finance Healthcare Marketing Paralegal Patient Care Technology and Cybersecurity Online Courses Intensive English Program 50+ OLLI Program Coming Soon Professional Annual Catalog Summer Camps CPE Expo Advertise With Us Student Resources Career Development Resources Catalogs Financial Assistance Frequently Asked Questions About About CPE Blog Contact Give to CPE Instructor Application Login Login to Register Login to Moodle Success Stories Celebrating Kia Redwine’s GSMA Life Membership Award Categories Success Stories Date June 10, 2026 By Marilyn Ogunfowora In April, KSU Community and Professional Education (CPE) Healthcare Program Manager Nikal "Kia" Redwine, MPA, RN, BSN, CMA (AAMA), accepted the Georgia Society of Medical Assistants (GSMA) Life Membership Award at the 67th Annual GSMA Conference. This honor recognizes individuals the GSMA Executive Board and past presidents unanimously agree have demonstrated an exceptional commitment to advancing the medical assisting credential and profession. Several years have passed since the award was last presented, and we are proud that Kia is this year's recipient. On the day of the award ceremony, Kia entered the conference center to find her mentor already on stage, speaking about a member in the room who was "always busy, volunteered across multiple organizations, and was very passionate about the Medical Assisting profession and the professional growth of those around them." Kia had no idea the person being described was her. The nomination had been kept secret. The GSMA leadership had long wanted to present the award but waited for a meaningful milestone: the completion of Kia's Master of Public Administration degree, so her full credentials would be reflected when she received the award. As KSU CPE's Healthcare Program Manager, Kia oversees the University's Medical Assisting (MA) program , preparing students for careers in one of healthcare's fastest-growing fields. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, employment for medical assistants is projected to grow 23% in the state of Georgia through 2033 , faster than the average for all occupations. Demand in Georgia continues to outpace the national average as healthcare systems expand outpatient and ambulatory services. Medical assistants play a vital role in healthcare organizations by providing both clinical and administrative support. Their versatility makes them valuable members of healthcare teams across a variety of settings. KSU's Medical Assisting program prepares students for these opportunities and allows graduates to pursue the national credential that best aligns with their career goals. Upon completion, students may sit for certification exams including the Certified Medical Assistant (CMA, AAMA), Registered Medical Assistant (RMA), Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA), or National Certified Medical Assistant (NCMA). Behind that preparation is a team of experienced healthcare professionals dedicated to student success. As a nationally recognized healthcare leader and recipient of the GSMA Life Membership Award, Kia brings decades of professional experience, industry connections, and a passion for education to KSU CPE's healthcare programs. She supports students with the same dedication she has shown throughout her career and volunteer service. When asked what she hopes students take away from the Medical Assisting program , she shared: "I hope students see that they can have an amazing, rewarding, and productive career. I've been able to volunteer on the local, state, and national levels. I have attended some of the most informative conferences across the state and across the country, where I continue to learn cutting-edge information within the healthcare field from prominent professionals. The medical assisting professionals that I have had the privilege to work with are phenoms in their fields. I hope each student is afforded a career that is as purpose-driven and rewarding as I have had the opportunity to enjoy." For students entering the KSU Medical Assisting program, Kia's career serves as more than a resume of accomplishments. It offers a roadmap for what is possible through dedication, service, and lifelong learning. Her recognition by GSMA reflects the high standard she sets for herself and the example she brings to the program every day. Interested in taking a step forward in your healthcare career? Call (470) 578-6765 to learn more about the KSU CPE Medical Assisting certificate . Categories Professional Education Date August 26, 2026 The job market rewards people who can prove their skills quickly. Professionals are turning to a strategy called credential stacking, also known as stackable credentials or stackable certificates, to build expertise, strengthen their resume, and move up faster. Kennesaw State University’s Community and Professional Education (CPE) offers a range of professional certificates designed to help you build in-demand skills and advance your career. What Does It Mean to Stack Credentials? Credential stacking means earning a series of certificates or certifications over time, with each one adding a new layer of skill on top of the last. Instead of one broad credential, you build a personalized set of qualifications that fit your career goals. Think of it like building a toolbox. Each certificate adds a new tool. Over time, you end up with a well-rounded set of skills that make you more valuable to employers, whether you are starting a new career or advancing in your current one. Stacking can look different depending on your goals. Some professionals stack credentials in the same field to go deeper, such as pairing a foundational certificate with a more advanced specialization. Others stack across fields to become more versatile, such as combining a technical skill with a business or communication skill. Why Stacking Credentials Works It builds skills at your own pace. Certificates are shorter and more focused than a full degree. You can complete one, apply what you learned, and decide what to add next based on where your career is heading. It shows employers a clear growth path. A resume with multiple related certificates tells a hiring manager that you are committed to your field and know how to keep your skills current. It keeps you flexible. The job market changes quickly. Stacking credentials lets you add new, relevant skills without starting over. It can be more affordable and manageable. Certificates are more targeted than degree programs, making it easier to balance learning and a full-time job. Stacking Credentials Through Kennesaw State University’s Community and Professional Education KSU CPE offers certificates across fields including business, technology, healthcare, cybersecurity, culinary arts, and more. Many of these certificates are designed to work well together. One example is the Cybersecurity Specialization Certificate . This program bundles four individual cybersecurity classes covering foundations, network security, incident response, and cybersecurity management. Students can take the classes separately, or register for all four together for a discount, building a layered set of cybersecurity skills. Healthcare is another field where stacking makes sense. A student might start with a Medical Office Assistant Certificate to build front office and administrative skills, then add a Medical Coding Specialist Certificate or an EKG Technician Certificate to expand into clinical or specialized areas. Each certificate builds on the last, creating a broader healthcare skill set. For entrepreneurs, stacking credentials means building the exact mix of skills needed to run a business without hiring out every function. An entrepreneur might stack a Social Media Marketing Certificate to manage their own advertising and social media, then add a Payroll Fundamentals Certificate to confidently handle employee pay and compliance as the business grows. Each added certificate reduces reliance on outside vendors and builds a more self-sufficient, well-rounded business owner. Getting Started The right combination of certificates depends on your career goals. If you are early in your career, stacking can help you build a well-rounded foundation. If you are already established, stacking lets you specialize or branch into a new area without committing to a full degree program. Explore CPE’s full range of certificates at cpe.kennesaw.edu. text: Courses Professional Certificates & Courses Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business and Management Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Construction Fundamentals Culinary Arts Data Science and Analytics Drone Pilot Training Finance Healthcare Marketing Paralegal Patient Care Technology and Cybersecurity Online Courses Intensive English Program 50+ OLLI Program Coming Soon Professional Annual Catalog Summer Camps CPE Expo Advertise With Us Student Resources Career Development Resources Catalogs Financial Assistance Frequently Asked Questions About About CPE Blog Contact Give to CPE Instructor Application Login Login to Register Login to Moodle Search for: Courses Professional Certificates & Courses Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business and Management Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Construction Fundamentals Culinary Arts Data Science and Analytics Drone Pilot Training Finance Healthcare Marketing Paralegal Patient Care Technology and Cybersecurity Online Courses Intensive English Program 50+ OLLI Program Coming Soon Professional Annual Catalog Summer Camps CPE Expo Advertise With Us Student Resources Career Development Resources Catalogs Financial Assistance Frequently Asked Questions About About CPE Blog Contact Give to CPE Instructor Application Login Login to Register Login to Moodle Professional Education Certified Professional Life Coach Training and Career Guide Categories Professional Education Date September 9, 2026 The demand for personal and professional development support continues to grow as individuals seek guidance in navigating career changes, improving relationships, achieving goals, and building more fulfilling lives. This trend is reflected in the personal development market, which Grand View Research estimates will grow from $53.8 billion in 2026 to $79.8 billion by 2033. As a result, life coaching has emerged as a rewarding profession for those who are passionate about helping others unlock their potential. Life coaches provide accountability, encouragement, and structured guidance that can help clients move forward with confidence. Whether working with individuals pursuing career advancement, personal growth, or major life transitions, coaches play an important role in helping clients clarify goals and create actionable plans for success. For those interested in a career focused on empowering others, becoming a professional life coach can offer both meaningful impact and professional opportunities. What Is a Life Coach? A life coach is a professional who helps individuals identify goals, overcome obstacles, and create actionable plans for personal or professional growth. Life coaches provide guidance, accountability, and support as clients work toward meaningful changes in areas such as careers, relationships, confidence, wellness, and life satisfaction. Their role aligns with the broader concept of professional growth, which Indeed defines as applying new experiences and skills to positively impact one’s current situation and future aspirations. Life coaches may help clients with: Career development and transitions Leadership and professional growth Goal setting and achievement Confidence and mindset improvement Work-life balance Personal fulfillment Relationship goals Self-discovery and personal development By helping clients gain clarity and direction, life coaches support lasting positive change and personal success. Why Life Coaching Matters Many people know what they want to achieve but struggle to determine how to get there. Life coaches help bridge the gap between intention and action by providing structure, support, and accountability. As the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) notes, life coaches partner with clients to identify where they are, where they want to be, and the steps needed to bridge that gap. Effective coaching can help clients: Clarify priorities and values Create realistic and measurable goals Develop strategies to overcome obstacles Improve decision-making skills Increase self-awareness Build confidence and resilience Maintain accountability and momentum The growing demand for coaching reflects a broader need for career and personal guidance. According to the BLS, employment of school and career counselors and advisors is projected to grow through 2034, with approximately 31,000 openings projected each year on average. As more individuals invest in personal and professional development, the need for qualified coaching professionals continues to expand. Career Opportunities in Life Coaching Life coaching offers flexibility and a variety of career paths. Some coaches operate independent coaching businesses, while others incorporate coaching skills into existing professions. Life coaches may work with: Individuals seeking personal growth Business professionals and executives Entrepreneurs Students and young professionals Individuals navigating career transitions Clients pursuing work-life balance goals Coaching skills can also complement careers in: Human resources Leadership development Education and training Wellness and health coaching Consulting Employee development programs According to the International Coaching Federation’s 2023 Global Coaching Study, coach practitioners reported an average annual coaching income of approximately $67,800, with earnings often increasing as coaches gain experience, earn credentials, and expand their client base. Income can vary significantly based on specialization, location, and credential level, with many new coaches earning between $30,000 and $50,000 annually. These figures align with Lightcast labor market data for Georgia, which reports an average salary of $39,478 for professionals in the field, reflecting the wide range of earning potential across career stages and coaching niches. Benefits of a Career in Life Coaching For individuals who enjoy helping others succeed, life coaching offers several advantages. Meaningful Work Life coaches have the opportunity to make a positive impact by helping people achieve important personal and professional goals. Flexible Career Options Many coaches work independently, allowing them to create schedules and business models that align with their lifestyle and professional interests. Growing Demand As awareness of coaching continues to increase, more people are seeking qualified professionals who can provide guidance and accountability. Entrepreneurial Opportunities Life coaching can provide a pathway to launching your own business while building a career centered on helping others. Continuous Professional Growth Coaches regularly develop their own communication, leadership, and personal development skills while supporting clients. Build Industry-Relevant Skills With Kennesaw State University The Certified Professional Life Coach (Exam Included) program from Kennesaw State University is designed to help aspiring coaches develop the skills, confidence, and professional knowledge needed to work effectively with clients. The program incorporates coaching concepts modeled after the International Coaching Federation (ICF) Core Competencies and the International Association of Professional Recovery Coaches (IAPRC) Code of Ethics. Key topics include: Coaching fundamentals Coaching ethics and professional responsibility Establishing a coaching mindset Communication strategies for effective coaching Client-centered coaching techniques Coaching assessments and tools Tracking client progress Business planning and practice management Building and maintaining a coaching business Students also complete practical exercises designed to help them develop a unique coaching style and apply coaching principles in real-world scenarios. Earn a Professional Coaching Credential Upon successfully completing the course and passing the final certifying body exam, students earn the Certified Professional Coach (CPC) credential issued by the International Association of Professional Recovery Coaches (IAPRC). This certification demonstrates professional training and can help establish credibility with future clients while supporting your long-term coaching goals. Flexible Online Learning The online program is designed to accommodate busy schedules and offers: 60 course hours Open enrollment Self-paced learning Six months of access to complete coursework Whether you are exploring a new career opportunity, enhancing your professional skill set, or preparing to launch your own coaching practice, flexible online learning allows you to train on your schedule. Start Your Coaching Career Journey If you are passionate about helping others achieve personal and professional success, life coaching may be an excellent career path. Professional training can help you develop the communication skills, coaching techniques, ethical foundations, and business knowledge needed to work effectively with clients and build a successful practice. Ready to take the next step? The Certified Professional Life Coach (Exam Included) program from KSU can help you gain the skills and confidence needed to pursue a rewarding career in coaching. That’s why KSU Community and Professional Education now offers the Paralegal Certificate in a self-paced online asynchronous format, alongside the in-person and online live options already available. All three formats cover the same curriculum and lead to the same certificate. What changes is how and when you learn, so you can choose the path that fits your schedule, your learning style, and your life right now. How Each Format Works If you’ve been considering the Paralegal Certificate but weren’t sure a set class schedule would work for you, the self-paced format was built with you in mind. Here’s a closer look at how the two learning styles compare. In-Person/Online Live In-person and online live classes are led by an instructor and follow a set weekly schedule. You’ll log in or show up at the same time each week, learn alongside classmates, and get real-time feedback as you go. In-person classes are held at the KSU Center located at: 3333 Busbee Drive, #3301 Kennesaw, Georgia 30144 Online Asynchronous The online asynchronous format takes the same course material and puts you in control of the pace. There are no live class times to work around. Instead, you’re given a set start and end date with roughly 90 days of access to complete your coursework on your own schedule. Your instructor is still there to answer questions and provide feedback, just not in a live classroom setting. With three formats to choose from, it helps to picture how each one would actually fit into your week. In-Person If you thrive in a classroom setting and want face-to-face time with your instructor and classmates, in-person classes at the KSU Center offer that structure and community. Online Live If you want the accountability of a set class schedule and real-time instructor interaction but would rather skip the commute, online live classes bring the classroom experience to you. Online Asynchronous If your week doesn’t leave room for a fixed class time, the self-paced online asynchronous format lets you complete coursework whenever it works for you, within your access window. text: Courses Professional Certificates & Courses Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business and Management Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Construction Fundamentals Culinary Arts Data Science and Analytics Drone Pilot Training Finance Healthcare Marketing Paralegal Patient Care Technology and Cybersecurity Online Courses Intensive English Program 50+ OLLI Program Coming Soon Professional Annual Catalog Summer Camps CPE Expo Advertise With Us Student Resources Career Development Resources Catalogs Financial Assistance Frequently Asked Questions About About CPE Blog Contact Give to CPE Instructor Application Login Login to Register Login to Moodle Search for: Courses Professional Certificates & Courses Artificial Intelligence (AI) Business and Management Computer-Aided Design (CAD) Construction Fundamentals Culinary Arts Data Science and Analytics Drone Pilot Training Finance Healthcare Marketing Paralegal Patient Care Technology and Cybersecurity Online Courses Intensive English Program 50+ OLLI Program Coming Soon Professional Annual Catalog Summer Camps CPE Expo Advertise With Us Student Resources Career Development Resources Catalogs Financial Assistance Frequently Asked Questions About About CPE Blog Contact Give to CPE Instructor Application Login Login to Register Login to Moodle Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate Program Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate Train in real kitchens, develop professional culinary skills, and earn a culinary certificate from Kennesaw State University Community and Professional Education See Financial Assistance Options See Culinary Apprenticeship Courses About the Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate If you have a passion for food and hospitality, the Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate can help you build the skills and confidence to pursue opportunities in the culinary industry. Serving the Atlanta metro area, this hands-on culinary training experience prepares students for careers in catering, event production, restaurants, and fine dining environments. Unlike a traditional classroom-only culinary school model, this apprenticeship-style program emphasizes real-world kitchen experience in a professional setting. Students develop practical skills and industry insight while working alongside experienced culinary professionals. Students gain practical training in: Professional cooking techniques Kitchen operations and workflow Food safety and sanitation Menu development Restaurant preparation and service environments Students can select the schedule that works best for them: an accelerated 11-week Fast-Track option or the traditional 22-week program . The curriculum is the same for both pathways. The traditional program meets once a week, while the Fast-Track program meets twice a week. Students exploring culinary school options in the Metro Atlanta area benefit from focused skills training, mentorship, and career-ready preparation designed to meet the needs of today’s hospitality industry. Whether you are beginning your culinary journey or refining your expertise, this program provides structured, hands-on learning to help you move forward with confidence. Course Offerings Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate (Wed) Instructor: Rich Matthews Start: January 14, 2027 Length: 22 Weeks Price: $8,995 Time: 6:00pm - 10:00pm Enroll Now Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate (Fast-Track) (Mon/Thu) Instructor: Rich Matthews Start: June 14, 2027 Length: 11 Weeks Price: $8,995 Time: 6:00pm - 10:00pm Enroll Now Inside the Kitchen What You'll Learn in the Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate Course ServSafe Exam Prep and Intro to Knife Skills Soups (Consommé, broth, and purée), Sauce, and Sandwiches Sauce and Pasta (dry vs. fresh pasta), Gnocchi, and Potatoes Dry Heat Cooking Poultry Fabrication and Moist Heat Cooking (Steamed, Shallow Poach, and Deep Poach). Combination Cooking Methods: Stewing and Braising, Veal Shank Garde Manger Basics Whole Beef Tenderloin, Cookies, Cupcakes, Frosting Pork Loin Roast Beef Strip Loin Roast Menu Planning and Nutrition Seafood: Salmon, Lobster, Clams Cooking Eggs, Hollandaise, Breakfast Meats, Grinding Meats Cost Control Baking and Pastry Basics Lamb Leg Roast Ask Questions and Schedule a Tour of Our Kitchen! Complete the form and a member of our team will connect with you to provide details on schedules, materials, and how to get started. You can also schedule a kitchen tour to see the learning environment firsthand. We’re here to help you take the next step toward your culinary career. First Name* Last Name* Email * Phone # Please enter your questions or comments Tell Me More Meet Chef Rich Chef Rich Matthews is our instructor for the Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate and Culinary Apprenticeship Certificate Fast-Track. Chef Rich brings extensive experience to the programs, including student instruction, restaurant management, and designing cuisine for thousands at major events throughout the country. A career changer himself, Chef Rich is uniquely positioned to mentor students who may be entering the culinary world while juggling other career and life responsibilities. Read the blog: Meet Chef Rich Apprenticeship Sites Your apprenticeships will consist of approximately 12–15 hours per week in rotation between several prestigious venues. * Venues are subject to change based on availability. Atlanta Country Club Ronald McDonald House Atlanta Canoe District Events and Catering KSU’s Commons and Stingers Holbrook Communities Maven Restaurant Group Seed Kitchen & Bar * Venues are subject to change based on availability. Frequently Asked Questions What elevates this certificate above other similar programs? This certificate course is immersive and places our students in working kitchens to enhance their learning. Students are given the opportunity to work in different types of kitchens and experience different styles of food preparation. This system allows students to meet various chefs, cooks, and hospitality leaders to enhance networking. We try to have students experience an industrial, fine dining, senior living, and a catering kitchen. Why do I need health insurance and a background check? Health Insurance is required because of the apprenticeship portion of this program. CPE students will be working as apprentices in live kitchens and injuries are not covered under worker’s compensation. Background checks - All students must successfully complete a background check before being placed into an apprenticeship site. Are there payment options? Yes. This program accepts payment plans, scholarships, MyCAA, educational loans, and other benefits. Contact Enrollment at 470-578-6768 to discuss all of our finance options. Learn more about all of our financial aid options . What other supplies will I need? Each student is required to have a chef’s knife set (not required on the first night of class), black non-skid shoes, and black chef pants, and cover any transportation costs. It is recommended to purchase a food thermometer and a small notebook and pen set. These supplies are at the expense of the student. Chef coats and textbooks are provided. I currently work in a kitchen. Can I use that towards my apprenticeship hours? No, all apprenticeship hours must be completed at one of the pre-approved kitchens that we partner with. All the sites we partner with go through a long process to be approved apprenticeship locations to ensure you have the best educational experience. How does the apprenticeship work? Students will be assigned to various apprenticeship locations throughout the class and will complete a total of 240 apprenticeship hours with a mentor’s guidance at their apprenticeship site. Students must turn in hard copies of their time sheets, signed in ink by their mentor each week. This program is offered through a partnership between Kennesaw State University and Alpha Drones USA and prepares individuals for careers in the rapidly growing field of professional drone operations. Enroll Now Certification Overview The Remote Drone Pilot Training Program combines FAA certification preparation with hands-on flight training using professional-grade drone equipment. Participants gain practical experience designed to prepare them for real commercial applications and operational environments. Phase 0: Information Session & Enrollment Attend a live or virtual Information session Learn program details with live Q&A opportunities Complete enrollment process and secure your place Receive access to preliminary learning materials Phase 1: FAA Remote Pilot Certification Course Comprehensive preparation for the FAA Part 107 Knowledge Exam 4 weeks of training with ten online classroom sessions Self-study computer-based training software (included in program cost) In-depth study of airspace regulations, weather, flight operations, and safety Expert guidance on FAA application procedures after exam completion Phase 2: Flight Training & Qualification Select your preferred sUAS/UAS from Alpha Drones USA fleet options Ground school in-class training sessions (4 hours) Hands-on flight training (10 hours) with professional-grade commercial drones Equipment-specific operational training Learn service-specific applications (agriculture, cinematography, inspections, etc.) Performance evaluation and qualification assessment Course Prerequisites To participate in our program and obtain an FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate, applicants must: Be at least 16 years of age Be able to read, write, and speak the English language Be in a physical and mental condition to safely fly a UAS PPE and Safety Equipment are provided for use during Phase 2, and must be returned. Alpha Drones USA and KSU Drone technology is transforming industries including agriculture, construction, infrastructure inspection, media production, and environmental monitoring, creating growing demand for skilled commercial drone operators. Alpha Drones USA is owned and operated by commercial airline pilots who bring decades of aviation experience to drone operations. Their expertise helps ensure the training reflects the safety standards, operational procedures, and expectations used throughout the aviation industry. Unlike many drone courses that focus only on passing an exam, this program emphasizes hands-on training and practical skills that prepare participants for real commercial drone services. Located in the North Metro Atlanta area, the program provides accessible workforce training for individuals looking to enter the expanding drone industry. ▶ Certification Highlights Hands-on flight training (10 hours) with professional-grade commercial drones Equipment-specific operational training Instruction on service-specific drone applications including agriculture, cinematography, and infrastructure inspections Performance evaluation and qualification assessment Training is designed to build workforce-ready skills that can be applied in commercial drone operations across multiple industries. No previous experience is required, though basic familiarity with drones is helpful. Our program starts with fundamentals and builds to advanced commercial applications. What equipment will I use during training? You’ll train on the same professional equipment used in commercial operations, including agricultural drones, cinematography platforms, and inspection-specific models. The program fee includes: Training Materials FAA exam preparation Hands-on flight instruction Qualification assessment The only additional cost is the FAA testing fee (approximately $175), which is paid directly to the testing center.
