My session ended unexpectedly Next Steps Getting Help R R Installing Packages Table of contents Overview Before You Begin Launch Jupyter Account Mode Root Directory Number of Hours Number of GPUs Number of Cores Email Notification Choose a Kernel Working in Jupyter Using Slurm Commands from a Notebook Reconnect to a Running Session End the Session Browser Notifications Legacy Command-Line Method Troubleshooting My session remains queued Jupyter does not open I closed the Jupyter tab A Slurm command is not found My session ended unexpectedly Next Steps Getting Help Using JupyterLab on the VHPC Overview The recommended way to run JupyterLab on the VHPC is through Open OnDemand. Open OnDemand launches Jupyter as a Slurm job on a VHPC compute node and provides a browser-based connection to the running session. No manual SSH tunneling, port forwarding, or token handling is required. Open OnDemand also provides several preconfigured system Jupyter kernels for common scientific and machine-learning workloads. Note The older ksu-jupyter-lab command-line workflow is still available for users who prefer the legacy SSH -tunneling method. See Using the Legacy ksu-jupyter-lab Workflow . Before You Begin You must be connected to the KSU VPN -Groups service before accessing Open OnDemand. You'll need to connect to our VPN to access the Kennesaw State University VHPC. To begin, open your web browser to vpn-groups.kennesaw.edu , then install the appropriate GlobalProtect VPN client for your computer. Warning If you already have a GlobalProtect VPN client installed, make sure you have a connection for vpn-groups.kennesaw.edu , not vpn.kennesaw.edu . Using the vpn.kennesaw.edu gateway will not allow you to access the VHPC. Open Open OnDemand at: https://ondemand.kennesaw.edu Sign in with your Kennesaw State University NetID. Launch Jupyter From the Open OnDemand navigation bar: Open Interactive Apps . Select Jupyter . The Jupyter launch form allows you to choose how and where the session starts, along with the resources requested from Slurm. Open OnDemand Jupyter launch form. Account Select the Slurm account associated with the project or work being performed. Only accounts available to your VHPC user account should appear. Mode Choose either: JupyterLab Jupyter Notebook JupyterLab is the recommended interface for most users. Root Directory Choose the directory where Jupyter should begin. If no directory is selected, Jupyter starts in your home directory. Use Select Path to choose a different directory. Number of Hours Enter the maximum amount of time the Jupyter session should remain active. The session ends when this time limit is reached, even if Jupyter is still open in your browser. Number of GPUs Enter the number of GPUs required for the session. Use 0 if your work does not require a GPU . GPU requests may wait longer in the queue because GPU resources are more limited. Number of Cores Enter the number of CPU cores required for the session. Request only the resources your workload is expected to use. Email Notification Select I would like to receive an email when the session starts if you want Slurm to notify you when the session begins. After completing the form, select Launch . Open OnDemand submits the request to Slurm and displays the session under My Interactive Sessions . The session initially appears as Queued while it waits for Slurm to assign the requested resources. When the session reaches Running , select Connect to Jupyter . Running and completed Jupyter sessions in My Interactive Sessions. Jupyter opens in a new browser tab. Choose a Kernel After Jupyter opens, select the kernel appropriate for your workload. VHPC provides several preconfigured system kernels for common scientific and machine-learning software stacks. Available kernels may include: BioPython PyTorch SciPy TensorFlow The available kernels may change as software is updated or new environments are added. Working in Jupyter Once connected, you can create or open notebooks using the available kernels. Save notebooks and other important files to persistent VHPC storage, such as: Your home directory Your Work directory Your Staging directory An approved project directory Files stored only in temporary compute-node locations may be removed when the session ends. Using Slurm Commands from a Notebook If you need to run Slurm commands such as squeue , sbatch , sacct , or scontrol from within a Jupyter notebook, you may need to initialize the VHPC Slurm environment first. module load slurm This provides the Slurm command-line tools and the VHPC Slurm configuration needed to communicate with the cluster. Reconnect to a Running Session Closing the Jupyter browser tab does not stop the underlying Slurm job. To reconnect: Return to Open OnDemand. Open My Interactive Sessions . Locate the running Jupyter session. Select Connect to Jupyter . You can reconnect as long as the session is still running and has not reached its requested runtime limit. End the Session When you are finished: Save your work. Exit Jupyter normally when appropriate. Return to My Interactive Sessions . Select Cancel for the running session. Confirm the action. Using Jupyter's own shutdown command may also stop the Jupyter process and cause the Open OnDemand session to complete. After ending the session, verify that its state changes to Completed . Warning Closing only the Jupyter browser tab does not stop the Slurm job. The job may continue running and holding allocated VHPC resources until it is cancelled or reaches its runtime limit. Browser Notifications Open OnDemand can use browser notifications to alert you about interactive-session events, such as when a session is nearing the end of its requested runtime. Your browser must allow notifications from: ondemand.kennesaw.edu If notification permission is blocked, use the browser's site-permission settings to allow it before enabling notifications in Open OnDemand. Legacy Command-Line Method The older ksu-jupyter-lab command remains available for users who prefer to launch Jupyter manually and connect using SSH tunneling. See Using the Legacy ksu-jupyter-lab Workflow . Troubleshooting My session remains queued The requested resources may not yet be available. GPU requests, large memory requests, or requests for many CPU cores may take longer to start. Do not submit duplicate sessions while the original request remains queued. Jupyter does not open Confirm that the session has reached Running and that the Connect to Jupyter button is available. If the session failed, record the session ID, Slurm job ID, and any visible error message before deleting the session card. I closed the Jupyter tab Return to My Interactive Sessions and reconnect. Closing the browser tab does not normally stop the Jupyter session. A Slurm command is not found If commands such as squeue , sbatch , or sacct are unavailable from a notebook, load the VHPC Slurm environment: module load slurm My session ended unexpectedly The session may have: Reached its runtime limit Exceeded its memory allocation Been cancelled Encountered a Jupyter or kernel error Experienced a compute-node or service problem Review the session card and any application output files for additional information. Next Steps Running Interactive Applications Manage files through Open OnDemand Use the web-based shell Using the Legacy ksu-jupyter-lab Workflow Getting Help If a Jupyter session repeatedly fails, cannot be opened, or behaves unexpectedly, contact the Kennesaw State University Service Desk. Method Students Faculty/Staff Web ServiceNow ServiceNow E-Mail studenthelpdesk@kennesaw.edu service@kennesaw.edu Phone 470-578-3555 470-578-6999 When reporting a problem, include: Your NetID The approximate date and time of the problem The Slurm account selected The requested resources The Slurm job ID, when available The interactive session ID, when available Any visible error message Back to top Kennesaw State University - University Information Technology Services | 1000 Chastain Road, Kennesaw, GA 30144 Made with Material for MkDocs

text: Skip to content Kennesaw State University HPC Installing Packages Initializing search Kennesaw State University HPC Home About About Cluster Hardware User / Job Limits Citing the HPC Associations Getting Started Getting Started Account Requests Connecting To The VHPC Connecting To The VHPC Getting Connected VPN Client for Linux Environment Modules Introduction To Linux FAQs Space Management Open OnDemand Open OnDemand Overview Logging In and Navigating Managing Files Using the Web-Based Shell Monitoring and Managing Jobs Running Interactive Applications Using an Interactive Desktop Troubleshooting Software Software Currently Available Software Slurm Slurm Introduction to Slurm Porting PBS Scripts to Slurm Example Scripts Example Scripts Comsol Script Gaussian Script Gurobi Script LAMMPS Script MATLAB Script Rmpi Script Tensorflow Script Training Training Conda Environments Interact Sessions Jupyter Notebooks R R Installing Packages Installing Packages Table of contents Prepare Your Account CRAN: The Comprehensive R Archive Network Installing R Packages via CRAN Installing R Packages without CRAN Acknowledgments Table of contents Prepare Your Account CRAN: The Comprehensive R Archive Network Installing R Packages via CRAN Installing R Packages without CRAN Acknowledgments Installing R Packages Locally Prepare Your Account You need to create a new directory specifically for R package installation. We recommend creating a directory in your home directory called R_libs, like: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ mkdir ~/R_libs CRAN: The Comprehensive R Archive Network CRAN is a network of FTP and web servers around the world that store identical, up-to-date versions of code and documentation for R. It provides access to both the official source code of the R software, and tens of thousands of R packages. Installing R Packages via CRAN Load the appropriate module for the R version you plan to use. In this case, we'll use R/4.3.2-gfbf-2023a . To load R and then run the R console on the VHPC, run the following commands on the login node: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ module load R/4.3.2-gfbf-2023a [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ R Once you're in the R console, you'll need to use the function install.packages to download and install the desired packages. For example, to load the remeta package, you could run the following code: install.packages ( "remeta" , repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org" , lib = "~/R_libs/" ) The first parameter is the package name we want to install, in this case, remeta . The second parameter, repos , is the location we want to download the package from (most everything is downloaded from http://cran.us.r-project.org ). The third parameter is the location of the local library directory you created above. To use the package from R, we use the library function. By default, library only searches the system directories, so we have to specify our local R_libs directory: library ( "remeta" , lib = "~/R_libs/" ) To quit the R console, enter the command q() . Installing R Packages without CRAN If the R packages are unavailable on CRAN or you want to install an older version of the packages, you can download the compressed file to your home directory and install it. In this section, we'll use ggplot2 version 2.0.0 as an example. It is helpful to cd into your new R_libs directory for R package installation and load the R module: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ cd ~/R_libs [ barney@vhpc ~/R_libs ] $ module load R/4.3.2-gfbf-2023a Since we know the URL , the command wget can be used to download the .tar.gz file. You can also copy the compressed file to the directory if you have the file on your local machine or somewhere else on the server. [ barney@vhpc ~/R_libs ] $ wget http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/ggplot2/ggplot2_2.0.0.tar.gz Now, to install the package manually, we need to run the following command: [ barney@vhpc ~/R_libs ] $ R CMD INSTALL --library = ~/R_libs/ ggplot2_2.0.0.tar.gz Open the R console and use the library function to load the newly installed library: library ( "ggplot2" , lib = "~/R_libs/" ) Acknowledgments Content for this document was borrowed from the UCONN web page https://bioinformatics.uconn.edu/resources-and-events/tutorials-2/install-python-r-packages-in-users-home-directory/# . title: Sharing Files On The VHPC Cluster - Kennesaw State University HPC
text: Skip to content Kennesaw State University HPC Sharing Files On The VHPC Cluster Initializing search Kennesaw State University HPC Home About About Cluster Hardware User / Job Limits Citing the HPC Associations Getting Started Getting Started Account Requests Connecting To The VHPC Connecting To The VHPC Getting Connected VPN Client for Linux Environment Modules Introduction To Linux FAQs Space Management Open OnDemand Open OnDemand Overview Logging In and Navigating Managing Files Using the Web-Based Shell Monitoring and Managing Jobs Running Interactive Applications Using an Interactive Desktop Troubleshooting Software Software Currently Available Software Slurm Slurm Introduction to Slurm Porting PBS Scripts to Slurm Example Scripts Example Scripts Comsol Script Gaussian Script Gurobi Script LAMMPS Script MATLAB Script Rmpi Script Tensorflow Script Training Training Conda Environments Interact Sessions Jupyter Notebooks R R Installing Packages Table of contents Introduction Sharing Within A Project Group Granting Write Permission Sharing In Your Personal Directories Using a /tmp Directory References Sharing Files On The VHPC Cluster Work In Progress This article is a work in progress. Chances are, information is either incomplete or just plain missing. Introduction On the VHPC, when you collaborate with other users on a project, you will occasionally wish to share files between project members. There are several ways to do this, often determined by how often and for how long sharing is needed. Sharing Within A Project Group Leveraging a group is a convenient way for users to share files repeatedly over an extended period. To use this method, request a project group and directory by email. Send the following information: A reason for the request A group name that meets the following criteria: It should be short (up to some eight (8) characters), It should be descriptive, and It should be distinctive. The initial user list (later changes are simple to request). Once UITS receives the request, they'll create a new group with your requested members. If you are connected to the VHPC when the group is created, you'll need to log out and log in to join the group. A group directory will be created and can be accessed by one of the following names: /data/share/groupname ~groupname The directory will be mutually readable and writable among group members and will not be accessible by other users. The group will usually be inherited by all files and directories created there. Tip Fortran programs typically cannot interpret the ~groupname shortcut form of the share directory. Give the full path or cd into the directory before running the program, then use relative path names. Granting Write Permission The directories in /data/share are configured such that users of a group can read and write files and directories. However, when you move existing directories and files from somewhere else into the share directory, they may not be writable for the group. To make files writeable by group members [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ chmod g+w file To make a directory and all files thereunder (-R) group writable, which includes the ability to delete files: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ chmod -R g+w dirname Learn more about chmod, chown, and chgrp . Sharing In Your Personal Directories You can give access to some of your directories in your home or scratch directories by opening permissions. This option is typically useful for one-way sharing. For bidirectional sharing, you will need to grant world-write permissions, which is not recommended for files in your own directory space. You may need to open permissions whenever anything is added to the directory. You, as the owner , can arrange this on your own as follows: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ chmod a+x ${ HOME } / [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ mkdir ${ HOME } /share # put new content into your share... [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ chmod -R a+rX ${ HOME } /share This will yield read ("r") and execute ("X") permissions for all users ("a"), meaning users can browse directories, and read and execute already executable files there. You may have to repeat the last step after you add files in the shared directory. Direct your fellow users as follows: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ cd /data/home/userid/share [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ ls [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ cp -p .... The first cd is crucial to have your collaborator step into a sharing directory you designated instead of stepping in from your home directory. Other users are not usually able to simply rummage around your home directory with ls -- it is up to you to show them a specific directory they can browse. Using a /tmp Directory You can drop files into a login node's general-use /tmp directory and set permissions as needed. This way of sharing is: suitable for one-off exchanges, typically fairly loose with permissions, resides on only one host, world-write is not recommended, likely to need chmod whenever more files are added. To share files under /tmp , do the following: [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ mkdir /tmp/foo # put files and directories in your temp directory [ barney@vhpc ~ ] $ chmod -R a+rX /tmp/foo References Adapted from the Argonne National Laboratory Wiki page: https://wiki.anl.gov/cnm/HPC/Sharing_Files Back to top Kennesaw State University - University Information Technology Services | 1000 Chastain Road, Kennesaw, GA 30144 Made with Material for MkDocs

title: Apache Spark - Kennesaw State University HPC
text: Skip to content Kennesaw State University HPC Apache Spark Initializing search Kennesaw State University HPC Home About About Cluster Hardware User / Job Limits Citing the HPC Associations Getting Started Getting Started Account Requests Connecting To The VHPC Connecting To The VHPC Getting Connected VPN Client for Linux Environment Modules Introduction To Linux FAQs Space Management Open OnDemand Open OnDemand Overview Logging In and Navigating Managing Files Using the Web-Based Shell Monitoring and Managing Jobs Running Interactive Applications Using an Interactive Desktop Troubleshooting Software Software Currently Available Software Slurm Slurm Introduction to Slurm Porting PBS Scripts to Slurm Example Scripts Example Scripts Comsol Script Gaussian Script Gurobi Script LAMMPS Script MATLAB Script Rmpi Script Tensorflow Script Training Training Conda Environments Interact Sessions Jupyter Notebooks R R Installing Packages Table of contents What Is Apache Spark Credits Getting Started Creating Your Environment Batch Jobs Interactive Jobs Using Spark In A Jupyter Notebook Apache Spark Work In Progress This article is a work in progress. Chances are, information is either incomplete or just plain missing. What Is Apache Spark Apache Spark is an open-source unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing. Spark provides an interface for programming clusters with implicit data parallelism and fault tolerance. Originally developed at the University of California, Berkeley's AMPLab, the Spark codebase was later donated to the Apache Software Foundation, which has maintained it since. Credits Our implementation of Spark on the Kennesaw State University HPC environment is based on code released by the University of Michigan's Advanced Research Computing (ARC) group through their https://github.com/umich-arc/spark-on-hpc . We reworked the code to use Torque instead of SLURM. Getting Started These instructions provide a step-by-step walkthrough for setting up a stand-alone Spark instance on the KSU HPC environment. The accompanying code is tailored for researchers who are proficient in the technical nuances of sizing a stand-alone Spark instance and need to submit a batch job to Spark. Creating Your Environment Take a look at our Setting Up A Conda Environment page as well as our Using Jupyter Notebooks On The HPC page. Batch Jobs To launch a Spark instance on an HPC cluster, you need to copy the example PBS job script batch-job.sh and customize it with your email address, the resources you require for your Spark job, and the location of your Spark code. Then, you will run the PBS job script with qsub batch-job.sh . As the PBS job runs, it will call the spark-start script which launches a standalone Spark cluster and submits a Spark batch job with spark-submit . When the Spark job finishes, the PBS job will terminate. Spark driver logs are written to the PBS job's output log. batch-job.sh #!/bin/bash #PBS -N spark-cluster #PBS -q batch #PBS -l nodes=2:ppn=24,walltime=60:00 #PBS -m abe #PBS -M barney@kennesaw.edu # These modules are required. You may need to customize the module version # depending on which cluster you are on. module load Spark/3.5.0 Anaconda3/2023.07 OpenJDK # Start the Spark instance. spark-start # Clean up PBS_JOBID to be a bit more useful JOBID = ${ PBS_JOBID %.* } # Source spark-env.sh to get useful env variables. source ${ HOME } /scratch/.spark-local/ ${ JOBID } /spark/conf/spark-env.sh # Customize the executor resources below to match resources requested above # with an allowance for spark driver overhead. Also change the path to your spark job. spark-submit --master ${ SPARK_MASTER_URL } \ --executor-cores 1 \ --executor-memory 5G \ --total-executor-cores 70 \ /data/Apps/spark/spark-on-hpc/examples/pi.py # vim:set tabstop=4 shiftwidth=4 expandtab autoindent: Interactive Jobs To launch a Spark instance on an HPC cluster, you need to copy the example PBS job script interactive-job.sh and customize it with your email address, the resources you require for your Spark job, and the location of your Spark code. Then, you will run the PBS job script with qsub batch-job.sh . As the PBS job runs, it will call the spark-start script which launches a standalone Spark cluster. At this point, you'll need to load whatever modules are required for your tasks. At a minimum, you'll need to do the following to make sure that you can run spark-submit and or pyspark : [ barney@hpcprdssh03 ~ ] $ module load Spark/3.5.0 Anaconda3/2023.07 OpenJDK At this point you can use spark-submit to submit jobs interactively to the cluster. Information on the host and port you'll need to use to connect to the spark cluster instance can be found in a file called spark-cluster-jobid.log in your working directory. When you are finished, you'll need to terminate your job using the qdel command. interactive-job.sh #!/bin/bash #PBS -N spark-cluster #PBS -q batch #PBS -l nodes=2:ppn=24,walltime=60:00 #PBS -m abe #PBS -M barney@kennesaw.edu # Clean up PBS_JOBID to be a bit more useful JOBID = ${ PBS_JOBID %.* } cd ${ PBS_O_WORKDIR } LOGFILE = ${ PBS_O_WORKDIR } /spark-cluster- ${ JOBID } .log touch ${ LOGFILE } # These modules are required. You may need to customize the module version # depending on which cluster you are on. module load Spark/3.5.0 Anaconda3/2023.07 OpenJDK # Start the Spark instance. ( spark-start # Source spark-env.sh to get useful env variables. source ${ HOME } /scratch/.spark-local/ ${ JOBID } /spark/conf/spark-env.sh echo "***** Spark cluster is running. Submit jobs to ${ SPARK_MASTER_URL } . *****" ) | tee ${ LOGFILE } sleep infinity # vim:set tabstop=4 shiftwidth=4 expandtab autoindent: Using Spark In A Jupyter Notebook We've added an option to the ksu-jupyter-notebook script we use to start Jupyter Notebook sessions to also start up a Spark Cluster. You just need to add either -S or --spark to the command, so it looks something like: [ barney@hpcprdssh03 ~ ] $ ksu-jupyter-notebook -l nodes = 1 :ppn = 24 ,walltime = 4 :00:00 --spark Back to top Kennesaw State University - University Information Technology Services | 1000 Chastain Road, Kennesaw, GA 30144 Made with Material for MkDocs

title: VPN Client for Linux - Kennesaw State University HPC
text: Skip to content Kennesaw State University HPC VPN Client for Linux Initializing search Kennesaw State University HPC Home About About Cluster Hardware User / Job Limits Citing the HPC Associations Getting Started Getting Started Account Requests Connecting To The VHPC Connecting To The VHPC Getting Connected VPN Client for Linux VPN Client for Linux Table of contents Installation Troubleshooting Files Environment Modules Introduction To Linux FAQs Space Management Open OnDemand Open OnDemand Overview Logging In and Navigating Managing Files Using the Web-Based Shell Monitoring and Managing Jobs Running Interactive Applications Using an Interactive Desktop Troubleshooting Software Software Currently Available Software Slurm Slurm Introduction to Slurm Porting PBS Scripts to Slurm Example Scripts Example Scripts Comsol Script Gaussian Script Gurobi Script LAMMPS Script MATLAB Script Rmpi Script Tensorflow Script Training Training Conda Environments Interact Sessions Jupyter Notebooks R R Installing Packages Table of contents Installation Troubleshooting Files GlobalProtect VPN Client For Linux Note This information is a courtesy to our users who use the Linux operating system to use the Kennesaw State University VPN to connect to on-campus resources. UITS does not officially support the Linux GlobalProtect clients, so be aware that any support is on a "best-effort" basis. Installation You can install the GlobalProtect app for Linux as either a Graphical ( GUI ) version or a Command Line ( CLI ) version. This documentation will cover using the GUI client, although both are in the archives below. For this example, we'll be using the PanGPLinux-6.3.3-c42.tgz archive. Change the archive name as appropriate for the version that you are installing. Regardless of which version you wish to install, the first steps are the same: Download the GlobalProtect app for Linux from the Files section below. Create a directory to extract the archive to: mkdir GlobalProtect cp PanGPLinux-6.3.3-c42.tgz ./GlobalProtect cd GlobalProtect Extract the archive: tar xvfz PanGPLinux-6.3.3-c42.tgz You should see something like the following as it extracts the files from the archive: x ./ x ./GlobalProtect_deb-6.3.3.1-674.deb x ./GlobalProtect_deb_aarch64-6.3.3.1-674.deb x ./GlobalProtect_deb_arm-6.3.3.1-674.deb x ./GlobalProtect_rpm-6.3.3.1-674.rpm x ./GlobalProtect_rpm_aarch64-6.3.3.1-674.rpm x ./GlobalProtect_rpm_arm-6.3.3.1-674.rpm x ./GlobalProtect_UI_deb-6.3.3.1-674.deb x ./GlobalProtect_UI_rpm-6.3.3.1-674.rpm x ./gp_install.sh x ./gp_uninstall.sh x ./manifest x ./relinfo You will see multiple installation packages for supported operating system versions: DEB for Debian and Ubuntu distributions (and their derivatives). RPM for Centos and Red Hat distributions (and their derivatives). Install the app using the included installer: ./gp_install You can provide the --cli-only flag if you just want to install the command line version. If you are running on a Mac or another ARM platform, you'll need to give it either the --arm or the --aarch64 flag to specify either 32bit or 64bit versions of the architecture. Troubleshooting In newer Linux distributions, a long-outstanding security hole was finally closed. Unfortunately, to allow the VPN client to work, we need to relax the security settings. If you get an error message when trying to connect to the VPN that looks like the following, apply the appropriate fix below: SSL handshake failed Failed to load URL https://vpn-groups.kennesaw.edu/SAML20/SP/ACS. QtNetwork Error 6 Choose your operating system from the choices below: Debian / Ubuntu Fedora / Red Hat / AlmaLinux / Rocky Linux Make a backup of /etc/ssl/openssl.cnf . Edit /etc/ssl/openssl.cnf and find a section named [openssl_init] Add a line to that section, and then create two new sections immediately following that section so that it looks something like this: [openssl_init] providers = provider_sect ssl_conf = ssl_sect [ssl_sect] system_default = system_default_sect [system_default_sect] Options = UnsafeLegacyRenegotiation # List of providers to load Note You may already have the [ssl_sect] and [system_default_sect] sections. If that's the case, just add the Options = UnsafeLegacyRenegotiation line to the [system_default_sect] section. Save the file and exit. Reboot the machine. Make a backup of /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf . Edit /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf and find a section named [crypto_policy] Add a line after the section heading so that it looks like: [ crypto_policy ] Options = UnsafeLegacyRenegotiation .include = /etc/crypto-policies/back-ends/opensslcnf.config Save the file and exit. Reboot the machine. title: Can I submit this paper? (Undergraduate) - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Institutional Repository 10 Answers Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 accessibility 3 article 1 associated files 1 conference 1 embargo 3 faculty 1 journal 2 publication 1 revision 6 submission 2 undergraduate Ask-A-Librarian: Institutional Repository Search Ask Can I submit this paper? (Undergraduate) Is a paper completed during my undergraduate studies eligible for submission to Digital Commons? Answer Papers created as part of an undergraduate course at KSU are eligible to be submitted to the Digital Commons. Check the Student Hub to find an appropriate collection. If there is a collection for the specific course listed, please submit your paper there. If not, choose between the Undergraduate Scholarly Works collection or the Undergraduate Creative Works collection , depending on your paper content. You will have to create an Digital Commons account to submit, but you can use any email to do so. Please add an email address for each author if possible and provide as much detail as possible. When we receive a submission notice, we will reach out to your listed professor and confirm that your paper was done for the listed class and that the paper received at least a B. We don't ask for a specific grade; we just want to ensure that your submission reflects well on you and on KSU. After receiving confirmation from the professor, we will post the paper. title: Can I post related files (sound clips, data sets, etc.) alongside the published article? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Institutional Repository 10 Answers Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 accessibility 3 article 1 associated files 1 conference 1 embargo 3 faculty 1 journal 2 publication 1 revision 6 submission 2 undergraduate Ask-A-Librarian: Institutional Repository Search Ask Can I post related files (sound clips, data sets, etc.) alongside the published article? Answer Yes. The Digital Commons system refers to these supplementary items as Associated Files . You will be prompted to submit Associated Files when you upload your submissions. The name of the files you upload will appear on the web site along with your short description of it. Viewers must have the necessary software to open your files; that is not provided by the Digital Commons system. Please be sure that there are no permissions issues related to use of the associated material. Sometimes, especially with images, you must write a letter seeking permission to use the material before it can be posted. Also note that where possible, items such as images, charts and tables that are referenced in the document (or otherwise an integral part of the document) should be included directly in the article itself and not posted just as associated files. title: I want to publish elsewhere. Do I need to take down my submission? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Institutional Repository 10 Answers Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 accessibility 3 article 1 associated files 1 conference 1 embargo 3 faculty 1 journal 2 publication 1 revision 6 submission 2 undergraduate Ask-A-Librarian: Institutional Repository Search Ask I want to publish elsewhere. Do I need to take down my submission? I previously submitted something (dissertation, thesis, working paper, poster, etc.) to the IR, but I want to publish it elsewhere. What do I need to do? Answer Many publishers do not have any restrictions on early versions that preceded an formal publication, especially if substantial revisions were made. You should check your author agreement with the publisher to confirm that there is no problem with leaving the working paper on the site. The institutional repository would constitute noncommercial use. Assuming the working paper does remain on posted in the repository, it is a good idea to include the citation to the published article on the cover page of the repository working paper. title: How do I renew my books online? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Access Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 27 Campus 32 Circulation 26 Library Facilities Question Q: How do I renew my books online? Answer These instructions work for KSU books only. Books received through GIL Express are not eligible for renewal. Interlibrary Loan (ILL) books must be renewed through your ILLiad account . S ee our renew Interlibrary Loan (ILL) books FAQ for more information. Online renewal process On the library webpage navigate to the University Libraries section on the left side. Select "Borrow & Request." Select "Sign in to my library account." Choose either "Faculty & Students" or "KSU Community Borrowers." KSU students, faculty, and staff can log in using their NetID and password. KSU Community Borrowers should log in using their primary ID number or barcode as their NetID. For more instructions on logging in as a community borrower, see this FAQ for directions . When you have signed in: Click your name in the upper-right corner. Click "My Library Account" in the top menu bar. On your library account page, click "Loans" underneath "My Library Account." Click "Renew" to renew books individually. If you have more than one book checked out, you can also renew all your books at once by clicking "Renew All." Review your new due dates. Please note that your loans and requests are listed under the school that owns the book. If you do not see the book(s) that you have checked out, check the list of schools on the left side of the page. Books cannot be renewed if: KSU books have been previously renewed three (3) times. For GIL books, the limit is two (2) times. Books are already overdue. Books must be renewed on or before their due date. Overdue books must be brought back to the Check Out Desk at either Johnson or Sturgis Library to be renewed. Your record is blocked due to outstanding fines or other obligations. title: I'm not a KSU student, but I live in the area. Can I use the KSU library? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Access Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 27 Campus 32 Circulation 26 Library Facilities Question Q: I'm not a KSU student, but I live in the area. Can I use the KSU library? Answer The following services are available to visiting patrons: Computers WiFi Borrowing Directions & Parking Computers Both Sturgis (Kennesaw) and Johnson (Marietta) libraries have public workstations, labeled as guest computers, that give visiting patrons access to the library catalog and the internet. These computers are available on a first come, first served basis. Guest computers do have webcams. Sturgis Library - the guest computers are in the first row of the main computer lab on the ground floor. Johnson Library - the guest computers are directly across from the checkout desk. More information on guest printing WiFi In your network settings, connect to "KSU Guest." Enter the WPA2 passphrase in the dialog box: Where it says "Enter the network security key" type "kennesaw" with all letters in lower case. You will be directed to the KSU Guest Wi-Fi Portal in your browser. Click "Click here to create a temporary guest account." You will be directed to the Create Account form. Complete the fields, select "I agree to the terms and conditions," and click "Register." You will be redirected back to the KSU Guest WiFi Portal. You will then receive an email and SMS containing your temporary guest credentials with the email and phone number provided. Enter your guest credentials and click "Sign On." You will be required create a new password. Complete the fields and click "Submit." You are now connected to the WiFi network. Note : Guests have limited bandwidth, will only be able to access the Network between 6am and midnight, and are restricted to Internet connectivity through a web browser. Guests will not be able to access the library catalog and digital collections on personal devices. For more information on connecting to the internet with KSU Guest WiFi, visit the UITS service page . Borrowing Residents of Georgia over the age of 18 may request a community borrower's card which provides limited borrowing privileges to the general collection. These privileges do not include remote access to electronic resources or Interlibrary Loan (ILL). Community borrowers may check out up to 5 books at a time for two weeks with 2 two-week renewals allowed. Library equipment reserves (headphones, calculators, laptops, etc.) are not available to guests or community borrowers. Directions & Parking Refer to the Visitor Parking FAQ for information on library parking locations for visitors. For directions to the library and up-to-date information on parking, visit the KSU's Directions & Parking website . Answer Library Fines KSU Libraries no longer charges overdue fines for library materials. Items that are lost or damaged will still be subject to replacement fees. Please return or renew your materials before the due date to avoid lost fees. Additional Information Requested and recalled items cannot be renewed. title: How do I reserve or cancel a study room in the library? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Access Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 27 Campus 32 Circulation 26 Library Facilities Question Q: How do I reserve or cancel a study room in the library? Answer To make a study room reservation Go to the library website. Select "Reserve a Study Room" from the homepage. Select the campus where you’d like to reserve the study room. Select the number of people of your group, date, and the time, then choose Continue. Fill in the information required: your name and KSU email address. Choose Submit My Booking. Effective May 8, 2025, users are required to verify a study room booking using a verification link emailed to them. If a reservation is not verified within 1 hour, it will be automatically cancelled and the room will be made available to others. When it's time for your reservation, stop by the checkout desk to check into your study room. You will be asked to show your Talon Card. Study room information Reservations will be held for 15 minutes. 15 minutes after the reservation starts, the room will be made available for other groups. You can reserve study rooms for up to 2 hours per day, up to 2x per week. Study rooms may be booked up to 1 week in advance. Group study rooms do not have any technology. However, the collaborative study rooms (Designated "Collaborative Technology Group Study") do have monitors to connect personal laptops or devices. Laptops and headphones can be checked out from both campuses checkout desks for in-library use only. ​To cancel a study room reservation The email confirmation you received when you reserved your study room includes a link to cancel your reservation. Click the link and confirm your cancellation. If you cannot find the email or if you have any questions, contact the checkout desk at the library where you reserved your study room: Sturgis Library at Kennesaw Campus: 470-578-6202 Johnson Library at Marietta Campus: 470-578-7276 Links & Files General study room FAQ Opens in new window For more information For more information visit, call, or email: Kennesaw: Sturgis Library checkout desk (Ground floor) 470-578-6202 Marietta: Johnson Library checkout desk (Main floor) 470-578-7276 Email: librarycirculation@kennesaw.edu Last Updated Last Updated Apr 10, 2026 Toggle action bar FAQ Actions Print Tweet Share on Facebook Was this helpful? title: How are books organized in the library? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Collection Development KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 9 Library Collections Question Q: How are books organized in the library? Answer We use the Library of Congress Classification system here at KSU Libraries. While most colleges and universities use this system, you may be used to the Dewey Decimal System from your high school or public library. How this works: Books are classified first by collection type: Reference (Sturgis/Kennesaw: 3rd Floor) General Collection (Sturgis/Kennesaw: 2nd Floor) Teen Literature (Sturgis/Kennesaw: 3rd Floor) Second by subjects with call numbers: Alphabetical: (A-Z) Each letter representing a subject with subcategories Numerical: (1 - 9999) further classifying each subcategory Here is an example: Sturgis General Collection - PS 1861 .C75 Now let's break it down. Sturgis General Collection: The Sturgis Library Floor Map tells me this is on the 2nd floor. PS: Ordered alphabetically by first letter (P) then second letter (PR, PS, PT). 1861: Then by a whole number. . C75: Finally another letter and a decimal number As you can see in the image below, PS 1861 .C75 would be located between PS 1853 .C74 and PS 1868 .N38 . Answer It depends on the type of material and where it is coming from. Physical items like books usually arrive in 7 to 10 business days, but can take up to three weeks. Digital resources like articles or book chapter scans are usually delivered to your KSU email in 1 to 3 business days. title: How do I request a book from another university? - Ask-A-Librarian

Answer If you need a book or other material that the KSU Libraries does not own, you have two options for requesting it: GIL Express or Interlibrary Loan (ILL). Both ILL and GIL Express are free for KSU students, faculty and staff! Interlibrary Loan (ILL) allows KSU faculty, staff, and currently enrolled students to place requests for library materials, including books, articles, and some digital media. The KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team partners with libraries across the country to borrow the requested material. Please note that you may not request required course texts through ILL. For more information about ILL, click here to access the interlibrary loan research guide . GIL Express allows KSU faculty, staff, and currently enrolled students to request books from libraries across the University System of Georgia (USG). GIL Express may only be used for books. For more information about GIL Express, click here to access the GIL Express research guide . For more help For more information visit the Resource Sharing Services Research Guide , or contact the KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team. title: How do I request books through GIL Express? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 19 Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Question Q: How do I request books through GIL Express? Answer GIL Express allows Kennesaw State University students, faculty, and staff to borrow books from other University System of Georgia (USG) libraries. Book requests are placed through the shared USG online catalog and they usually arrive at your selected pickup location in 3-5 business days. You may select either KSU library location as the pickup location for your GIL Express book request. You may also select another USG institution as your pickup location - just be sure to bring your KSU Net ID with you to the library for checkout. For more information, including GIL Express policies, click here to access the GIL Express research guide . How to request a book through GIL Express Open the GIL Universal Catalog from the KSU Libraries website. Click here to access the GIL Catalog. In the library catalog, make sure the drop-down menu to the right of the search bar is on University Systems of Georgia instead of Kennesaw State University. Search for the book title or author of the item you are looking for. Next, click on the item. This will open a new window that will show you the more detailed information. You are looking for the section called "Get It." Under this section, you should see which USG school has the item and if it is available or not. If you aren't already logged into your library account, sign in with your campus ID and password. You can do this by clicking right in the "Get It" section. Click on the university, and you should see a bar prompting you to log in to see more options. Click the arrow to the right of one of the libraries to get more information and to open a request box. Click Request. (If you do not see the Request button, you are probably not signed in.) Select your pick-up location from the drop-down menu and click Request. Check your library account to make sure the request was successful and monitor your request's status. When the status is "On hold," the item is ready to be picked up. You will also receive an email when the request is available for pick up. For more help For more information visit the Resource Sharing Services Research Guide , or contact the KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team. title: What is interlibrary loan (ILL) and how do I use it? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 19 Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Question Q: What is interlibrary loan (ILL) and how do I use it? Answer Interlibrary loan (ILL) is a resource sharing practice between libraries, on behalf of patrons. The KSU Libraries ILL service allows Kennesaw State University faculty, staff, and currently enrolled students to request books, articles, and other materials that are not part of our collections. Once our KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team receives a request, they get to work searching for a library who can provide the materials. ILLiad is the system we use to manage interlibrary loan requests. Click here to access your ILLiad account . First time users should simply log into the location they would like to set as their “home” location with their KSU Net ID and password. ILL service is free to KSU students, faculty, and staff members! However, article requests can get expensive. We may reach out to you about particularly costly article requests to confirm they are truly necessary for your research. How to request materials through ILL Before placing a request, first check whether the item is available in the Library Catalog. Click here to access the catalog . For books, also check whether the item is available through the University System of Georgia Catalog, if they are, you will receive these books faster by placing a GIL Express request. Click here to access the University System of Georgia Catalog . Click here to learn more about GIL Express . To place a request, login to ILLiad with your KSU Net ID and password. Place a separate request for each item by choosing the request type from the New Request menu. You can also place requests using the FindIt@KSU button in most databases and the Request via Interlibrary Loan (ILL) link in the library catalog. When your request arrives, we will email you. Books usually take 7 to 10 days to arrive, and articles usually take 3 to 4 days. However, there are a number of determining factors, such as the item's availability and the distance of the lending library. ILL recommends that patrons allow up to three weeks to receive items. For more help For more information visit the Resource Sharing Services Research Guide , or contact the KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team. Answer It depends. The lending library determines the loan period, conditions of use, and renewals for interlibrary loan (ILL) books and materials. Failure to adhere to those conditions may cause a library to stop lending to the KSU Libraries. Your cooperation is essential to maintaining a good relationship with our lenders. Please note the following regarding loan periods, conditions, and renewals: You cannot request textbooks or required readings for current KSU classes. Average loan periods range from 2 to 4 weeks. Loan periods start the date an item leaves the lending library. The lending library may request the immediate return of an item at any time. Some items cannot be checked out and can only be used in the library. You are responsible for all charges that arise from a failure to return a loan promptly. There is a 7-day window (3 days before your due date through 3 days after your due date) when you may request a renewal. Some items cannot be renewed, including items with "NO RENEWAL" printed on the cover label. The lending library must approve (and may decline) any renewal requests. You may request a renewal for your ILL books, but it is up to the lending library to grant it. To request a renewal for an ILL book: Log into your ILLiad account. Click here to access the log in page. . Click Checked Out Items under the View menu on the left side of the screen. Choose the item you want to renew by clicking the Transaction Number in the first column. Click Renew Request above the Transaction Information box (note: if you are outside of the 7-day window, there will not be a link). For more information, click here to access the ILL research guide. For more help For more information visit the Resource Sharing Services Research Guide , or contact the KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team. title: Can KSU library books be delivered between the two KSU library locations? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 19 Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Question Q: Can KSU library books be delivered between the two KSU library locations? Answer Yes, this service is called Intercampus Book Delivery and is run by the KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team. KSU faculty, staff, and currently enrolled students may request books from either KSU library location. When you place a request for a book, you will select the library location that you would like to pick up the book from (either the Sturgis Library on the Kennesaw campus or the Johnson Library on the Marietta campus). How to place an Intercampus Book Delivery request: From the KSU Libraries website, set the search bar parameter to books and search for the item you’d like to request. Once you find it, click on the title of the book to display more information. In the Get It section, sign into your account with your KSU Net ID and password. Next, click the Request button under Request Options. A box will appear that allows you to select a pickup location from a dropdown menu. The pickup location is the campus library where you want to check out the book. The remaining fields are optional. When you are done, click Send Request. You will receive confirmation that your request was placed. When the book arrives at your preferred library location, you will receive an email notice that your book is ready for pickup at the library checkout desk. If the item is not picked up within ten days, the request will be canceled and the book will be returned to its home campus. Requested items take about 1-3 business days to arrive at the selected campus library. Remember, you can check your library account to see the status of your request at any time. Click here to access your library account . For more help For more information visit the Resource Sharing Services Research Guide , or contact the KSU Libraries Resource Sharing Team. title: How do I schedule a library instruction session for my class? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: How do I schedule a library instruction session for my class? Answer To schedule a library instruction session as a faculty member: From the library homepage , click on "Faculty Resources" on the left side of the page. Under Instructional Support, click the first icon labeled "Request a Librarian for My Class." Fill out the form completely. Be sure to upload either the assignment, course syllabus, and/or event description in the field. Then select one of the following instruction options: Asynchronous Learning Support Materials: Online learning tools designed to be utilized asynchronously Course Integration: Librarian works with instructor and students over 1-2 weeks. Can be guest lecture sessions, asynchronous materials, and one-on-one research consultations Class Guest Lecture: 50-minute guest lecture in person or online Guest Lecture and Micro-Research Consultation Session (2 sessions): Online or in-person guest lecture followed by lead librarian and 1-3 additional librarians assisting students with research in class. Note that ENGL 1101 classes are not eligible for this format. You may request that a synchronous guest lecture be held in your classroom, online, or in the Sturgis Library 101 classroom (seats 40). Please make sure to use our date scheduler for all synchronous requests. You will be contacted via email when your class time is approved and a librarian is assigned. Notes about library instruction sessions: Requests must be made with 14 days advance notice. Faculty must be present for all library instruction classes. If you cannot be present, we will be happy to reschedule your class. We require all requests for synchronous guest lecture sessions be accompanied by a research assignment. General Orientations KSU Libraries welcomes you to embed our first-year orientation modules into your course D2L. Our Orientation Homepage includes instructions for faculty and students that will help you embed these modules into your course. Questions? For questions about our instruction offerings or to change your instruction reservation after you have submitted it, contact Kristina Clement at 470-578-2791 or kcleme19@kennesaw.edu. title: What is a peer-reviewed article, and what is the easiest way to find them? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: What is a peer-reviewed article, and what is the easiest way to find them? Answer What is a peer-reviewed article? Peer review describes the process that an article goes through before it can be published in a scholarly or academic journal. Peer-reviewed articles are also referred to as academic, scholarly, or refereed articles. An academic or expert writes an article whose intended audience is other academics, experts, or students. The article is then submitted for review to the editors of an academic journal Example: Editors of Social Science Quarterly Editors review the article Options: Acceptance, Return with Suggestions, Reject Example: Social Science Quarterly accepts about 15% of submissions. For more information on what it means to be peer-reviewed, check out our Research 101 Guide . This guide can also be found on the library homepage under the Research Guides tab. Finding peer-reviewed articles You can find articles (in magazines, newspapers, scholarly or peer-reviewed journals) from the SuperSearch Tab on the library website . Here you can enter keywords that will search both our KSU library catalog (books, e-books, government documents, films, etc.) and many of the subscription databases all in one search engine. Once you conduct your search, you can limit the results to scholarly or peer-reviewed publications by clicking the button on the left side of the screen that reads "Scholarly (Peer-Reviewed) Journals." What is a scholarly source? Scholarly sources are texts that are written for academics. They are aimed at the following: an audience of academics experts college students They are not intended for a general audience like magazines or newspapers. Scholarly articles are not necessarily peer reviewed, but peer-reviewed articles are always scholarly. What are popular articles? Unlike scholarly articles, popular articles typically are not written or reviewed by experts. They are written by professional writers or journalists for a general audience. They are usually published in magazines or newspapers. title: How do I cite a source? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: How do I cite a source? Answer While the Library will help you research your topic, we aren't able to check your citations. The best place to go for citation help is the KSU Writing Center Many databases, though, have a citation function. When you click on the title of a result, there will often be a link on the right-hand side that reads "Cite." By clicking this link, you will be given a computer-generated citation. Since it is computer-generated, it may not be correct. Always check your citation manual or the KSU Writing Center before using a computer-generated citation in an assignment. Citation Tutorial Handouts Also, you can view the KSU Writing Center's handouts page . This page includes resources on AP, APA, Chicago, IEEE, and MLA. The Sturgis Library also offers many official citation manuals as well as the RefWorks citation management software. Avoiding Plagiarism While working on your paper you will probably use a number of books, articles, journals, reports, lectures, interviews and more. When presenting ideas developed by others, don't forget to provide a reference every time you quote or paraphrase someone else’s ideas, theories or data. You must acknowledge the sources you used in your analysis and research. The source must be referenced whether it is: published or unpublished electronic or hard copy text based or audio/visual If you don't cite the sources properly you might be accused of plagiarism. This is when you copy someone else's ideas or work as if it is yours — whether intentional or unintentional. You can even be accused of plagiarism if you reuse your own previous work without citing it (this is called self-plagiarism). Students that plagiarize anyone's work could face disciplinary action. For more information see the KSU Student Code of Conduct . Links & Files How do I setup a Writing Center appointment? title: Why can't I access Linked Full Text articles in SuperSearch? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: Why can't I access Linked Full Text articles in SuperSearch? Answer Some articles found in SuperSearch only have full text availability through specific databases. Click the "Linked Full Text" link to go directly to the article in another database. Click the "Use Find to Locate Full Text" link to go to a list of the databases that contain the article. If the links in SuperSearch do not take you to the article, you may be able to find the article by locating the journal in which it was published. On the library homepage , click the "SuperSearch" tab and select "Journals" from the dropdown. Either search for the title of the publication or click the "Journals by title" link under the search bar that appears to browse for the title. Click the hyperlink of the journal name to access it electronically. You can search for the title of your article from here. You will be able see the years of publication for the journal that the library has access to next to the journal name. If you are still unable to access an article, the quickest way to get help is to ask the library chat service. If the library does not have access to the journal or article that you're looking for, you can request it through Interlibrary Loan for free. text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: How do I find out how many times an article has been cited? Answer There are a couple places where you can find out how many times an article has been cited by other scholars: Option 1: Scopus Navigate to Scopus , which can be found under "S" in " Find a Database ". From here all you need to do is search for the article in which you are interested. To the right of the search results, you can see the number of times the article has been cited. You can also analyze whole journals by clicking on the "Analyze Journal" link above the search box and searching for a journal. Option 2: Google Scholar Navigate to Google Scholar , which can be found under "G" in " Find a Database ". Here you simply search for the article in which you are interested. Under the link, you can see the number of times the article has been cited. Option 3: Clarivate's Journal Citation Reports Clarivate's Journal Citation Reports (JCR) provides the number of times an articles has been cited, though it focuses on overall journal metrics. Individual article citations can be found using Clarivate's underlying Web of Science database. From Clarivate's Journal Citation Report search the title of the journal that the article is published in. Once the Journal report pulls up, you can find citable items (articles) under Journal Impact Factor contributing items that will list citation count. Please note: these methods may not produce a complete list of all times an article is cited because each searches different databases and sources. title: What is Kanopy and how does it work? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: What is Kanopy and how does it work? Answer What is Kanopy ? Kanopy is a video streaming service providing access to more than 30,000 independent and documentary films ─ titles of unique social and cultural value from The Criterion Collection, The Great Courses, Media Education Foundation, and thousands of independent filmmakers. Can I stream a film in class or at an event? The purchase of a Kanopy film title license (covering 1 to 3 years), includes public performance rights through the platform. The library does not handle any viewing or screening rights/fees. Per KSU Libraries guidelines, KSU Libraries does not purchase audio/visual materials in physical formats. KSU Libraries does not negotiate with vendors for public viewing rights of DVD content, nor does it pay any associated licensing fees. When will KSU purchase the Kanopy license? The library will typically order a film within 1-5 business days if funds are available. The library is limited by yearly budgets that are determined at the beginning and end of the fiscal year. Please submit inquiries to the library purchase request form (or directly through Kanopy’s “Request for Access” form on currently-unavailable videos) and library staff will be in touch. What is the price for a Kanopy license? It typically costs $150 per title to acquire a 1-year Kanopy license, but prices vary. What other streaming databases does KSU subscribe to? In addition to Kanopy , the library system also subscribes to Swank Digital Campus , Digital Theatre+ , Academic Video Online (AVON) , Alexander Street Press , American History in Video , Theatre In Video , and Dance in Video . title: How can I limit my EBSCOhost search results to HTML Full Text articles? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Research and Instructional Services KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 1 Databases 10 Faculty Services 46 Research Question Q: How can I limit my EBSCOhost search results to HTML Full Text articles? Answer Combinations of different field codes and Boolen operators may be use to limit searches to HTML Full Text results only. FM T - Enter FM T in the search box and use a Boolean operator to combine it with your terms to limit results to only HTML Full Text results matching your terms. Example: Enter FM T AND global warming in the search box to retrieve all results pertaining to global warming that include HTML full text. FM C - Enter FM C in the search box and use a Boolean operator to combine it with your terms to limit results to only HTML Full Text results with Graphics matching your terms. Example: Enter FM C AND global warming in the search box to retrieve all results pertaining to global warming that include HTML full text with Graphics. Click here for more information about using Field Codes to limit EBSCOhost search results . title: How do I print as a guest at the library? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Technology KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 22 Computers and Printing 21 Databases 8 Library Catalog Question Q: How do I print as a guest at the library? Answer KSU Libraries provides guest printing services for visitors through the purchase of Guest Printing cards. Both the Sturgis Library in Kennesaw and the Johnson Library in Marietta have guest computers available for printing. Guest Card Overview Before printing, make sure you have purchased a KSU Guest Printing Card and loaded enough money on it to cover your printing costs. You must have a Guest Card to print at the KSU Libraries. Guest cards can be bought at any Kcash machine located on campus. Kcash machines are available near the printers in both the Sturgis Library and the Johnson Library. Purchasing a Guest Card Go to the machine and tap the screen to start using. S elect "Purchase." Accept the Terms and conditions. Choose your payment method: Cash or Card/Mobile Payment. Cash: Follow the on-screen prompts. The screen will display a $2 purchase fee for the Guest Card. Any amount over $2 that you insert will appear under "Card Amount." This is the amount available to use on the card. Insert cash into the machine. ​​​​​ Card/Mobile Payment: A range of amounts starting from $25 will be displayed. If you wish to add an amount less than $25, select "Other Amount" at the bottom of the screen. After entering your desired amount, select "Continue." The screen will show the $2 card fee plus your chosen amount, resulting in a "Grand Total." Select "Pay Now" and follow the on-screen prompts. Insert or tap your payment method on the slider on the far right. If you would like a receipt for this transaction, select "Yes." Otherwise, select "No." Collect your Guest Card. Reloading a Guest Card Go to the machine and select "Reload," then choose "Kcash." Swipe your Guest Card on the swiper located to the immediate right of the touchscreen. Select "Accept." Choose your payment method: Cash or Card/Mobile Payment. Cash: Insert cash into the machine. Card/Mobile Payment: A range of amounts starting from $25 will be displayed. To add an amount less than $25, select "Other Amount" at the bottom of the screen and enter your desired amount before selecting "Continue." Follow the on-screen prompts to complete your transaction. If you would like a receipt, select "Yes." Otherwise, select "No." Printing Overview Guests are permitted to use any printer that has a card slider. In Sturgis Library, there are two guest printers available. One printer is located between the cabinets on the back wall near the stairwell on the ground floor, and the other is situated on the first floor. At Johnson Library, the guest printer is on the right side in the Hive Computer Lab near the stairs. How do I send my document(s) to the printer? Pull up your file on one of the library guest computers. ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ ​​​​​​​ ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ Note: Guests cannot open documents from flash drives or USB drives on these computers. ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ Click the “print” button or hit “Ctrl & P” on the keyboard to pull up the print screen. Make sure your document pulls up correctly on the preview screen. Send your job to either the black and white printer (Guest-Print-BW) or color printer (Guest-Print-Color). After sending the document to print, you will receive a Ricoh Printer Popup window on the computer screen. Enter the KCash Guest Card identification number. This number is located on the back side of your K-Cash Guest Card and starts with a "G". How do I release a print job? Head to the guest printer. You can use any guest machine for black and white printing, but for color printing, make sure to use a color printer. Swipe your K-Cash Guest Card through the card swiper attached to the guest printer. A list of your pending documents will appear. Select the print job(s) you want to release and press the "Print" button. Remove your printed document from the tray. If you encounter any problems, please visit the library checkout desk for assistance. title: How do I access eBooks? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Technology KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 22 Computers and Printing 21 Databases 8 Library Catalog Question Q: How do I access eBooks? Answer You can search for eBooks through the library catalog or by using the SuperSearch tab on the library homepage . Searching for eBooks in the library catalog: 1. At the top of the library homepage, click on the yellow “SuperSearch" dropdown bar and select the "Books & Media" tab. 2. Enter your search terms. You can find search tips here . 3. On the left side of the search results page, click on "Full Access Online." This will filter the results to show only eBooks that match your search terms. 4. Click “Online access” under the book title to view the eBook. 5. Under the heading “View Online – Full text availability,” click the link to the eBook. Note that some books may have more than one link. 6. You may need to log in to access the eBook. If prompted, use your NetID and password to open the book. Searching for eBooks in SuperSearch: 1. At the top of the library homepage, enter your search terms in the SuperSearch bar. 2. On the search results page, locate the “Source type” dropdown menu, Click “More,” and then check the box next to “eBooks.” 3. After clicking “Apply,” SuperSearch will filter the results to show only eBooks that match your search terms. 4. When you find the book you want, click the “Access options” dropdown menu and select a link that will take you to the eBook in our catalog. Additionally, books may also be available as PDFs or EPUBs within SuperSearch. You can click these links to read the books in your browser. If you encounter a message stating that the eBook is in use, it means that the publisher has limited access to one user at a time. Some other services may not have this restriction. If you receive this or a similar message, you can check back later or consider ordering a print copy through GIL Express or Interlibrary Loan. title: How do I add KCash to my Talon Card? - Ask-A-Librarian
text: Skip to Main Content Hours Chat With A Librarian FAQs Request A Research Consultation UNIVERSITY LIBRARIES Kennesaw State University Ask-A-Librarian Technology KSU Libraries FAQs Toggle menu visibility Search All FAQs Search Browse: All Groups Access Services Collection Development Default Institutional Repository Interlibrary Loan and GIL Express Research and Instructional Services Technology University Libraries Internal FAQs Topics 22 Computers and Printing 21 Databases 8 Library Catalog Question Q: How do I add KCash to my Talon Card? Answer KCash Overview KCash is the method used to pay for printing on campus. Campus printers do not accept cash or credit/debit cards directly. To print, you must load money onto your Talon Card, which is called KCash. KCash kiosks are located in each library, making it easy to add funds. Additionally, you can add money online using the KCash account manager . Please note: Funds added online may take up to 30 minutes to appear and become available for use on your Talon Card. Adding money to a Talon Card Go to the KCash machine and tap the screen to start using. Select "Reload." Click “KCash” then tap your Talon Card on the smart card reader. Accept the Terms and conditions. Choose your payment method: Cash or Card/Mobile Payment a) Cash: Insert cash into the machine. The minimum amount for cash deposits is $1.00. b) Card/Mobile Payment: A range of amounts starting from $25 will be displayed. If you wish to add an amount less than $25, select "Other Amount" at the bottom of the screen. For card and mobile payments, the minimum is $5.00. After entering your desired amount, select "Continue." Select "Pay Now" and follow the on-screen prompts. Insert or tap your payment method on the slider on the far right. title: What does it mean when a database says an article is epub ahead of print? - Ask-A-Librarian
