Whether your students are exploring their college options, preparing applications, or searching for scholarships, our dedicated resources make it easy for you to guide them toward success at KSU. This page is designed to provide quick access to admissions information, campus visit opportunities, and essential tools to help your students confidently take the next step toward becoming an Owl. Freshman Resources Dual Enrollment Program Resources Upcoming Events KSU Fast Facts More than 50,000 Students Enrolled R2 Carnegie-Designation, Among Only 8% of Universities in the Nation 24:1 Average Student-to-faculty Ratio in the Classroom 3.5 Average GPA of First-Year Enrolled Students 220+ Degree Programs Conference USA Division I Sports Freshman Resources 3.0 GPA Required for Fall 2027 Admission Beginning Fall 2027, first-year students must meet a minimum GPA of 3.0 to be considered for admission to the University. Visit the Freshman Requirements webpage to learn more. 2.5 GPA Required for Spring and Summer 2027 Admission Students applying for Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 can be admitted under the current GPA requirement of 2.5 or greater. Important Facts Freshman students apply to Kennesaw State on CommonApp . No essay is required, unless students are applying for the Honors College . KSU recalculates GPA based on the 17 required high school courses. The University System of Georgia (USG) high school academic courses required of all first-time students includes: 4 units of English | 4 units of Math | 4 units of Science | 3 units of Social Science | 2 units of same Foreign Language, 2 units of American Sign Language, or 2 units of USG approved Computer Science For additional information on the USG-Freshman Admission Requirements, visit Staying on Course: The Required High School Curriculum . Test scores are required for admission. Minimum test scores are: ACT: 18 – English or Reading and 18 – Math SAT: 500 – Evidence Based Reading and Writing and 490 – Math CLT*: 39 – Verbal and 16 – Math * Accepted beginning Fall 2027 Please note that certain programs may require higher minimum test scores such as Architecture . Students who apply by the priority deadline have early access to Housing and Orientation sign-ups. View Our First-Year Applicant Timeline Additional Information on Freshman Admission Requirements Freshman Application Deadlines Semester Application Opens Application Deadlines Document Deadline Classes Begin Spring 2027 August 1, 2026 November 16, 2026 December 1, 2026 January 11, 2027 Summer 2027 August 1, 2026 May 3, 2027 May 3, 2027 May 17, 2027 Fall 2027 - Priority Deadline* August 1, 2026 November 2, 2026 November 16, 2026 August 23, 2027 Fall 2027 - Regular Deadline August 1, 2026 July 1, 2027 July 1, 2027 August 23, 2027 *Encourage your students to apply by the priority deadline to have early access to Housing and Orientation sign-ups. On-campus housing is not guaranteed for all freshmen and is assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. Dual Enrollment Program Resources Important Facts Dual Enrollment students apply to Kennesaw State on GAFutures . A minimum GPA of 3.0 with qualifying test scores OR a minimum 3.2 GPA (test scores optional) to be admitted. We recalculate GPA based on the 17 required high school courses. The University System of Georgia (USG) high school academic courses required of all first-time students includes: 4 units of English | 4 units of Math | 4 units of Science | 3 units of Social Science | 2 units of same Foreign Language, 2 units of American Sign Language, or 2 units of USG approved Computer Science For additional information on the USG-Freshman Admission Requirements, visit Staying on Course: The Required High School Curriculum . Minimum test scores for 10th graders are: SAT: Composite score of 1200 in a single national test administration ACT: Composite score of 26 in a single national test administration Accuplacer not accepted for 10th graders. Minimum test scores for 11th and 12th graders are: SAT: 480 – Reading and Writing; 440 – Math ACT: 17 – English or Reading; 17 – Math CLT: 36 Verbal Reasoning + Grammar/Writing and 133 Quantitative Reasoning Accuplacer: 237 – Reading; 4 – WritePlacer; 258 – Quantitative Reasoning, Algebra & Statistics Kennesaw State University offers a seamless admissions process for students who would like to transition from a dual enrollment to a degree-seeking student. Additional Information on Dual Enrollment Admission Requirements Dual Enrollment Program Application Deadlines Semester Application Opens Application Deadlines Document Received Deadline Classes Begin Spring 2027 April 1, 2026 October 30, 2026 November 13, 2026 January 11, 2027 Summer 2027 August 1, 2026 April 2, 2027 April 16, 2027 May 17, 2027 Fall 2027 August 1, 2026 April 2, 2027 April 16, 2027 August 23, 2027 KSU is Test Optional for Dual-Enrolled Students However, students are highly encouraged to take the SAT or ACT in preparation for their freshman admissions. Join our Counselor Mailing List Upcoming Events Kennesaw State hosts an annual counselor retreat as well as other events you are welcome to be a part of. To stay up to date on the latest, join our counselor email list. High School Group Tours Between our two campuses, we offer more than 190 degree programs. Tours are offered on both campuses based on the desired major. Special Events for Prospective & Admitted Students KSU offers many special events throughout the year for future students, from spotlight tours for specific areas of study to accepted student events. Open House at KSU Students learn more about their major, admission requirements, and financial aid while also hearing from current KSU students. Additional Resources KSU Admissions Viewbook Check out the Admissions Viewbook to learn more about what KSU has to offer! Bachelor’s Degrees at KSU Easily search the available degree programs at KSU with a click. KSU Cost Calculator Students can answer four easy questions and get an estimated cost of attendance for one year (15 credit hours for fall/spring) at KSU. Journey Honors College at KSU Encourage your high-achieving students to explore the benefits and opportunities of the Honors College. Support for Students Who Have Experienced Homelessness or Foster Care KSU’s ASCEND program provides support to these students, ranging from case management to a living learning community in on-campus housing. Application Fee Waivers Students can complete the application fee waiver within the CommonApp and provide your information for us to verify. Alternative Admissions Pathways Kennesaw State University and higher education institutions across the state of Georgia are joining forces to provide coordinated transfer processes and enriching educational experiences through the LINK Program, paving the way for student success. Prior Learning Assessment Opportunities Students can earn college credit through examination including AP and IB in high school and CLEP and DSST during their studies at KSU. Financial Aid and Scholarships The Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid aims to connect incoming and currently enrolled students with opportunities to help fund their education. Still have questions? Connect with your Admissions Recruiter ! We know how stressful enrolling in college can be, and we want to make the process as simple as possible. To help you navigate, use the buttons below to jump directly to the section that applies to you: Freshman & Transfer Freshman Transfer Student International Student Nontraditional Student Readmitted Student Dual Enrollment Student If you have any questions about the enrollment process, contact the Admissions Office to speak with a college admissions counselor. Freshman and Transfer Freshman Next Steps: Follow these steps to ensure you’re ready for Orientation and the first day of class. As soon as Possible: 1) Reply to your Admissions Offer (Accepting your Admission to KSU) Let us know if you intend to come to KSU so we can plan your arrival to The Nest Complete Intent to Enroll 2) File your FAFSA Submit the FAFSA any time after it opens on October 1 . FAFSA is required to determine if you are eligible for any federal financial aid and to access loans. File your FAFSA 3) Complete your profile on Scholarship Universe KSU’s one-stop shop for available scholarships, Scholarship Universe, pairs you with potential scholarships that match the academic achievements and information outlined in your profile. KSU scholarships open annually on November 1 , and external scholarships are open throughout the year. Sign up for Scholarship Universe 4) Apply for Housing Applications for on-campus housing open on December 1 , and you are encouraged to apply early. On-campus housing is limited and assigned on a first-come, first-served basis. On-Campus Housing Information Off-Campus Housing Information 5) Sign up for Mandatory New Student Orientation Orientation allows you to connect with peers, complete class advising and course registration, and learn about resources. Early sign-up is encouraged for you and your parents/guests. Orientation Information 6) Join our ZeeMee Community A social platform for prospective and current college students, ZeeMee helps to connect you with peers, find a roommate, and learn about campus life! Join ZeeMee Before Mandatory Orientation: 1) Schedule an Appointment with Your Academic Advisor Approximately two weeks prior to your orientation date, schedule an appointment to meet with your academic advisor to go over any dual enrollment, AP, or IB credit that you have received or review coursework for your first semester at KSU. Find Your Academic Advisor 2) Check for Holds that will Prevent Registration at Orientation Unresolved holds will prevent your registration for classes. Admission is pending until your final official transcripts are received. Before Orientation, check for holds or missing transcripts in Owl Express. Check Holds 3) Complete Legal Name/Lawful Presence Verification In accordance with the University System of Georgia's procedure for consistent identity management and to reduce the risk of fraud by impersonation, all new students are required to verify their legal name in our system. For students who are Georgia residents or are receiving an out-of-state tuition waiver, the same document is used to satisfy Lawful Presence. Submit Legal Name Verification 4) Submit Final High School and/or College Transcripts Work with your high school and/or Dual Enrollment institution to send us your official* transcript(s) documenting all coursework taken during your high school career. *Your official transcript(s) must come from your high school or the institution you were enrolled for Dual Enrollment. If you are a homeschool student, please complete the Homeschool Portfolio. 5) Submit Official AP/IB Scores KSU cannot award credit for your AP/IB coursework until official scores are submitted by the respective testing organization. If you have pending test scores, be sure to talk with your academic advisor and submit the scores as soon as they are available. More Information on AP/IB Before Classes Start: 1) Submit Immunization Records KSU requires all students to provide proof of immunization of specific vaccines verified by their health care provider. Documents can be submitted online through the Immunization portal , mailed, or hand-delivered to the Enrollment Customer Service Center (Marietta Campus) or the Office of the Registrar (Kennesaw Campus). Submit Immunization Records 2) Review your Financial Aid Package *If applicable You can view your financial aid package in Owl Express under the Financial Aid tab. It shows your awarded federal financial aid, scholarships, loans, grants, and how they apply to your bill. Review Your Aid Package 3) Review your Bill via the Bursar’s Office The Bursar's Office is where you can find information on tuition and payment options. You are encouraged to explore your options well in advance of the first day of classes. You can view the balance owed on Owl Express. Bursar’s Office 4) Explore Campus Services Find out about dining, meal plans, parking, card services, postal services and more. To be considered for the Flight to Excellence Scholarship, students must first be accepted to Kennesaw State University. Students selected for the scholarship will be automatically notified through their KSU student email address. No separate scholarship application is required. Recipients who receive a waiver qualify for in-state tuition but are responsible for all applicable fees. There are a limited number of waivers available and the application for a waiver is competitive. Recipients of the Out-of-State Waiver and Scholarship must maintain satisfactory academic performance which will be reviewed each semester. The waiver is valid up to eight semesters and will be renewed each semester for students who have maintained a 2.5 grade point average and have earned 12 semester hours each academic term (fall and spring). Out-of-State Eligibility Application Deadlines: Submit your admission application and supporting documents by the dates below for priority consideration for the Flight to Excellence Scholarship for out-of-state students. Spring 2027 - November 16, 2026 Fall 2027 Freshmen: November 2, 2026 Transfers: April 1, 2026 For any questions, please contact Office of Undergraduate Admission at KSUadmit@kennesaw.edu . Out-of-State Eligibility: First-Time Freshmen Be a domestic out-of-state or international student Have a High School GPA of 3.5 as determined by KSU. Must be on track to complete Required High School Curriculum. Meet the following test score minimums: 1050 SAT, 20 composite ACT score, or 68 CLT score. Home Educated applicants will be considered based on meeting the SAT/ACT standard only. Please Note: Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee a waiver. Preference will be given to students who have exceeded GPA requirements and demonstrate superior academic potential. Transfer Students Be a domestic out-of-state or international student Have earned at least 30 semester hours or 50 quarter hours that will transfer to KSU. Have a transfer GPA of 3.3 in their college coursework. The cumulative transfer GPA for admission eligibility is calculated on all academic work attempted from all institutions attended. If a course is repeated, then both grades are calculated. Please Note: Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee a waiver. Preference will be given to students who have exceeded GPA requirements and demonstrate superior academic potential. Adult Learning is the voice that speaks for campus-wide adult learning programs, much as the academic departments speak for their majors. The primary goal of the Adult Learning is to develop and maintain a unified, integrated, and effective adult learning and prior learning assessment program. The committee is advisory in nature and submits proposals to the Office of the Provost and Senior Vice President of Academic Affairs. Coming Back to School as an Adult? Have you ever considered attending college later in life, but find that the cost is too high and the process too difficult? Are you concerned about balancing your work, family and personal life while taking college courses? We’ve got you covered! Whether you are looking to advance your career or achieve your lifelong learning goals, you have come to the right place. Kennesaw State University offers degree completion and credit for prior learning programs, including accelerated courses and 100% online degrees. Adult learners at KSU can take advantage of affordable tuition, multiple financial aid options, as well as scholarships and federal grants. Our tight-knit community of working professionals and lifelong academics are always here to support you in your educational journey. The support services and campus resources will help you reach your goals while walking you through every step of the process. Learn more about getting credit for prior learning. CPL is a process through which students identify areas of relevant learning from their experiences or portfolio and submit documentation for credit. Learn more about CPL. However, many scholarships and financial aid opportunities are available to non-traditional students to assist them in achieving their educational aspirations. Check out these scholarship options available for college-bound individuals who do not fit the classic student mold. Walmart Associate Scholarship Osher Reentry Scholarship Program Georgia HERO Scholarship Program Grants for Adult Learners If you’re going back to school as an adult, you should first complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). The U.S. federal government and universities need to review your FAFSA to give you access to federal grants, loans and work-study programs. There are no age restrictions on federal aid — an adult learner completes the same FAFSA as a high school senior. Even if you don’t qualify for grants, you should still fill out the FAFSA to access federal and state-funded student loans. These loans usually have lower interest rates with more accommodating repayment terms than private student loans, helping you save more money. Campus Bookstore The KSU Bookstore , located on both the Kennesaw and Marietta campus, provides alumni a 10% discount on most KSU branded clothing and gift purchases (the discount is not available for online purchases at this time). Campus Parking Alumni can pay for hourly or daily parking in the Visitor parking lots. Alternatively, alumni frequently on campus can purchase an Alumni parking permit, which costs $23 per month and is valid in any Visitor parking area on the Kennesaw or Marietta Campus. Please note, alumni permits are not available to students actively registered for classes at KSU. Visit the Visitor Resources page to learn more. Professional Education KSU alumni (graduates) receive a 10% discount on all classes with a maximum discount of $500 per Professional Education class . There is no limit to the number of courses KSU Alumni may take. Classes delivered online are not eligible for this discount. UGA - Small Business Development Center (UGA - SBDC) The UGA – SBDC services are offered through KSU’s Coles College of Business. The center’s mission is to help grow Georgia’s businesses and educate business owners through a no-cost, confidential business consulting services paired with classes and training programs for established business owners and entrepreneurs starting a business. For more information or to schedule an appointment, call (470) 578-6450 or email kennesaw@georgiasbdc.org . Zuckerman Museum of Art The Bernard A. Zuckerman Museum of Art is free and open to alumni. The museum presents significant works from the University’s permanent art collection and regularly exhibits contemporary works of various media by local and nationally-recognized artists. Parking is $3/hour ($12 maximum), and the first 30 minutes are free. Upon your graduation from KSU, you are automatically a member of the KSU Alumni Association. How do I update my contact and employment info? A network is only as strong as those who participate in it. Update your profile now: Update Your Information How do I get a membership to the Rec Center? As a KSU Owl Alum, you can purchase an alumni membership to use the Dr. Betty L. Siegel Student Recreation and Activities Center (Kennesaw campus) and/or the Recreation and Wellness Center (Marietta campus). To enroll, visit one of our recreation centers or purchase online. Sign Up Today Where can I get career help and advice? KSU and SPSU alumni have lifetime access to Alumni Career Services . Are there discounts if I enroll in a Professional Education class? KSU alumni (graduates) receive a 10% discount on all classes with a maximum of $500 per course. There is no limit to the number of classes a KSU Alumni may take. The discount can only be applied to the KSU graduate and is not transferable to any other family member. Classes delivered online are not eligible for this discount. To learn more about what courses are offered, click the button below. Learn More How long do I have my NetID? You have access to your NetID for up to 1 year (3 consecutive semesters of not attending KSU classes). For more information, please contact University Information Technology Services (UITS) at (470) 578-3555. How long do I have access to my KSU email? You will have access to your KSU email for up to 1 year after graduation. For more information, please contact University Information Technology Services (UITS) at (470) 578-3555. How do I become more involved? There are a number of ways for you to get and stay connected with your alma mater and fellow alumni. You can select from opportunities with our affinity groups, participate in volunteer opportunities, attend alumni events and much more. Get Involved How do I get a replacement diploma? To get a replacement diploma, complete the Diploma Replacement Request Form . How do I get a copy of my transcripts? To get a copy of your transcripts, visit the Office of the Registrar's website , and follow the instructions per your graduation date. Where may I park when visiting campus? Kennesaw State University encourages alumni to remain active within the KSU community. Alumni can pay for hourly or daily parking in the Visitor parking lots. Alternatively, alumni frequently on campus can purchase an Alumni parking permit, which costs $23 per month and is valid in any Visitor parking area on the Kennesaw or Marietta Campus. Please note, alumni permits are not available to students actively registered for classes at KSU. Learn More How can I get the Wingspan alumni e-newsletter? Just update your information with us and we will be sure to get you on the e-newsletter list. Update Your Information What are the responsibilities of the Alumni Association Board of Directors? The KSU Alumni Association Board provides leadership for the Alumni Association and acts as a liaison between the University and you, our alumni. Check out their programs and members here . These awards include: Distinguished Alumni Award Alumni Service Award Young Alumni Service Award Alumni Community Impact Award SPSU Legacy Award You can learn more about the criteria for each award using the drop-downs below. Alumni Awards Criteria Distinguished Alumni Award The KSU Distinguished Alumni Award is the most prestigious and highest honor given by the KSU Alumni Association. It honors an alumnus/a who brings recognition and pride back to the University through excellent leadership and service to the University, the community, and his or her profession. Alumni Service Award The KSU Alumni Service Award goes to an alumnus/a who demonstrates exceptional service to KSU by volunteering their time and expertise. Young Alumni Service Award The KSU Young Alumni Service Award recognizes an alumnus/a who graduated within the last ten years who demonstrates exceptional service to KSU by volunteering their time and expertise. SPSU Legacy Award The SPSU Legacy Award is awarded to an alumnus/a who illustrates commitment to the STEM field and continued service to the University. The SPSU legacy lives on within the foundation of KSU, inspiring generations of STEM students to come. Alumni Community Impact Award The KSU Alumni Community Impact Award is presented to an alumnus/a who has shown remarkable achievements in local, national, and/or global service. Eligibility Requirements Nominees must have earned a degree from Kennesaw State University or Southern Polytechnic State University (or any preceding iteration of either institution). This does not include certificate programs. Current KSU faculty and staff who are also alumni are eligible. Current members of KSU Alumni Board of Directors and their immediate family members are not eligible to receive an award while serving. Members of the Kennesaw State University Board of Trustees are not eligible to receive an award while serving. Members of Public Office (appointed or elected) are not eligible to receive an Alumni Award during their term. Once the individual no longer holds an elected or appointed position in political office, they are eligible. Past Alumni Award honorees are only eligible in categories other than the category in which they have already been given an award. In addition, their subsequent achievements must be substantially different from those for which their first award was given. Alumni who have received an Honorary Degree from Kennesaw State University are not eligible. * The Kennesaw State University Alumni Association reserves the right to verify that the nominees meet the criteria and reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to reject any nominee for any reason. 2026 Alumni Award Honorees Distinguished Alumni Award Alex Kendrick '94 Alumni Service Award Patrick H. Kennesaw State has achieved a “Gold Standard” of success. KSU football is the winningest startup program in college football history along with four conference titles and four NCAA Playoff appearances. Most recently, KSU won the 2025 CUSA championship and earned its first bowl game at the Myrtle Beach Bowl. In 2023, men’s basketball won its first ASUN championship and showcased its talents nationwide in March Madness. They repeated the honor by winning the 2026 CUSA championship and making their second appearance in the Big Dance! KSU has won two individual national championships with Daniel Haugh’s 2019 hammer throw and Isaiah Rogers’ 2023 weight throw gold medals. In total, KSU has won 66 conference crowns at the Division 1 level, and its competition cheerleading squad has garnered eight national championships. Before you get started, keep up-to-date below with our newsletter! stay updated with our newsletter Men's Sports Baseball Basketball Cross Country Football Golf Tennis Track & Field Women's Sports Basketball Cross Country Golf Lacrosse Soccer Softball Tennis Track & Field Volleyball Welcome Message from Milton Overton, Athletics Director Owl Nation, There has never been a better time to be a Kennesaw State Owl! We are thankful for what we have achieved together in our brief but mighty history. We have a powerful combination of our present success, historical achievements, and bright future. While college sports shifts to a new model, rest assured that our core values and primary mission to graduate productive student-athletes is stronger than ever. I am proud to say that with the support of Kennesaw State President Kathy Schwaig, we have reached new heights, and we have a path to soar higher. I appreciate you taking the time to read our annual report, where you will be reminded that together we raised trophies, excelled in the classroom at a conference and on a national level, gave back to our community, and did our best to better support the holistic well-being of our Owls. It is important to take a few moments to pause and reflect on what has transpired through our journey. I cannot thank you enough for your support of our fantastic university and its athletic programs, and I look forward to even greater moments ahead for Kennesaw State. As we look to the future, we will be guided by our strategic roadmap to build champions in the classroom and provide the best college experience for our student-athletes that promotes comprehensive success in life. Our focus is on fungi and the practical application of knowledge to solve problems. Our research spans a wide range of areas, including fungal pathogenesis and disease treatment, industrially-relevant chemical production, controlled environment agriculture, and culinary and medicinal mushroom cultivation, among others. We have a number of different projects supported by graduate and undergraduate students, as well as the VIP Team MycoSolutions – Solving Problems with Fungi. To learn more about our work, check out the Research and Publications pages. Visit Us The Bioinnovation Lab is located in room 2915 on the 2nd floor of the Prillaman Health Sciences building. This site is where we've been conducting treatment trials with volatile organic compounds in an attempt to suppress a deadly fungal disease among bats, known as white nose syndrome (WNS). We were joined by several journalists and photographers, for what we hoped would be positive results following our seconds year of treatments. Read the articles written about this day, the history of our research with WNS, and our future plans and aspirations, below. Fighting to Save America’s Bats is and op-ed written by Michael Ray Taylor for The New York Times. Fighting Extinction was written by Tiffany Capuano for Kennesaw State University's news, with a beautiful video giving a first-hand look at what it's like conducting bat research (including culvert surveys ) and treatments for WNS. Mushroom Cultivation Additionally, Georgia Magazine 's April issue included an article about KSU's farm by Jane F. Garvey, which included Dr. Kyle Gabriel's work with developing the capacity to cultivate edible mushrooms . Among them, is the Georgia chapter of The Wildlife Society dedicated to wildlife conservation, education, and research in the state. This chapter meets annually to allow students an opportunity to present ongoing research and state managers to discuss and coordinate efforts. The 2018 Annual meeting of the Georgia Chapter of The Wildlife Society was held in Tifton, GA on September 6th and 7th, 2018. Graduate and undergraduate students representing six universities across Georgia presented their research in the form of an oral presentation or a poster. Three students represented Kennesaw State University at this meeting, two from the BioInnovation Laboratory. Graduate student Kelly Lutsch gave an oral presentation detailing her research conducting culvert surveys for bats in coastal Georgia and collecting swabs to determine the presence of Pseudogymnoascus destructans , the fungal pathogen responsible for a deadly mycosis of bats known as white-nose syndrome . Undergraduate student Ashley McDonald presented a poster discussing her research investigating the in vitro inhibitory properties of various volatile organic compounds on P. destructans . Kelly was awarded second place in the oral presentation category and Ashley was awarded first place in the poster presentation category. Kennesaw State University representatives. From left: Kelly Lutsch, Ashley McDonald, and Miranda Gulsby. Poster and oral presentation winners. From left: Kassandra Arts, Ashley McDonald, Sarah Martin, Kelly Lutsch, and Angela Burrow. Kennesaw State University undergraduate student, Ashley McDonald, next to her poster. Our commitment to understanding fermentation processes and their effects on flavor and quality drives our studies in brewing, while our investigations into white-nose syndrome aim to protect vulnerable bat populations from a deadly fungal threat. Additionally, we are pioneering sustainable mushroom cultivation methods, utilizing advanced technologies to enhance food production and harness the unique properties of fungi for various applications. Learn more about our innovative research projects happening to further our growth and sustainability as a community! Brewing Science The Bioinnovation Laboratory is dedicated to advancing the field of brewing science by delving into the fermentation process and its influence on beer flavor and quality. Through innovative techniques like electron microscopy, the lab examines how materials, such as wooden barrels, interact with beer during fermentation. This research not only aims to refine brewing practices but also fosters creativity and collaboration within the brewing industry and the local community. This particular research focuses on the biological and chemical analyses for industrial beverage fermentation processes. Read More White-Nose Syndrome Pseudogymnoascus destructans (previously Geomyces destructans ) is a newly-discovered fungal pathogen responsible for white-nose syndrome in bats. Since its discovery in North America in 2006, it has spread throughout the eastern United States and Canada. White-nose syndrome (WNS) is a lethal fungal disease caused by *Pseudogymnoascus destructans*, threatening bat populations in North America. Characterized by white fungal growth on their skin, WNS primarily impacts bats during hibernation, resulting in high mortality rates. We are investigating the disease's mechanisms and collaborating to develop effective treatment and prevention strategies, focusing on environmentally safe solutions to address the unique challenges posed by bats' natural habitats. Read More Mushroom Cultivation Utilization of mushrooms and fungi in novel ways, including development of their culinary, biochemical, and structural properties. Mushroom cultivation offers a sustainable way to enhance food production, leveraging the unique capabilities of fungi to thrive on various substrates, including agricultural waste. The Bioinnovation Laboratory is researching how to develop efficient, low-footprint mushroom growing facilities using modified shipping containers. This initiative focuses on climate adaptability, automated environmental control, and the potential for fungi in bioconversion, with the newly formed VIP Team MycoSolutions exploring innovative applications in food production and beyond. Characterized by white mycelial growth on the bats' skin, WNS leads to high mortality rates during hibernation when bats are most vulnerable. The Bioinnovation Laboratory is researching the disease's mechanisms and developing treatment and prevention strategies in collaboration with institutions like Zoo Atlanta to help protect bat populations from extinction. Pseudogymnoascus destructans spores and mycelia (© Kyle Gabriel and Dr. Robert Simmons, Georgia State University) Pseudogymnoascus Destructans Pseudogymnoascus destructans is a psychrophilic fungus responsible for white-nose syndrome in bats. Named for the white mycelial growth on the skin of the muzzle, ears, and wings, WNS usually presents itself during winter, while bats are in a state of hibernation. During this torpor, the suppression of metabolic activity of the bat reduces energy expenditure, enabling survival through the winter until environmental conditions improve. Along with this comes reduced immune system function, leaving bats unable to adequately fight off this infection. In addition to physical damage by the fungus from colonization of tissue, the infection also affects water retention, provokes more frequent arousal, and increases energy use that prematurely depletes fat reserves, leading to high mortality among the infected. Photo by John Neville A pseudo-colored scanning electron micrograph of Pseudogymnoascus destructans grown on minimal media for 30 days. The area of interest is the joined conidia, which is an example of the micro-conidiation cycle that P. destructans undergoes (© John Neville, Georgia State University) Photo by John Neville Pseudogymnoascus destructans mycelia and conidia (© John Neville, Georgia State University) Photo by John Neville A 3D projection of Pseudogymnoascus destructans mycelia and conidia from confocal imaging (© John Neville, Georgia State University) P. destructans spores can remain viable in host-free environments for extended periods of time. Repopulating a WNS-affected cave with bats has the potential to facilitate infection of the new colony. In addition, the physical inaccessibility of many parts of caves where bats hibernate make developing disease management solutions a significant challenge. Our research focus is to develop methods for disease treatment and prevention that are safe for both bats and the environment, and can overcome the difficulties of working in karst environments. Fighting Extinction (2018) Developing disease management strategies for bat white-nose syndrome, produced in 2016 and funded by Williams/Transcontinental Gas Pipeline Company. Special Bacteria Helps Heal Sick Bats was produced in 2015 by National Geographic . It documents the first successful treatment of white-nose syndrome, by our research group and collaborators, and the release of those treated bats back into the wild. Battle For Bats: Surviving White Nose Syndrome was produced in 2013 for the USDA Forest Service by Ravenswood Media. It shows how government and private agencies have come together to search for solutions to help bat populations. Related Research Biocontrol Agents We are currently investigating novel and efficacious methods for biological and chemical control of P. destructans . Further study is needed to establish effective and safe treatment regimes as well as potential collateral impacts. However, initial testing has yielded positive results. Rhodococcus rhodochrous strain DAP 96253 is a strain of bacteria with unique metabolic activity. It was originally discovered by Dr. George Pierce and developed at Georgia State University for its ability to delay the ripening of climacteric fruit, after the bacteria underwent an induction process of being grown under specific conditions (as per the methods of Pierce et al., 2011). Interestingly, the delayed-ripening effects were being elicited without the fruit ever being in direct contact with the bacteria- they merely needed to share the same airspace. It was also observed that there was a lower fungal burden on exposed fruit. After a range of susceptibility tests, it was found to possess antifungal activity. We are currently investigating mechanisms behind the mode of action as well as application methods. The color seen in the image is the same as the actual pigment produced by R. rhodochrous. (© John Neville, Georgia State University) Antifungal VOCs Antifungal volatile organic compounds (VOCs), VOC formulations, essential oils, and other compounds are also being investigated for their ability to inhibit fungal growth. Development and testing is underway on a device to modulate dispersal of these compounds (patent pending, 62/036497). Strengthen the capabilities and give a competitive edge to KSU to perform materials research and development for and with industry (Lockheed-Martin, Sonoco, Gulfstream) and government agencies (NSF, DoD, NASA). Complement existing material research equipment and infrastructure at KSU, such as the equipment in the existing Engineering Materials Laboratory, the Mechanics and Materials Laboratory, and the Composite Materials Laboratory. Provide a long-term, sustainable, and synergistic impact on the entire University’s degree programs by external sponsored funding in cutting-edge materials research. Goals & Objectives CAMRE will meet the increasingly stringent requirements of cutting-edge materials technology by fundamental research, education, innovation and improved methodologies in the following thrust areas: Fabrication : Processing and synthesis of advanced materials and structures. Characterization : Developing both field characterization techniques and in-situ monitoring for the microstructural and the effective behavior of advanced materials and structures. Durability : Predicting long-term performance (over lifetimes up to several decades) of materials and structures as well as understanding environmental exposure affects. Failure : Understanding the failure modes of materials and structures, and how the microstructure and morphology of these materials affect the failure modes. Education : Providing research opportunities for KSU undergraduates during the academic year and providing opportunities for summer research experiences. Outreach : Motivating, informing, and stimulating interest through participation in seminars, workshops, symposia and conferences. Presentation : Developing the oral and poster presentation skills of KSU undergraduates by dissemination of research results at professional meetings and conferences, and enhancing their verbal skills through technical report writing. Founded in 2009 at Southern Polytechnic State University (merged with KSU in 2015) in Marietta, Georgia, GPTRC has addressed many pressing issues related to civil and construction infrastructure at local, state, and national levels. At GPTRC faculty and student work together through various interdisciplinary and cross-border collaborations and funded projects for the advancement of scientific and technological research in the areas of transportation, road pavement, construction materials, and sustainability. While focusing on those areas, we always aspire to explore new research needs and to build long-term partnerships with other institutions You can be our next team member or collaborator. Please consider joining GPTRC. Thank you very much! Sunanda Dissanayake Director of GPRC Professor and Chair of the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering Mission and Goals Mission The mission of GPTRC is to improve the safety, mobility, and productivity of transportation systems through innovative research focusing on the following themes. (1) Improve the safety, economy, and durability of highway pavement by conducting research in pavement materials, performance modeling, design, construction, rehabilitation, and maintenance. (2) Improve the safety and efficiency of transportation infrastructure by conducting research in innovative infrastructure systems design and management, active/proactive traffic management, and traffic control technologies. The GPTRC’s mission directly aligns with the University’s research, scholarship, creative activities, and public service initiatives, which aim to expand and apply knowledge, contribute to economic development, and improve the quality of life in local communities, Georgia, the nation, and the world. Goals Establish a nationally recognized research program in pavement and transportation engineering. Serve the local and regional research needs with extensions to critically important issues at the national and international levels. Foster multidisciplinary research through partnership or collaboration with other universities, research institutes, public agencies, industry, and individuals. Serve as a regional resource center for transportation/pavement professionals and industry in Georgia. GPTRC aims to develop and offer certification and professional education/training programs in pavement and traffic engineering. GPTRC also provides laboratory and field test services and products evaluation to help expedite commercialization and adoption of new or emerging technologies. Those include, but not limited to: Testing on pavement materials (e.g., asphalt, concrete, aggregate, and soils) Performance testing of mix designs Evaluation of evolving Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) technologies, such as emerging vehicle detection technologies, adaptive signal control systems, Bluetooth or Wi-Fi based travel time systems, transportation initiatives related to smart cities. Exploration of "Deep Learning" and “Big Data” applications in the field of pavement and traffic engineering. Serve as an on-campus resource center to supplement classroom learning and provide research opportunities to students. Students in related fields will have opportunities to gain research and hands-on experience and financial support from the Center by participating in both externally and internally funded research projects. Members GPTRC Members are KSU faculty who span a wide spectrum of academic departments in all colleges at KSU, as well as the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Their areas of focus and research interests are aligned with one or more of GPTRC’s research goals. You have tackled difficult exams, participated in extracurricular activities, and possibly completed an internship or research project — all while making life-long friends and memories. Rather than an ending, commencement (both the word and the ceremony) represents a beginning. It is appropriate that an occasion that marks the beginning of a new phase of life should be conducted with pomp and circumstance, stateliness, and tradition. Apply to Graduate Important Dates Watch the Ceremony Live! A live stream of each commencement ceremony is available 15 minutes prior to each ceremony. Important Dates and Deadlines Aug 31: Application to Graduate Deadline* If you intend to graduate in Fall 2026, you must Apply to Graduate by August 31, 2026, to be eligible to participate in Commencement. Participation includes walking across the stage at the KSU Convocation Center in your cap and gown to receive your personal recognition. If you apply to graduate after this date, you will not be eligible to participate in Commencement. Only students who apply to graduate by this deadline will receive an email from decisions@kennesaw.edu with instructions to complete the Commencement Participation Acknowledgment, which is also required to participate. Sept 1: Participation Acknowledgment Deadline* If you applied to graduate by August 31, 2026, and would like to celebrate your graduation with us by participating in your college’s commencement ceremony, you must complete the Commencement Participation Acknowledgment by September 1, 2026. If you do not complete the acknowledgment by this deadline, you will not be eligible to participate in Commencement. Only students who complete the acknowledgment by this deadline will receive an email from diploma@diploma.kennesaw.edu on Sept. 8, 2026, when Tassel, the commencement reservation portal, is open to begin accepting reservations. This email will contain instructions on how to RSVP “Yes” for Commencement, which is also required to participate. Sept 28: RSVP Deadline* If you completed the Commencement Participation Acknowledgment by September 1, 2026, you will receive an email from diploma@kennesaw.edu on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, with instructions on how to RSVP “Yes” for Commencement by the Monday, September 28, 2026, deadline. Selecting “Yes” will allow you to reserve up to four (4) guest tickets. Additional guest tickets for your college’s commencement ceremony may become available for purchase at a later date. If so, you will receive an email from diploma@kennesaw.edu with more details. If you do not RSVP by this deadline, you will not be eligible to participate in Commencement. Doctoral candidates will not receive these emails and must coordinate with the Graduate College regarding their attendance and guest tickets instead. Oct 5: Ceremony Information Available Each college’s designated commencement ceremony date and time will be posted to the Commencement Ceremonies webpage by October 5, 2026. Oct 28: Regalia Home Delivery Deadline October 28, 2026, is the deadline to order regalia through Jostens for delivery to your home address via USPS by December 11, 2026. After this deadline, you may also order through the KSU Bookstore for in-store pickup. Official KSU regalia is required for all graduates participating in Commencement. Graduates who do not wear official KSU regalia will not be permitted to participate in the ceremony. Nov 17: Name Pronunciation Submission Deadline On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, you will receive an email from diploma@kennesaw.edu prompting you to log into Tassel, the commencement reservation portal, to review your assigned ceremony date and time. You may also submit the phonetic spelling of your name, so it will be pronounced correctly during the ceremony. This step is not required to participate in Commencement. The deadline to submit the phonetic spelling of your name is Tuesday, November 17, 2026. *Required to be eligible to participate in Commencement Visit Commencement Ceremonies for more information. Check your KSU email regularly to stay informed. Make sure you’re opted into Registrar communications. He oversees 25 public colleges and universities with a more than $12.6 billion annual budget, 50,000 faculty and staff, and more than 382,000 students. The Georgia Public Library Service and the Georgia Archives are also part of USG, which has been recognized nationally for its efforts in affordability, cost savings and student attainment. The number of students annually earning degrees has increased more than 50.6% since 2011. Prior to becoming chancellor, Perdue was the 31st Secretary of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) from 2017 to 2021. He also served two terms as the governor of Georgia, from 2003 to 2011, and was a member of the Georgia Senate from 1991 to 2001, where he chaired the Senate Higher Education Committee and eventually became Senate President Pro Tem. As Agriculture Secretary, Perdue managed a workforce of 110,000 employees with the stated objective of being the most efficient, effective and customer-friendly agency in federal government. This included stabilizing the food supply chain during the COVID-19 pandemic and launching the Farmers to Families Food Box program to ensure the most vulnerable Americans were fed. As governor, he reformed the state budget and focused on eliminating wasteful spending while Georgia faced unprecedented twin recessions. His fiscal management during those eight years prepared Georgia to excel when revenues returned and allowed Georgia to maintain its Triple-A bond ratings. During his term, high school graduates in Georgia posted the highest graduation rates and SAT scores in state history. His tenure in the state Legislature came at a time when lawmakers worked with Georgia Gov. Zell Miller to craft one of the most innovative higher education programs in the nation, the HOPE Scholarship. Perdue in his role as higher education chairman also helped recruit USG Chancellor Stephen Portch to Georgia. This work reinforced a passion for higher education that continues today, including a commitment to maintaining the connection between a world-class university system and economic success for the benefit of the state and all Georgians. Born in Perry, Georgia, on Dec. 20, 1946, and raised on a farm in Bonaire, Perdue is a veterinarian and agribusiness owner who graduated from Warner Robins High School and earned his Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from the University of Georgia. He is also a veteran, serving four years in the U.S. Air Force. He is married to the former Mary Ruff, also a UGA graduate. They have four children, 14 grandchildren and have served as foster parents for eight children awaiting adoption. When the ceremony is completed, faculty may process out at the same time as the platform party and exit through the back of the Convocation Center. Please join us in congratulating your students at the Siegel Student Recreation and Activities Center starting 90 minutes prior to each ceremony’s start time. This is a great photo opportunity and send-off! If you need assistance or special accommodation due to a physical limitation, please contact Academic Affairs ( academicaffairs@kennesaw.edu or 470-578-6023) to advise the Faculty Processional Team so they may assist you accordingly. Volunteers play a key role in ensuring the smooth operation of the ceremonies, and your support helps make the day memorable for graduates and their loved ones. Find essential information for graduates preparing to participate in the ceremony, including how to RSVP, get tickets, and access photos from the event! Check‑In Information Check‑in opens 2 hours before the ceremony. Graduates must check in at least 30 minutes before the ceremony begins. Late arrivals will not be permitted to participate. Quick Links: Commencement Attendance Portal - Tassel Day of Commencement Academic Regalia - Caps and Gowns Graduating with Honors Alumni #ForeverOwlFest Photography Fall 2026 application deadline is Monday, August 31 A graduation application is required. To participate in commencement, it must be submitted by Monday, August 31. Commencement Attendance Portal - Tassel Tassel is the system used to manage commencement operations, including graduate RSVPs, graduate communications, and grad passes. Graduates must create an account in Tassel to RSVP their attendance, to receive four guest tickets, to ensure their name is pronounced and listed correctly for the commencement ceremony. All students (except doctoral students) wanting to participate in commencement MUST log into the Commencement Attendance Portal -Tassel and RSVP their intent to participate in commencement. Students who do not RSVP their intent to participate in commencement may not be able to participate in commencement and may not receive guest tickets. The Fall 2026 Tassel Commencement Reservation portal will open on September 8 and close on September 28. You will receive an email from Tassel when the portal is ready to accept reservations. Commencement Regalia Day of Commencement On the day of commencement at Kennesaw State, it’s important to plan ahead using the following list for a smooth graduation experience. Student's must check-in 30 minutes prior to the ceremony start time. Students arriving late will not be allowed to participate. All Graduates must park in the Central Parking Deck . All bags MUST meet the clear bag policy . Any bag larger than 4.5” x 6.5” will be turned away. Remember to transfer your claimed tickets to your guests prior to your arrival. This ensures your guests have time to download their tickets before approaching the doors. Tickets will NOT be available for purchase on the day of the ceremony. Check in at the Dr. Betty L. Siegel Student Recreation and Activities Center 2 hours before your ceremony begins. You should arrive dressed and ready to graduate, with your gown on but unzipped to speed up security screening. Graduates must be checked in 30 minutes before the ceremony starts to participate. Any graduates arriving after that time will need to check in with registrar staff to see if they can attend a later ceremony. The Dr. Betty L. Siegel Student Recreation and Activities Center will have a no re-entry policy, so once you check in, you will not be allowed to leave and re-enter before the start of the ceremony. A ticket office representative will be on site to help with any potential ticket issues, and we will have snacks and drinks available for purchase if necessary. Bottled water will be provided for free. Any unauthorized modifications to regalia will be confiscated and returned to the graduate after the ceremony. Unauthorized modifications include noise-making items on mortarboards, or any language that violates the law, Board of Regents or KSU policies, such as threatening, harassing, obscene, or discriminatory content. The livestream of the ceremony will begin 15 minutes before the advertised start time. Academic Regalia - Caps and Gowns Graduation is an exciting time at Kennesaw State University as student accomplishments are celebrated throughout campus, culminating with a commencement ceremony. In preparation for this significant occasion, it is required for graduates to wear the appropriate graduation attire and academic regalia. Graduates who are not wearing the required KSU regalia will not be allowed to participate in the commencement ceremony. The university reserves the right to require graduates to change their cap if it is deemed inappropriate. Please follow the guidelines listed below. We recommend underneath the graduation gown, graduates wear dark, professional attire and shoes to complement the black academic regalia of Kennesaw State University. Academic regalia can be purchased through Jostens . Josten's regalia home ship deadline is October 28, 2026 for undergraduate and graduate regalia (excluding Doctoral regalia) to ensure delivery for Commencement week. Undergraduate and Graduate regalia, with the exception of doctorate regalia, may also be purchased at the KSU Bookstore any time prior to commencement ceremonies. Doctoral regalia must be ordered by October 10, 2026 to ensure delivery beginning November 25, 2026. Undergraduate Degree Undergraduate degree graduates must wear the new black gown with gold piping designed with two gold embroidered KSU school seals, black mortarboard (cap), and black and gold tassel. (Note: The tassel is worn on the right side of the mortarboard (cap) prior to the degree being conferred, and on the left side after the degree is conferred.) The university reserves the right to require graduates to change their cap if it is deemed inappropriate. Graduate or Specialist Degrees Master’s and Specialist degree graduates wear the new black gown with gold piping designed with two gold embroidered KSU school seals, a hood, and a black mortarboard (cap) with black and gold tassel. Each hood has a separate color* based on the discipline and it is the most distinctive feature of this academic attire. Education Specialist hoods are somewhat different in that they are longer and wider than the master’s hoods. The university reserves the right to require graduates to change their cap if it is deemed inappropriate. Graduate Hood Colors by Major (PDF) Doctoral Degrees Doctoral students need to apply for graduation by the posted deadline and be approved by the Graduate College to participate in commencement to receive guest tickets. For more information, please contact gradcollege@kennesaw.edu *Doctorate students will be contacted by the Graduate College for Commencement attendance and ticking purposes. Nationally Recognized KSU Registered Organizations Recognition Attire: Membership in an honor society is independent from KSU graduation honor policy. Students who qualified for membership in registered Student Organizations, Honor Societies, or Department Discipline Honor Programs while attending KSU may wear approved regalia representing these societies/programs during the Commencement ceremonies. The only types of regalia items that may be approved are Honor cords, stoles, medallions, or pins. Students must contact the appropriate academic department or sponsoring student organization for more information on obtaining these items. The KSU Bookstore is not responsible for ordering honors Commencement regalia. Students who are members of multiple honor societies may wear multiple pieces of regalia. International stoles received by graduating students who earned a previous degree from their home country may be worn during Commencement. During Commencement, student members of the organizations listed below are eligible to wear the following approved designations of their respective society/program: Approved Regalia PDF Regalia Assistance Available for Graduating Students Regalia Assistance Available for Graduating Students We are committed to ensuring all students have the opportunity to participate in their commencement ceremony, regardless of financial circumstances, by offering loaned regalia to students who are unable to afford the cost of graduation attire. Regalia will be available for ceremony use only and is distributed based on demonstrated financial need. Please note that availability is limited. To submit your application, visit: https://kennesaw-advocate.symplicity.com/collections/regalia_request. For questions, contact CARE Services at careservices@kennesaw.edu . Graduating with Honors Undergraduate Honors Students are required to have an adjusted GPA of at least 3.5 and earn at least 30 semester credit hours in residence at KSU to graduate with honors. Summa Cum Laude (3.90 - 4.00) Magna Cum Laude (3.70 - 3.89) Cum Laude (3.50 - 3.69) Graduates receiving honors for their undergraduate degrees are acknowledged at commencement by the public announcement as they cross the stage and the gold-colored honor tassels worn with the graduation mortarboards (caps). Students participating in commencement will be recognized with Honors using the cumulative institutional GPA from the prior semester from the term in which they walk. For example, students graduating in the Spring 2026 semester will have the cumulative institutional GPA used from the Fall 2025 semester and students participating in the Fall 2026 semester will have the cumulative institutional GPA from Summer 2025 to determine their honors designation. The diploma and transcripts will have the appropriate honors based on the GPA at the time the student completes his/her degree. Honor Society Membership in an honor society is independent from KSU graduation honor policy. See the Nationally Recognized Organizations for your honor cords (pdf). Alumni The KSU Alumni Association serves the alumni of the University and supports the initiatives of KSU by: Building positive, long-term relationships among KSU alumni, the University, and the community Providing value-added services to KSU alumni through networking opportunities, affiliation programs, and KSU-wide events Supporting the long-term objectives of the University through fundraising, fostering community support, and advocating for KSU As a new member of the KSU alumni community, you benefit from partnerships with the University and Alumni Association. Make sure you don't miss out on this chance to get a free gift from your Kennesaw State Alumni Association, photo opportunities to capture your big moment, live music, and more! Lodging and Dining Visitor's Guide Tickets Know Before You Go Ceremony Guidelines Commencement is an exciting time for you and your graduate. Please follow these guidelines and be considerate of other guests so everyone may have a great experience. Thank you. The ceremony will be held in the Convocation Center . The doors open 1.5 hours prior to the start of the ceremony. There is a clear bag policy for Commencement. No outside food or beverages are allowed inside the Convocation Center. There is a concession stand open once you enter the building. Any unauthorized modifications to regalia will be confiscated and returned to the graduate after the ceremony. Please allow adequate time to arrive at KSU, park, enter the facility, and be seated prior to the ceremony. The ceremony will start promptly at the advertised time. You must present a ticket to be admitted. Children three and under do not need a ticket for admission. Saving seats in the Convocation Center is allowed up to 15 minutes prior to the start of the ceremony. Strollers are not permitted in the arena, but there will be a stroller check-in located in the lobby. Balloons are not permitted inside the Convocation Center. Following the ceremony, all graduates will be outside of the Convocation Center. Plan accordingly and prearrange a designated area to meet your guests and graduates. Clear Bag Guidelines Approved for Entry All Bags Are Subject to Search At Kennesaw State University, our venue policies are in place to ensure the safety and well-being of all attendees during commencement. Clear bags are required, with sizes not exceeding 12"x6"x12" for totes, 11"x11" for zip lock bags, and 6.5"x4.5" for small clutches or purses. All bags are subject to search. Prohibited items include weapons, outside food, and large signs. Please see the full list of prohibited items below. For your convenience, a $5 bag check is available at the venue , with all proceeds supporting KSU Cares. Please also note that KSU is a smoke-free campus, and security may inspect items for safety at any time. Clear Tote Size may NOT exceed 12”x6”x12”. Logo may only be on one side of the bag. Items in the tote MUST be loose. Clear Zip Lock Bag Size may NOT exceed 11”x11”. Resealable Clear Clutch Bag or Small Purse Size may NOT exceed 6.5”x4.5”. May include a handle or strap. Does NOT need to be clear. Prohibited Items Security has the right to inspect any item at any time for the purpose of safety. Prohibited items* must be returned to cars or disposed of before entering the venue. No place will be offered to store any of these items. Alcohol Aerosol/pressurized cans Animals (except service animals and service-in-training) Artificial noisemakers including airhorns, whistles, musical instruments, etc. Balloons (or balloons on Sticks) Diaper bags Flags, banners, posters, or signs bigger than 24”x18” (medium poster size) Flower vases Flyers, handouts, advertisements Glassware of any kind Glitter Illegal substances, drugs, and chemicals of any kind Inflatables Instruments of any kind Laser pointers Non-biodegradable Confetti Open flames Outside food or beverages (empty bottles allowed) Poles or staffs of any kind (metal, plastic, wooden) Weapons, flares, fireworks, and smoke devices Use of cigarettes, cigars, e-cigarettes, vapes, juuls, dip, chew, etc. Tri-pods and cameras with lenses above 4 in" Exception: Medical bags are only allowed if they are no larger than what is required to transport necessary medical equipment. Kennesaw State University is committed to the health and well-being of all members of the KSU community. A smoke/tobacco-free campus means that everyone, including guests, are free to travel and visit anywhere on campus without having to avoid potentially health-hazardous situations. Prior to Commencement ceremonies, KSU offers a bag check for $5 before entering Commencement. All proceeds go to support KSU Cares. support ksu cares *Event management reserves the right to make exceptions upon its discretion. Please visit the Bookstore website for more information. The concessions stand will be open during all ceremonies and will accept major credit cards. Outside food and beverages are not allowed (empty bottles allowed). Please keep in mind this setup is a card-only venue for all purchases. Items the concession stand offers: Light Refreshments Snacks Bottled Soft Drinks Bookstore Photography The Grad Team will take the official graduation photos for the commencement ceremonies. This will include candid photographs before and after the ceremonies, as well as an on-stage photo with the President, and a graduation portrait. These marshals carry KSU batons — created for the inauguration of President Daniel S. Papp — as they lead the processional lines. Like the mace, the baton was originally a war club – though miniature in stature. The four batons, created by biology professor Bowman Davis, are hand-turned staff made out of walnut, featuring a hand-carved, stylized owl, complete with an ebony finish to reflect the styling of the mace. Gold and black tassels complete the batons. The Dais Party The dais party is the last group in the procession to enter the hall. The group consists of the president, the provost and vice president for academic affairs, cabinet members, the registrar, deans of the colleges and invited honored guests, such as the commencement speaker. When members of the dais party reach their seats, the processional ends. The chief faculty marshal declares the candidates for graduation to be assembled and the ceremony begins. Kennesaw State University Mace The Kennesaw State University Mace is a ceremonial staff carried by the chief faculty marshal of the academic procession; an honor given to the chair of the Faculty Senate. Steeped in rich tradition, the practice of carrying a mace dates to the Middle Ages. Originally designed as a weapon, a mace was carried by a respected senior member of the community chosen to protect and guide leaders as their group traveled through crowded streets. Kennesaw State takes special pride in its mace, which was designed by Patrick Taylor, former chairman of the Department of Visual Arts, and hand-crafted on campus. The polished bronze handgrip is a stylized owl. In addition to being Kennesaw State’s mascot, the owl is the symbol of Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom. A large bronze medallion displaying the university seal, along with festive ribbons representing university colors, adorn a globe near the top of the mace, symbolizing graduates venturing out into the world. Atop the globe sits the traditional symbol of higher education – a lamp of learning, with a flame representing the quest for knowledge. Presidential Seal The Kennesaw State University Seal is an adaptation of the state seal of Georgia with Kennesaw Mountain in the background. M. Thomson Salter III, professor emeritus of art and a charter member of the faculty, designed the seal. The Chain of Office The Chain of Office is a tradition that dates to the Middle Ages as a symbol or badge of office. Universities continue the tradition by incorporating the chain and medallion during ceremonial occasions, denoting the president's status as the presiding authority over the ceremony. Our four-inch medallion bears the official University seal. The medallion is suspended by a chain link with the names and years in office of the previous University presidents suspends the medallion. During the ceremony, the Chain of Office will rest on a pedestal on stage. Gonfalons The third presidential inauguration at KSU ushered in many new changes, including the academic gonfalons. Banners suspended on a crossbar, gonfalons are another piece of medieval history that have been incorporated into academic tradition. The gonfalons reflect a timeless style, incorporate the university’s colors and represent all 11 colleges at Kennesaw State University. Academic Regalia The caps and gowns worn at commencement connect contemporary graduates with scholarly tradition that dates back as long as universities have existed. Clerics, ecclesiastics and scholars wore hoods or caps and heavy gowns at European universities during the Middle Ages. Beginning in the middle of the 14th century, scholars at English universities wore an academic costume of “bunge-and sand-colored habits.” A costume for commencement has been a tradition since the beginning of higher education in America. In 1895, the Intercollegiate Bureau of Academic Costume was created and a standard code of academic dress for commencements was adopted. It calls for the existing cap and gown (the traditional bachelor’s gown with long, open, pointed sleeves) and the master’s gown (with its long sleeves hanging down from the elbow) to set apart the graduates. The doctoral gown has bell-shaped sleeves, with three velvet stripes on each sleeve. As such, the University strives to be alert to the needs of the University community by maintaining an environment in which appeals, grievances, and complaints are addressed in an expeditious, fair, and collegial manner. KSU’s approach to resolving formal written appeals, grievances, or complaints is to direct the matter to the most appropriate office. The personnel of those offices possess the qualifications, experience, and knowledge to manage a formal resolution process as well as to work in a collaborative and confidential manner to reach a resolution for each individual based on the merits of his or her case. This page was developed to assist current and prospective students of Kennesaw State University in submitting complaints and appeals and to direct them to the most effective venue for accurate information and resolution. KSU’s policy on complaints resolution may be found at the Policy website . Thank you. Kennesaw State University Complaints and Appeals Resources Undergraduate Catalog - Student Rights and Responsibilities/Academic Policies Graduate Catalog - Student Rights and Responsibilities/Academic Policies Student Handbook - Directory of Departments and Contact Information Ombuds Office - Independent Conflict Resolution Resource Registrar - Student Consumer Information Online Course Complaints and Appeals - Student Consumer Information The Office of the University Ombuds is a confidential, impartial, and independent conflict resolution resource at Kennesaw State University. The services of the Ombuds are available to all members of the KSU community: students, faculty, and staff. Whether it is your first step or your last resort, you may contact the Ombuds when regular channels have failed to bring resolution to your problem or when you are not certain what step to take next. Submitting Concerns Kennesaw State University is committed to maintaining an environment in which concerns are addressed in a fair and collegial manner. The KSU Concern website provides a place to submit a formal, written concern where a resolution has not been informally reached. The more information that you can provide, the better we can serve you. Submit Your Concern Alternative Complaints and Appeals Resources Kennesaw State University strives to satisfactorily resolve student complaints and appeals. If a complaint cannot be resolved internally, the student may then file a grievance with the regulatory agency in the state where they are receiving instruction and/or the institution’s accrediting agency. Any student or employee in the University System aggrieved by a final decision of the president of an institution may apply to the Board of Regents for a review of the decision by referring to these Board of Regents’ policies: Student Appeals: Policy 4.7 Employment Appeals: Policy 8.2.21 Application for Discretionary Review: Policy 6.26 Fraudulent activity related to the University System of Georgia, or suggestions to improve ongoing operations may be reported to University System of Georgia Ethics & Compliance or by calling 1-877-516-3466. The USG and Kennesaw State University are committed to the highest ethical and professional standards in pursuit of its mission to create a more educated Georgia.
