Alumna earns competitive scholarship to study in Japan September 25, 2026 It was a trip to Japan during high school that sparked Leah Hackaday’s curiosity about how other countries operate and interact with each other, a curiosity that eventually led her to major in international affairs when she enrolled at Kennesaw State University. The opportunity to spend a semester in Japan during her junior year at KSU only grew her interest in the country. Today, thanks to earning a competitive scholarship from the Japanese government, Hackaday, a graduate of KSU’s School of Government and International Affairs, has now begun studying for a master’s degree in international affairs at Waseda University in Tokyo. Read More Kennesaw State researcher developing safer, more efficient computing systems for intelligent vehicles September 24, 2026 Modern vehicles are becoming computers on wheels, powered by increasingly complex software and artificial intelligence. As those systems take on more responsibility, they must process information quickly and reliably enough to keep critical functions running safely. Kennesaw State University computer science researcher Kun Suo is working to improve how those systems operate through a $356,782 National Science Foundation (NSF) grant focused on developing more efficient and secure computing infrastructure for intelligent vehicles. Read More Kennesaw State rises in U.S. News rankings of top universities September 23, 2026 Kennesaw State University continues to rise in stature among the nation’s universities while earning a top spot in Georgia for undergraduate engineering programs, according to the U.S. News & World Report 2027 Best Colleges rankings released on Sept. 22. Read More Recent NIH grants aim to improve parasite research, acquire crucial instruments September 21, 2026 Kennesaw State University researcher Soon Goo Lee recently secured two National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants to advance parasite research and expand the university's biomedical research capabilities through new instrumentation. The assistant professor of molecular biology earned an R16 grant from the NIH’s National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) to continue his study of an essential enzyme, called PMT, in protozoan parasites in hopes of finding an attackable weak spot for therapies that treat parasitic diseases. Read More Hornet Hub gives Kennesaw State competition teams space to build, innovate September 18, 2026 Kennesaw State University celebrated a new chapter in hands-on learning with the official opening of the Hornet Hub on the Marietta Campus. The 12,000-square-foot facility provides student competition teams, which design and build projects for regional and national competitions, dedicated space and resources to bring their work from concept to completion. Read More $500,000 Gift from Dr. Audrey Morgan honors KSU Provost - Dr. Ivan Pulinkala September 17, 2026 A transformative $500,000 gift from longtime Kennesaw State University philanthropist Dr. Audrey Morgan will establish the largest scholarship in KSU’s Department of Dance in honor of its founder, Dr. Ivan Pulinkala. The endowment celebrates the leadership and legacy of Pulinkala, who served as Dean of the Geer College of the Arts, prior to becoming KSU’s Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs. Read More KSU associate professor honored with 2026 Georgia Civic Excellence Award September 17, 2026 For his efforts to strengthen and protect democracy, Kennesaw State University political science associate professor Eric Castater has been honored with a 2026 Georgia Civic Excellence Award from the Georgia Democracy Resilience Network. Read More Construction management gala celebrates 25 years of student support September 16, 2026 Kennesaw State University’s Construction Management Fundraising Gala marked its 25th anniversary on Sept. 10 by continuing a longstanding tradition of support for students and the Department of Construction Management. Read More Kennesaw State launches Presidential Fellows Cohort for high-achieving Georgia students September 15, 2026 Kennesaw State University (KSU) will launch a Presidential Fellows Cohort in fall 2027, establishing a premier scholarship and leadership initiative designed to attract, retain and develop some of Georgia's highest-achieving students. Housed within the KSU Journey Honors College, the Presidential Fellows Cohort will offer Kennesaw State’s largest and most prestigious scholarship package, providing recipients with a $10,000 annual scholarship for up to four years. Read More Kennesaw State students expand research horizons in India September 14, 2026 While growing up in Guatemala, David Roque Perez saw several of his relatives battling cancer with limited access to treatment and therapies. So, for the Kennesaw State University biology major, spending the summer in India researching treatments for lung cancer not only built on his growing passion for research but also his goal of improving access to care in Guatemala. Kennesaw State software engineering student develops AI-powered navigation system September 11, 2026 For Kennesaw State University software engineering student Robert Hoeh, finding a room inside an unfamiliar building could one day be as simple as asking a question. Hoeh is helping develop an AI-powered augmented reality navigation system that lets users ask for directions and guides them through complex indoor spaces. The technology could improve accessibility for people with cognitive disabilities while also helping first responders navigate unfamiliar buildings more quickly. Read More Dr. Bobbie Bailey School of Music enters educational partnership with Atlanta Symphony September 10, 2026 Kennesaw State University’s Dr. Bobbie Bailey School of Music and the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra (ASO) are joining forces to create new opportunities for the next generation of musicians in Metro Atlanta. Beginning this fall, the educational partnership will connect KSU music students with professional musicians through masterclasses, performance opportunities and access to ASO concerts — bringing students closer to the artistry, mentorship and professional experiences that define a career on the stage. Read More Kennesaw State student publishes study on alcohol's impact on Ugandan women September 10, 2026 Few undergraduates can add “lead author in a peer-reviewed journal” to their list of accomplishments. Kennesaw State University student and Harry S. Truman Scholarship finalist Allisa George is one of them. George, an Honors student double majoring in public health and biology, is the first author of a National Institutes of Health-funded study examining alcohol and mental health among women in Uganda recently published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. Read More Power restored on Kennesaw Campus September 08, 2026 The Kennesaw campus has experienced a major power outage. We are assessing the impacts and working with Georgia Power. Updates will be provided as more information is available. Read More Kennesaw State student developing robotic rehabilitation arm inspired by family experience September 08, 2026 Watching his grandfather lose mobility after a traumatic accident gave Kennesaw State University student Kai Clifford a firsthand look at how difficult everyday movement can become. Now, the senior mechanical engineering student is using robotics research to explore ways rehabilitation could become more comfortable and effective. Read More Research into muscular degeneration wins top prize at Birla Carbon Symposium September 04, 2026 Kennesaw State University biology student Pedro Santos’ research project on muscular degeneration in fruit flies won the top prize at the 2026 Birla Carbon Scholars Symposium. Read More Student explores link between social media use and mental health in youth September 03, 2026 The American Psychological Association estimates that teens are spending an average of five hours a day on social media. At Kennesaw State University, one student is examining whether this prolonged use can also impact their mental health. Through KSU’s First-Year Scholars Program, Chance Lundy, a Keeping Sights Upward Journey Honors College student, studied the relationship between frequent social media use and suicidal ideation among adolescents. Read More Physics and mathematics double major explores theory and experiment in summer research experience August 31, 2026 Caitlyn Garrett has sampled both experimental and theoretical physics in her time at Kennesaw State University. This summer, the physics and mathematics double major combined the two during a research experience at Louisiana State University. Read More Kennesaw State architecture alumnus finds early career success August 28, 2026 Just one year after graduating from Kennesaw State University, Michael Rixom ’25 has reached a significant milestone in his profession. At just 23 years old, Rixom has achieved the rare distinction of becoming one of Georgia’s youngest licensed architects. Read More Brain research leads to publications on THC exposure, Alzheimer's drugs August 27, 2026 Kennesaw State University researcher Vishnu Suppiramaniam is advancing understanding of brain health across the lifespan, joining collaborators in publishing studies that examine the harmful effects of prenatal THC exposure and a promising Alzheimer's disease treatment. Student research into AI-powered crop monitoring system aims to prevent plant loss August 26, 2026 According to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization, plant pests and diseases destroy up to 40% of crops worldwide each year, threatening jobs and the global food supply. Kennesaw State University computer science major Brendan Miller is working on technology that could help farmers catch those problems before they spread. Read More KSU's Summer Undergraduate Research Program helps undergrads transform curiosity into societal impact August 25, 2026 Almost every day this summer, biology major Frances Conkle began her morning by meticulously sorting hundreds of fruit flies by their sex before pairing them, according to their genetics, for reproduction. The routine was part of her research into how fat tissue changes shape and moves as fruit flies grow and develop. Conkle was among 25 Kennesaw State University students who spent eight weeks, mentored by faculty, working full time on various research projects through the Summer Undergraduate Research Program. Read More Cobb Chamber names KSU President Kathy S. Schwaig as its 2028 Board Chairwoman August 24, 2026 The Cobb Chamber’s Board of Directors has named Kathy “Kat” S. Schwaig, president of Kennesaw State University, as its 2028 Chairwoman of the Board. Read More Two KSU students trade the Gold Dome for Capitol Hill August 24, 2026 Six months ago, Jada Barronton and Saideep Chilukuri answered phones in House and Senate offices under the Gold Dome. Over the summer, they both helped track legislation and conduct policy research for U.S. congressional offices on Capitol Hill. The two Kennesaw State University students, who received the university’s D.C. Owls Scholarship, spent their summer interning in Washington, and both credit a semester at the Georgia State Capitol with helping them succeed. Read More Kennesaw State student explores the mental effects of workplace automation August 21, 2026 As new technologies become a larger part of the modern workplace, Kennesaw State University student Blessing Onyekachi is researching how working alongside them affects employees' mental health. As part of KSU’s Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP), architecture student Onyekachi is studying how workers adapt as automation becomes more common in industries such as construction, manufacturing, and logistics. Read More Launch '26 celebrates new school year, sustained momentum August 20, 2026 Momentum provided the theme as Kennesaw State University’s faculty and staff gathered at VyStar Arena on Aug. 20 to celebrate the opening of the 2026-27 academic year with Launch ’26. Speakers and guests enjoyed a look into KSU’s future, illustrated by visions of continued growth, academic excellence, ascendant and relevant research, and continued student success. Read More KSU, Technovative AI sign pilot agreement with Moultrie Police Department for AI-powered behavioral health detection tool August 20, 2026 Technovative AI, Inc. and Kennesaw State University today announced a pilot agreement with the Moultrie Police Department to deploy CaseFinder, an AI-powered behavioral health detection platform that analyzes police incident reports and 911 call transcripts to identify individuals in behavioral health crisis who would otherwise go undetected. Read More Kennesaw State's economic impact tops $2.55 billion August 13, 2026 Kennesaw State University continues to be a major economic engine in metro Atlanta, growing its economic impact to more than $2.55 billion in fiscal year 2025, according to a University System of Georgia (USG) report released on Aug. 13. Read More Kennesaw State adds more on-campus housing for students August 13, 2026 Kennesaw State University is expanding its on-campus housing options for students by opening a new residence hall for the 2026-27 academic year and renovating an existing residential community. Read More Research Matters: Losing weight through personalized step counts August 12, 2026 In this episode of Research Matters, we talk with Professor of Exercise Science Bob Buresh, who leads an interdisciplinary team investigating how walking can be a transformative, accessible, and cost-effective approach to fighting obesity. KSU bolsters infrastructure to support student experience, University's growth August 12, 2026 From new residence halls to expanded academic and student support facilities, Kennesaw State University’s Campus Master Plan is taking shape through a wave of completed and ongoing projects that are transforming both campuses and positioning the university for continued growth. Read More Marietta Campus to feature new dining, transportation, and campus upgrades this fall August 11, 2026 Students returning to Kennesaw State University’s Marietta Campus this fall will find more dining options, new bus routes, and several campus improvements designed to enhance the overall student experience. Leading the updates is the opening of the Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center. Officially opened in April, the new facility serves as a hub for interdisciplinary research while also providing students with a place to study, gather, and recharge between classes. Read More Kennesaw State is harnessing momentum to advance research, elevate the student experience, and build for the future August 10, 2026 A theme is emerging for Kennesaw State’s ascension as one of the fastest-growing institutions in the country: momentum. Read More Kennesaw State professor earns national award for contribution to education August 07, 2026 Kennesaw State University professor Erik Malewski has received a national award for his decades of contribution to teaching and learning. A professor of curriculum studies in the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education, Malewski has been selected to receive the Curriculum & Pedagogy Group Lifetime Award. The national honor recognizes scholars whose careers have made lasting contributions to curriculum and pedagogy through scholarship, mentorship, and leadership. Read More Kennesaw State appoints Tracy Fasolino as associate dean, Wellstar School of Nursing director August 06, 2026 Kennesaw State University has named accomplished nursing educator and healthcare leader Tracy Fasolino, Ph.D., as associate dean and director of the Wellstar School of Nursing (WSON) and professor of nursing, effective Aug. 1. Read More Kennesaw State expands on-campus residential housing with the opening of The Summit II August 04, 2026 Kennesaw State University has officially opened The Summit II, a residence hall designed to foster connection, belonging, and student success while adding a new on-campus housing option for first-year students. Read More Kennesaw State student explores how children respond when adults lie July 31, 2026 By age 6, most children know that lying is wrong. But what do they think when adults lie, especially someone they trust like a parent? Kennesaw State University psychology student Charlie Clement is examining how children ages 6 to 11 interpret lies told by people with varying levels of authority. Read More Research consortium leads to opportunities for Kennesaw State students July 31, 2026 In March of this year, Kennesaw State University joined the Oak Ridge Associated Universities, a consortium of more than 170 universities that collaborate on research initiatives, share resources, and help place students in federal research opportunities at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee. Junior chemistry major Miriam Raggs is spending this summer conducting research at Oak Ridge, through the lab’s Research Student Internship (RSI) program, thanks in part to this association but also thanks to her research mentor, Assistant Professor of Chemistry Madalynn Marshall. Read More Mechatronics engineering student uses AI-powered system to keep waterways clean July 30, 2026 It is estimated that up to 23 million metric tons of plastic enter waterways each year, according to the United Nations Environment Programme. While harmful materials continue to plague governments around the world, a Kennesaw State University student is developing an artificial intelligence-powered system to detect litter before it reaches the ocean. Mechatronics engineering student Saam Grami is creating a system that detects, classifies, and tracks floating litter in rivers. Read More Kennesaw State professors use NSF grant to strengthen semiconductor education through interactive learning July 29, 2026 As the United States works to strengthen its semiconductor industry, Kennesaw State University researchers are helping prepare the next generation of engineers. Through a National Science Foundation-funded project, they are using interactive visualizations to make one of electrical engineering's most challenging subjects easier for students to understand. Greece study abroad challenges KSU students to tell stories of the past with bones July 28, 2026 In a small village on the island of Crete, just southeast of mainland Greece, anthropology major Jess Drilling learned to identify signs of osteoarthritis in skeletal remains, helping piece together the stories of people who walked the earth centuries ago. Drilling is one of four Kennesaw State University students who spent part of their summer at an archaeological research center, studying human skeletal remains dating from the fifth to seventh centuries to uncover clues about how people lived, what they ate, and the injuries and illnesses they experienced. Read More Chemistry students engage in research through KSU lab's NSF C-CAS affiliation July 27, 2026 Like many college students, Kennesaw State University senior Lilianna Kocai and junior Genevieve Insalaca have spent their summer surrounded by a buzzing cohort of friends – without leaving campus. The two chemistry students have spent the summer synthesizing fluorescent compounds and running computer-assisted simulations in the laboratory of KSU Associate Professor of Organic Chemistry Carl Saint-Louis. Their work is part of an innovative program funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) that involves computer-assisted programming as another method of experimentation. Read More Record number of Gilman Scholars at Kennesaw State travel the globe July 24, 2026 Aaliyah Uchendu is one of a record number of KSU students awarded the Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship this year. The Gilman Scholarship is a prestigious award funded by the US State Department that provides recipients up to $5,000 to support study or internships abroad; only about 20%-25% of applicants are selected for the award. Read More Mosquito research draws KSU environmental science major to the woods for the summer July 23, 2026 Kennesaw State University senior Brooklyn Galvan has found a happy place for the summer – in the mosquito-infested woods near Hattiesburg, Mississippi. The environmental science major is conducting research into mosquitoes as pollinators as part of the National Science Foundation’s Research Experiences for Undergraduates for Gulf Coastal Plains Ecology. The experience builds on Galvan’s experience researching the importance of mosquitoes to the ecosystem in the lab of KSU Assistant Professor of Microbiology Andrew Haddow. Read More Kennesaw State professor earns Texas Innovator's Award for AI platform supporting student success July 22, 2026 Kennesaw State University assistant professor Sagnik Dakshit, of the College of Computing and Software Engineering, has earned a Texas Innovator's Award for developing an artificial intelligence-powered platform that supports student success. He received the honor for creating VTA, or Virtual Teaching Assistant, a tool designed to provide personalized academic support while helping instructors improve learning outcomes. Read More Physics student enriches knowledge at National High Magnetic Field Laboratory July 21, 2026 Kennesaw State University physics student Matt Bonvissuto has taken what he has learned on campus to the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory in Tallahassee, Florida, on a Research Experiences for Undergraduates project funded in part by the National Science Foundation. Read More Kennesaw State University showcases global impact through the FIFA World Cup 2026 July 20, 2026 With the world’s eyes fixed on Atlanta during the FIFA World Cup 2026™, Kennesaw State University emerged as a key partner in executing one of the globe’s most celebrated sporting traditions, emphasizing KSU’s growing status as a vital contributor to Georgia’s economic success. Read More Kennesaw State's Mookerji Innovation Fund hits 50 startups in just over five years July 15, 2026 A little more than five years ago, Kennesaw State University set out to prove that student entrepreneurs could build real, fundable companies. Today, the University’s Robin and Doug Shore Entrepreneurship & Innovation Center Mookerji Innovation Fund achieved this goal by investing in its 50th startup company, Esoteric Sync. Read More From personal tragedy to innovation: Professor advances virtual reality grief support July 14, 2026 Shaped by experience navigating loss and grief, a Kennesaw State University researcher is leveraging emerging technologies that could improve access to community and support for bereaved parents. Funded by a two-year grant from the National Science Foundation, Lei Zhang, a human-computer interaction researcher in College of Computing and Software Engineering, is building a virtual reality system that lets bereaved parents meet, share memories, and process grief together in a shared immersive digital space, inspired by his own experiences losing a child to cancer. Read More Kennesaw State team building miniature satellite with sights on reaching orbit July 13, 2026 For Cary Chun ’21, ’25, space has been a lifelong fascination. As a child, watching NASA's Spirit and Opportunity rovers explore Mars convinced him he wanted to build robots capable of exploring places humans cannot. Now, the Kennesaw State University alum is helping students pursue that same dream. NASCAR star visits Kennesaw State, meets with engineering students on motorsports team July 10, 2026 NASCAR Cup Series driver Ricky Stenhouse Jr. knows the hard work that goes into building a fast race car, having grown up working in an engine shop in Mississippi before enjoying a successful 18-year career in stock car racing. The 2023 Daytona 500 champion and driver for Hyak Motorsports recently visited the Kennesaw State University Marietta Campus to tour the KSU Motorsports team facilities and speak to students from the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology (SPCEET). Read More Kennesaw State University Alumni Association announces 2026-2027 officers July 09, 2026 The Kennesaw State University Alumni Association has elected its 2026–2027 officers, naming a distinguished group of alumni leaders who will help advance the Association's mission of fostering lifelong engagement among more than 160,000 Kennesaw State and Southern Polytechnic State graduates. Read More Kennesaw State architecture chair honored with ARCC Mary Kihl Distinguished Service Award July 09, 2026 When Professor of Architecture Saif Haq learned he had been selected to receive the 2025–2026 ARCC Mary Kihl Distinguished Service Award, the recognition carried special meaning. The Mary Kihl Distinguished Service Award recognizes individuals who have made significant, lasting contributions to architectural research through the consortium. Read More From KSU Owl Network to FIFA World Cup, alumna builds sports media career July 08, 2026 In preparation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Kennesaw State University alumna Maddie Crews ’24 marked her calendar for 49 consecutive days of covering the competition for multiple media outlets. Read More Ph.D. student finds AI can detect warning signs of global oil crises before they happen July 07, 2026 As geopolitical conflicts continue to disrupt global energy markets, Kennesaw State University Ph.D. student Nzubechukwu Ohalete found that artificial intelligence (AI) can identify warning signs of major oil crises weeks before they occur. Read More Engineering graduate turns campus involvement into a foundation for future success July 06, 2026 From leading student organizations, to conducting research, and gaining industry experience, Samantha Bevis ’25 has made the most of every opportunity during her time at Kennesaw State University. Those experiences helped shape her into a leader and aspiring educator, paving the way for her continued studies in mechanical engineering. Read More Wellstar College launches first study abroad program to Amsterdam, providing a transformative global experience for KSU students July 02, 2026 Kennesaw State University's Wellstar College launched its first Amsterdam study abroad program, giving students immersive global public health experiences through research, cultural engagement, and experiential learning. Read More Sophomore Scholar explores drone technology to expand internet connectivity in remote areas June 30, 2026 Imagine a network of sensors spread across a remote farm, collecting data about soil conditions and water levels. Now imagine those sensors are miles from reliable internet access. For Kennesaw State University student Drew Haase, solving that communication challenge is the focus of research that could help connect hard-to-reach locations using unmanned aerial vehicles. Read More Journalism student plying her craft as a World Cup photographer June 29, 2026 As a young soccer player growing up in Georgia, Sofia Cupertino never imagined that one day she would be standing on the sidelines of a FIFA World Cup match, camera in hand, photographing some of the game's biggest stars on the world’s biggest stage. Now a journalism student in Kennesaw State University’s Norman J. Radow College of Humanities and Social Sciences, Cupertino is covering World Cup matches in Atlanta this summer with Soccer Down Here (SDH), an Atlanta-based soccer media outlet. Read More Anthropology student explores digital tipping and customer behavior June 26, 2026 As a barista, Alexandria Nottage has witnessed many customers hesitate whenever the digital payment screen asks whether they would like to leave a tip. Those daily interactions got Nottage thinking about how tipping had changed from a voluntary gesture of appreciation into something many customers now feel expected to do. To find out, Nottage, a Kennesaw State University anthropology major, conducted a research study examining how digital tipping influences customer behavior and perceptions. Engineering graduate rises above adversity to shape healthcare technology June 25, 2026 In May 2019, Tahir Upshaw walked across the stage at Kennesaw State University’s Commencement to earn his degree in mechanical engineering, a culminating moment after years of personal sacrifices and perseverance. Despite early setbacks in his academic career, Upshaw relished in earning his degree, in part, because of the community he built at Kennesaw State and through the mentorship of faculty in the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology (SPCEET). He has turned that experience into a fruitful career as an integration engineer and tech lead at Emory Healthcare, where he has contributed to innovative healthcare technology projects. Read More KSU student helps bring a fresh approach to music education using colors June 23, 2026 As a child, Kennesaw State University student Laurin McCoy loved music but struggled to understand traditional music notation. While she learned to play the piano by ear, the experience left her saddened that children might never discover or develop their musical talents simply because they were unable to read music. Years later, McCoy found an opportunity to help address that challenge through research. Read More AOPA announces 2026 Howard R. Thranhardt Award recipients, including Kennesaw State's Dr. Mark Geil June 23, 2026 AOPA announces 2026 Howard R. Thranhardt Award recipients, including Kennesaw State’s Dr. Mark Geil Read More Kennesaw State experts offer insight on World Cup topics June 23, 2026 Atlanta is an epicenter of the global sporting world as the city hosts matches in the FIFA Men’s World Cup soccer tournament. Kennesaw State University experts can offer insight on a range of topics related to soccer and the World Cup, including sport technology, sport science, fan loyalty, economic impact, brand marketing, hydration and nutrition, and the physics of a soccer kick. Read More Kennesaw State celebrates Juneteenth through art, music, and community June 22, 2026 Kennesaw State students, faculty, staff, and community members gathered throughout this past week to commemorate Juneteenth through a series of events hosted by Student Engagement and Support. Read More KSU master's graduates benefit from NIH-funded bridge program June 22, 2026 Recent Kennesaw State University graduate April Ford engaged in a program designed to help master’s students in the College of Science and Mathematics gain the experience they needed to pursue doctoral degrees elsewhere. She’ll stand as an example of the Peach State Bridges to the Doctorate program’s effectiveness, having earned her Master of Science in Integrative Biology (MSIB) and acceptance into a Ph.D. program. Ford, Jojo Croffie, and Lindsey Knight all earned their MSIB degrees, and thanks to enrichment through the Peach State Bridges to the Doctorate program, each will start a Ph.D. in the fall. Read More Twins who grew up at Kennesaw State graduate as nurses June 18, 2026 Katelyn Dockery remembers being pre-school age, sitting in her father’s office after school, coloring on a white board with markers. Her twin sister Taylor recalls going to Kennesaw State University basketball games and getting her face painted in the lobby at VyStar Arena. Their father, KSU Faculty Director of General Education in KSU’s Office of Academic Affairs Chris Dockery, remembers it all — basketball games, afternoons spent in his office with his daughters, taking them to lunch at The Commons, among other activities. And 21 years later, the Dockery family has cemented its legacy at KSU, with a pair of new graduates. Read More Ph.D. student selected for research appointment at Savannah River National Laboratory June 17, 2026 What began as a childhood spent working on cars with his father and older brother has led Matthew Azaroff to one of the nation’s premier research institutions. The Kennesaw State University doctoral student has been selected for a summer research internship at Savannah River National Laboratory, where he will conduct advanced manufacturing research alongside leading scientists and engineers. Read More KSU study explores how childhood trauma affects body and mind June 16, 2026 Traumatic events in childhood do not only leave emotional scars. Sometimes, they leave biological ones too. Saloni Patel, a first-year psychology major at Kennesaw State University, is studying how adverse childhood experiences — commonly known as ACEs — leave a measurable biological mark that can affect how we think, focus, and learn. Her research examines whether inflammation triggered by early-life stress contributes to the cognitive struggles some students face in the classroom. Bagwell College of Education recently welcomed nearly 1,300 elementary school students representing 63 schools for the Georgia Elementary Science Olympiad State Tournament. So for her, KSU – in particular, the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education – felt like home. Alumna earns competitive scholarship to study in Japan September 25, 2026 It was a trip to Japan during high school that sparked Leah Hackaday’s curiosity about how other countries operate and interact with each other, a curiosity that eventually led her to major in international affairs when she enrolled at Kennesaw State University. The opportunity to spend a semester in Japan during her junior year at KSU only grew her interest in the country. Today, thanks to earning a competitive scholarship from the Japanese government, Hackaday, a graduate of KSU’s School of Government and International Affairs, has now begun studying for a master’s degree in international affairs at Waseda University in Tokyo. Read More Kennesaw State architecture alumnus finds early career success August 28, 2026 Just one year after graduating from Kennesaw State University, Michael Rixom ’25 has reached a significant milestone in his profession. At just 23 years old, Rixom has achieved the rare distinction of becoming one of Georgia’s youngest licensed architects. Read More Kennesaw State University Alumni Association announces 2026-2027 officers July 09, 2026 The Kennesaw State University Alumni Association has elected its 2026–2027 officers, naming a distinguished group of alumni leaders who will help advance the Association's mission of fostering lifelong engagement among more than 160,000 Kennesaw State and Southern Polytechnic State graduates. Read More From KSU Owl Network to FIFA World Cup, alumna builds sports media career July 08, 2026 In preparation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Kennesaw State University alumna Maddie Crews ’24 marked her calendar for 49 consecutive days of covering the competition for multiple media outlets. Read More Engineering graduate rises above adversity to shape healthcare technology June 25, 2026 In May 2019, Tahir Upshaw walked across the stage at Kennesaw State University’s Commencement to earn his degree in mechanical engineering, a culminating moment after years of personal sacrifices and perseverance. Despite early setbacks in his academic career, Upshaw relished in earning his degree, in part, because of the community he built at Kennesaw State and through the mentorship of faculty in the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology (SPCEET). He has turned that experience into a fruitful career as an integration engineer and tech lead at Emory Healthcare, where he has contributed to innovative healthcare technology projects. Read More 'Triple Owl' turns passion for teaching into doctoral success June 11, 2026 For high school chemistry teacher Ashley Thomas, coming back to Kennesaw State University to earn a third post-graduate degree was an easy decision. A science teacher in DeKalb County Schools, Thomas is now a ‘Triple Owl,’ having previously earned a master's and education specialist degree in instructional technology, and now a Doctor of Education in Instructional Technology. So for her, KSU – in particular, the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education – felt like home. Read More KSU alumni return to the nest to lead a new generation April 27, 2026 The draw of home has proven irresistible for scores of Kennesaw State University graduates. A degree from Kennesaw State opens a treasure chest of opportunity, and alumni take skills and experiences acquired at KSU into their own lives. Five KSU grads did just that – achieved great things in the world at large before returning to the nest to mentor and teach the next generations of Owls. Read More KSU math grad moves up the ranks in Marines March 31, 2026 No amount of data crunching could have foretold the story of Zach Navejas ’14. His love for math propelled him to a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics from Kennesaw State University. He combined the knowledge gleaned from his upper-level courses with his ability to network for a consistent career in data science and consultation – but not without a false start. Read More Navy veteran, alumnus transforms his career through mechanical engineering March 25, 2026 After years of repairing aircraft electronics in the U.S. Navy and building systems for military aircraft, Chris Payne ’22 came to Kennesaw State University determined to change his future. What followed was a return to the classroom that set him on a new path toward an engineering career. Read More Architecture alumnus helps guide downtown Smyrna redevelopment March 10, 2026 When Luis Calvo ’10 left Barranquilla, Colombia, at 18 to study architecture, he envisioned himself designing buildings. Little did the College of Architecture and Construction Management (CACM) alumnus know that he’d be designing entire city centers, guiding one of the most ambitious redevelopment efforts in metro Atlanta. Since earning his Bachelor of Architecture from the former Southern Polytechnic State University, Calvo has gone on to become an associate principal and Atlanta studio lead for the urban planning and design firm MKSK, overseeing projects that shape communities across the Southeast and Midwest. At just 23 years old, Rixom has achieved the rare distinction of becoming one of Georgia’s youngest licensed architects. Read More Kennesaw State student explores the mental effects of workplace automation August 21, 2026 As new technologies become a larger part of the modern workplace, Kennesaw State University student Blessing Onyekachi is researching how working alongside them affects employees' mental health. As part of KSU’s Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP), architecture student Onyekachi is studying how workers adapt as automation becomes more common in industries such as construction, manufacturing, and logistics. Read More Kennesaw State architecture chair honored with ARCC Mary Kihl Distinguished Service Award July 09, 2026 When Professor of Architecture Saif Haq learned he had been selected to receive the 2025–2026 ARCC Mary Kihl Distinguished Service Award, the recognition carried special meaning. The Mary Kihl Distinguished Service Award recognizes individuals who have made significant, lasting contributions to architectural research through the consortium. Read More Kennesaw State architecture student wins Super South competition with community-focused design June 10, 2026 Kennesaw State University architecture student Madison Wall turned a vision for Atlanta's historic Sweet Auburn district into a first-place finish at the Super South conference and competition. Read More Associate professor earns Associated Schools of Construction regional educator award June 08, 2026 Kennesaw State University associate professor Minsoo Baek has earned the Associated Schools of Construction (ASC) Regional Outstanding Educator Award, recognizing his excellence in teaching, mentorship, and service to the construction education profession. Read More Architecture students earn AIA Georgia Design and Honor Awards June 01, 2026 Two student teams from Kennesaw State University’s College of Architecture and Construction Management were recently recognized at the 2026 American Institute of Architects Georgia (AIA Georgia) Design and Honor Awards. Read More Global architecture leaders gather at Kennesaw State for international research conference May 05, 2026 Kennesaw State University recently hosted an international architectural research conference, welcoming more than 200 scholars to address challenges like climate change, resource inequity, and sustainable urbanism. Organized by Kennesaw State’s Department of Architecture, the 2026 Architectural Research Centers Consortium (ARCC) and the European Association for Architectural Education (EAAE) International Conference was held April 8-11 at the Loews Atlanta Hotel and KSU’s Marietta Campus, carrying a theme of “local solutions for global issues.” Read More Architecture student thrives through leadership, design competitions, and community March 24, 2026 Raised in Rio de Janeiro, Gabriela de Almeida grew up surrounded by the vibrant culture and architecture of one of Brazil’s most iconic cities. It was there that she developed an early interest in architecture thanks to her mother, who once brought home a floor plan of her bedroom. Now an architecture student in KSU’s College of Architecture and Construction Management, de Almeida has since built a supportive community on campus. Dr. Bobbie Bailey School of Music enters educational partnership with Atlanta Symphony September 10, 2026 Kennesaw State University’s Dr. Bobbie Bailey School of Music and the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra (ASO) are joining forces to create new opportunities for the next generation of musicians in Metro Atlanta. Beginning this fall, the educational partnership will connect KSU music students with professional musicians through masterclasses, performance opportunities and access to ASO concerts — bringing students closer to the artistry, mentorship and professional experiences that define a career on the stage. Read More Reflecting on KSU Dance's 20-year journey May 27, 2026 In November, the University marked the 20th anniversary of KSU Dance with a series of performances choreographed by Pulinkala, KSU faculty members Shannon Alvis and Autumn Eckman, and renowned guest artist Yankalle Filtser. Pulinkala’s choreographic work, which featured 10 current students and four alumni, was intended to bridge generations of dancers who have helped shape the program. Read More KSU modern dance graduate sets sights on becoming a choreographer May 22, 2026 Deontae Nelson wants to travel the world and better understand how people in other countries consume dance. Now, the 2026 Kennesaw State University graduate is one step closer to doing just that. Read More Dance major makes most of his KSU journey May 06, 2026 Deontae Nelson likes to say that everyone is on their own journey, as much for himself as for those around him. Nelson’s journey has seen him serving in the Army National Guard, then earning an associate degree in biology from Georgia Military College before arriving at Kennesaw State University in 2022. All the while, he never could shake the idea of studying dance and decided to dive headlong into doing just that. Next week, he’ll graduate with his Bachelor of Arts in Dance with a concentration in Modern Dance from the Robert S. Geer College of the Arts, culminating one journey and commencing another. Read More New Connections Project provides shared learning for students and the incarcerated March 30, 2026 Kennesaw State University students are using theatre to help incarcerated persons prepare for life after prison, while gaining a better understanding of the population they will serve in their future careers. The initiative is part of the New Connections Project, a partnership between KSU and Common Good Atlanta, a not-for-profit organization that provides higher education for people who are or have been incarcerated. Read More Big semester for KSU's Chamber Singers includes conference, Spain tour January 30, 2026 Notwithstanding the joy of performing timeless music in front of appreciative crowds, Kennesaw State University juniors Trey Stannard and Nadia Wilson are looking forward to Spain’s food. That’s just one part of an important couple of months for KSU’s Chamber Singers – chosen to perform at this week’s annual conference for the Georgia Music Educators’ Association in Athens before heading to Spain over Spring Break for a seven-concert tour in March. Read More Wind ensemble one of two KSU groups chosen for Georgia Music Educators' Association performance November 12, 2025 A native Georgian, Kennesaw State University student Tyler Smith knows well the prestige of the Georgia Music Educators’ Association annual in-service conference. It conjures memories of music ensembles of all levels performing for a distinguished audience, and young musicians learning from some of the state’s best talent. Now, the alto saxophonist will have the chance to perform at this January’s conference in Athens as a member of KSU’s wind ensemble, appearing at the conference for the first time since 2017. Read More Kennesaw State's Arthur Liou installed as Audrey Bailey Morgan Distinguished Endowed Dean's Chair November 05, 2025 Kennesaw State University’s Arthur Liou was installed as the inaugural Audrey Bailey Morgan Distinguished Endowed Dean’s Chair in the Robert S. Geer Family College of the Arts on Wednesday at Morgan Performance Hall. Read More Kennesaw State vocal music instructor named 2025 Jazz Hero by national organization October 23, 2025 A lifetime as a performer and eight years as a Kennesaw State University instructor have culminated in Karla Harris being named Atlanta’s Jazz Hero for 2025 by the Jazz Journalists’ Association. Read More Kennesaw State assistant professor blends art and technology to inspire next generation September 26, 2025 Shuchita Mishra works at the intersection of art, education, business, and technology. The Kennesaw State University assistant professor of illustration and sequential art comes to academia from a technology and marketing background, but couldn’t shake the artist within. Having developed a passion to tell stories with her drawings, she changed the course of her life and shifted focus to art education. After earning a Master of Fine Arts in Comics from the California College of the Arts, Mishra completed a writer’s residency at the Writer’s House in Pittsburgh while working for the Carnegie Museum of Art, then applied for a limited-term teaching position at Kennesaw State. Read More KSU's Megan Stoltzfus named Conference USA SAAC Choice Award recipient June 03, 2026 Conference USA has announced that Kennesaw State Director of Student-Athlete Development Megan Stoltzfus has been selected as the 2025-26 Conference USA SAAC Choice Award recipient. Read More Athletics momentum carries Owl Nation to Oregon, March Madness March 20, 2026 Kennesaw State University graduate Forest Callaway ’17 had known for years he was going to be in Portland’s Moda Center on Thursday night for the NCAA Tournament’s West Regional. What he didn’t know, however, was that he would be welcoming his alma mater to his home venue and opening the doors for the members of Owl Nation who winged their way 2,300 miles to the Pacific Northwest. From alumni and donors to students and fans, many Owls were on hand Thursday as Kennesaw State took on Gonzaga in the opening round of March Madness, fresh off winning the Conference USA tournament championship. Read More Momentum builds at KSU as Owls return to March Madness March 16, 2026 Fresh off its first Conference USA tournament title, the Kennesaw State University men’s basketball team joined an exuberant Owl Nation at VyStar Arena to learn its March Madness opponent during a Selection Sunday watch party. The Owls, who earned their second NCAA Division I Men’s Basketball Tournament berth in four years, were announced as the No. 14 seed in the West Region. They will face No. 3 seed Gonzaga at the Moda Center in Portland, Oregon on Thursday. Read More Owls celebrate KSU Day at State Capitol February 05, 2026 Kennesaw State President Kathy S. Schwaig, Deputy AD Brad Ledford and head football coach Jerry Mack were all on-hand at the Georgia State Capitol on Tuesday to celebrate KSU Day. Read More Business builds community through decade-long support of Kennesaw State athletics January 22, 2026 For Jay Cunningham, owner of Superior Plumbing in Kennesaw, providing sponsorship of school athletics programs is a fundamental part of building the community. The way he sees it, the gifts he and Superior Plumbing have given to Kennesaw State University for more than a decade are a key part of his business. Read More Mickey Dunn Stadium roars to life this spring January 14, 2026 When Owls shortstop Shamaar McDuffie laces up his spikes for the Kennesaw State University baseball team this spring, he will be among the first players to set foot inside Mickey Dunn Stadium at Henssler Financial Field. Named for alumnus Mickey Dunn ’18, who provided the lead gift in its development, the new facility sits on the site of the former Fred Stillwell Stadium and cuts an impressive figure with expanded seating capacity and improved amenities. The Ingenico Fintech Hub officially opened on Sept. 28 in the Michael J. Coles College of Business, representing the latest milestone in Kennesaw State’s efforts to expand financial technology education and industry collaboration. Read More Kennesaw State rises in U.S. News rankings of top universities September 23, 2026 Kennesaw State University continues to rise in stature among the nation’s universities while earning a top spot in Georgia for undergraduate engineering programs, according to the U.S. News & World Report 2027 Best Colleges rankings released on Sept. 22. Read More Two KSU students trade the Gold Dome for Capitol Hill August 24, 2026 Six months ago, Jada Barronton and Saideep Chilukuri answered phones in House and Senate offices under the Gold Dome. Over the summer, they both helped track legislation and conduct policy research for U.S. congressional offices on Capitol Hill. The two Kennesaw State University students, who received the university’s D.C. Owls Scholarship, spent their summer interning in Washington, and both credit a semester at the Georgia State Capitol with helping them succeed. Read More Kennesaw State's Mookerji Innovation Fund hits 50 startups in just over five years July 15, 2026 A little more than five years ago, Kennesaw State University set out to prove that student entrepreneurs could build real, fundable companies. Through KSU's First-Year Scholars Program, she turned that curiosity into award-winning research on restaurant franchising. Kennesaw State University students Emily Lesmes and Alaina Jean have been studying exactly that. Working with Associate Professor of Marketing and Sales Hyunju Shin, the students who are participants in the First-Years Scholars Program are exploring whether courtroom fashion shapes how the public perceives someone's guilt, remorse, or sincerity. Kennesaw State and Ingenico create hub for fintech innovation and learning September 29, 2026 Building on Kennesaw State University’s distinction as the first institution in Georgia to offer both undergraduate and graduate degrees in financial technologies, students now have a dedicated space to apply classroom learning to real-world challenges through the newly opened Ingenico Fintech Hub. The Ingenico Fintech Hub officially opened on Sept. 28 in the Michael J. Coles College of Business, representing the latest milestone in Kennesaw State’s efforts to expand financial technology education and industry collaboration. Read More Launch '26 celebrates new school year, sustained momentum August 20, 2026 Momentum provided the theme as Kennesaw State University’s faculty and staff gathered at VyStar Arena on Aug. 20 to celebrate the opening of the 2026-27 academic year with Launch ’26. Speakers and guests enjoyed a look into KSU’s future, illustrated by visions of continued growth, academic excellence, ascendant and relevant research, and continued student success. Read More Kennesaw State's economic impact tops $2.55 billion August 13, 2026 Kennesaw State University continues to be a major economic engine in metro Atlanta, growing its economic impact to more than $2.55 billion in fiscal year 2025, according to a University System of Georgia (USG) report released on Aug. 13. Read More Kennesaw State adds more on-campus housing for students August 13, 2026 Kennesaw State University is expanding its on-campus housing options for students by opening a new residence hall for the 2026-27 academic year and renovating an existing residential community. Read More KSU bolsters infrastructure to support student experience, University's growth August 12, 2026 From new residence halls to expanded academic and student support facilities, Kennesaw State University’s Campus Master Plan is taking shape through a wave of completed and ongoing projects that are transforming both campuses and positioning the university for continued growth. Read More Marietta Campus to feature new dining, transportation, and campus upgrades this fall August 11, 2026 Students returning to Kennesaw State University’s Marietta Campus this fall will find more dining options, new bus routes, and several campus improvements designed to enhance the overall student experience. Leading the updates is the opening of the Robin and Doug Shore Innovation Center. Officially opened in April, the new facility serves as a hub for interdisciplinary research while also providing students with a place to study, gather, and recharge between classes. Read More Kennesaw State is harnessing momentum to advance research, elevate the student experience, and build for the future August 10, 2026 A theme is emerging for Kennesaw State’s ascension as one of the fastest-growing institutions in the country: momentum. Read More Kennesaw State expands on-campus residential housing with the opening of The Summit II August 04, 2026 Kennesaw State University has officially opened The Summit II, a residence hall designed to foster connection, belonging, and student success while adding a new on-campus housing option for first-year students. Read More Kennesaw State University showcases global impact through the FIFA World Cup 2026 July 20, 2026 With the world’s eyes fixed on Atlanta during the FIFA World Cup 2026™, Kennesaw State University emerged as a key partner in executing one of the globe’s most celebrated sporting traditions, emphasizing KSU’s growing status as a vital contributor to Georgia’s economic success. Read More Kennesaw State recognizes outstanding staff at annual awards ceremony April 30, 2026 Kennesaw State University leaders on Wednesday presented awards to five of the institution’s most outstanding employees at its annual staff awards event at the KSU Center. Kennesaw State researcher earns prestigious NSF CAREER Award October 02, 2026 Kennesaw State University Associate Professor of Software Engineering Nasrin Dehbozorgi has received a National Science Foundation Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER) Award, one of NSF’s most prestigious honors for early-career faculty. The award will support her work advancing STEM education through a novel agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework. Read More Kennesaw State researcher receives NIH Grant to study sleep apnea October 01, 2026 Kennesaw State University researcher Shumit Saha has received a $235,520 grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to develop artificial intelligence tools that analyze snoring patterns to identify where the upper airway collapses during sleep and predict whether patients may respond to hypoglossal nerve stimulation. Read More Ph.D. student advances research regarding AI integration with devices with limited computing power September 29, 2026 In the artificial intelligence (AI) era, hospitals can leverage AI to uncover valuable insights from patient data, but privacy requirements and devices with low computing capabilities present hurdles to widespread adoption. At Kennesaw State University, Ph.D. student Nazmus Shakib Shadin is studying how hospitals can help train AI while keeping records private and using the equipment they already have. Read More Kennesaw State researcher developing safer, more efficient computing systems for intelligent vehicles September 24, 2026 Modern vehicles are becoming computers on wheels, powered by increasingly complex software and artificial intelligence. As those systems take on more responsibility, they must process information quickly and reliably enough to keep critical functions running safely. Kennesaw State University computer science researcher Kun Suo is working to improve how those systems operate through a $356,782 National Science Foundation (NSF) grant focused on developing more efficient and secure computing infrastructure for intelligent vehicles. Read More Kennesaw State software engineering student develops AI-powered navigation system September 11, 2026 For Kennesaw State University software engineering student Robert Hoeh, finding a room inside an unfamiliar building could one day be as simple as asking a question. Hoeh is helping develop an AI-powered augmented reality navigation system that lets users ask for directions and guides them through complex indoor spaces. The technology could improve accessibility for people with cognitive disabilities while also helping first responders navigate unfamiliar buildings more quickly. Read More Student research into AI-powered crop monitoring system aims to prevent plant loss August 26, 2026 According to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization, plant pests and diseases destroy up to 40% of crops worldwide each year, threatening jobs and the global food supply. Kennesaw State University computer science major Brendan Miller is working on technology that could help farmers catch those problems before they spread. Read More Kennesaw State professor earns Texas Innovator's Award for AI platform supporting student success July 22, 2026 Kennesaw State University assistant professor Sagnik Dakshit, of the College of Computing and Software Engineering, has earned a Texas Innovator's Award for developing an artificial intelligence-powered platform that supports student success. He received the honor for creating VTA, or Virtual Teaching Assistant, a tool designed to provide personalized academic support while helping instructors improve learning outcomes. Read More From personal tragedy to innovation: Professor advances virtual reality grief support July 14, 2026 Shaped by experience navigating loss and grief, a Kennesaw State University researcher is leveraging emerging technologies that could improve access to community and support for bereaved parents. Funded by a two-year grant from the National Science Foundation, Lei Zhang, a human-computer interaction researcher in College of Computing and Software Engineering, is building a virtual reality system that lets bereaved parents meet, share memories, and process grief together in a shared immersive digital space, inspired by his own experiences losing a child to cancer. Read More Ph.D. student finds AI can detect warning signs of global oil crises before they happen July 07, 2026 As geopolitical conflicts continue to disrupt global energy markets, Kennesaw State University Ph.D. student Nzubechukwu Ohalete found that artificial intelligence (AI) can identify warning signs of major oil crises weeks before they occur. Read More Kennesaw State awards first computer science doctoral degrees May 11, 2026 This month marks a landmark achievement for Kennesaw State University as it celebrates the graduation of the first two students from the new doctoral program in computer science, established in 2022. Kennesaw State professor earns national award for contribution to education August 07, 2026 Kennesaw State University professor Erik Malewski has received a national award for his decades of contribution to teaching and learning. A professor of curriculum studies in the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education, Malewski has been selected to receive the Curriculum & Pedagogy Group Lifetime Award. The national honor recognizes scholars whose careers have made lasting contributions to curriculum and pedagogy through scholarship, mentorship, and leadership. Read More KSU student helps bring a fresh approach to music education using colors June 23, 2026 As a child, Kennesaw State University student Laurin McCoy loved music but struggled to understand traditional music notation. While she learned to play the piano by ear, the experience left her saddened that children might never discover or develop their musical talents simply because they were unable to read music. Years later, McCoy found an opportunity to help address that challenge through research. Read More Bagwell College of Education hosts 2026 Georgia Elementary Science Olympiad June 15, 2026 Kennesaw State University’s Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education recently welcomed nearly 1,300 elementary school students representing 63 schools for the Georgia Elementary Science Olympiad State Tournament. Read More 'Triple Owl' turns passion for teaching into doctoral success June 11, 2026 For high school chemistry teacher Ashley Thomas, coming back to Kennesaw State University to earn a third post-graduate degree was an easy decision. A science teacher in DeKalb County Schools, Thomas is now a ‘Triple Owl,’ having previously earned a master's and education specialist degree in instructional technology, and now a Doctor of Education in Instructional Technology. So for her, KSU – in particular, the Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education – felt like home. Read More Kennesaw State, Fulton County Schools teaming to create pathways into teaching careers April 14, 2026 Kennesaw State University and Fulton County Schools are partnering to create new opportunities for high school students to accelerate their college education and pursue careers in teaching. Through the dual enrollment initiative, Fulton County students can earn college credit while in high school, gain early classroom experience, and have a streamlined admissions process into Kennesaw State’s Clarice C. and Leland H. Bagwell College of Education. Leaders from Fulton County Schools and Kennesaw State signed the agreement during a ceremony on Tuesday at KSU. Read More NSF-funded project explores the use of AI-powered chatbots to prepare future educators April 01, 2026 Funded by a three-year, $300,000 National Science Foundation grant, Associate Professor of Instructional Technology Dabae Lee developed an AI-powered agent system that simulates student interactions. The aim is to give pre-service teachers practice in “responsive teaching,” which is the ability to elicit and interpret students’ thinking and to extend their mathematical ideas by questioning. Read More Associate professor, CrossFit athlete finds strength in motion while navigating multiple sclerosis March 13, 2026 About ten years ago, Jennifer Wells stepped off a boat while visiting Robben Island in South Africa. She immediately felt what she describes as ‘pins and needles’ in her feet, a pervasive pain she thought was due to her cramped sitting position on the vessel. She thought it would go away in a few hours, but it didn’t. The symptoms only got worse, leading to numbness. For Wells, an associate professor of higher education and student affairs at Kennesaw State University, that episode marked the beginning of her journey with multiple sclerosis (MS), a journey of resilience that has taken her to the world stage as a CrossFit adaptive athlete. Read More Marrielle Myers elected next president of the Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators February 27, 2026 Marrielle Myers was recently elected president of the Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE), the largest professional organization devoted to improving mathematics teacher education. AMTE includes more than 1,000 members, including professors, researchers, and policy experts, who focus on the professional development of K–12 mathematics teachers. Read More Georgia Highlands College and Kennesaw State University expand transfer pathways February 25, 2026 Georgia Highlands College (GHC) and Kennesaw State University (KSU) are expanding their LINK partnership, a collaborative initiative to create seamless transfer pathways and expand academic opportunities for students. Read More Kennesaw State among nation's top universities for online degrees in U.S. News rankings January 29, 2026 Continuing its rise as a leading provider of online education, Kennesaw State University earned national distinction in U.S. News & World Report’s 2026 Best Online Programs. KSU also ranked first in Georgia in two categories, Best Online MBA and Best Online MBA for Veterans. Engineering student creates robotic hand designed to track patient health October 09, 2026 A robotic hand capable of grasping a patient’s wrist and measuring vital signs may sound futuristic, but Kennesaw State University mechatronics engineering student Daksh Garg is already bringing the concept to life through research in robotics and biomedical sensing. The Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology student is building a 3D-printed robotic hand equipped with sensors designed to collect health information while interacting with a person. Read More Kennesaw State researchers receive NSF grant to advance soft robotics education October 08, 2026 Soft robots that can bend, flex, and safely interact with people are becoming more common in research and industry. However, many engineering students still have little exposure to the technology. Kennesaw State University researchers are working to change that with the support of a recent National Science Foundation (NSF) grant. Read More Engineering student uses NASA data to study distant star systems October 07, 2026 Kennesaw State University electrical engineering student Thi Tran never imagined herself conducting astronomy research. Now, she is using data from a NASA satellite to help researchers distinguish distant planets from stars that can produce nearly identical signals. Read More Engineering student combines technical and marketing skills through hands-on experiences October 05, 2026 Kennesaw State University student Cynthia Konziase is building a versatile skill set by combining industrial and systems engineering with marketing and hands-on industry experience through opportunities within the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology (SPCEET). Read More Student cooks up success through engineering and content creation September 28, 2026 When Kennesaw State University engineering student Joel Louise began creating cooking videos this summer, he knew very little about preparing meals or producing social media content. What he did understand was how to analyze a problem, learn from mistakes, and improve a process. Louise developed those skills through KSU’s First-Year Scholars Program, an early research experience he credits with inspiring his approach to content creation. Read More Kennesaw State rises in U.S. News rankings of top universities September 23, 2026 Kennesaw State University continues to rise in stature among the nation’s universities while earning a top spot in Georgia for undergraduate engineering programs, according to the U.S. News & World Report 2027 Best Colleges rankings released on Sept. 22. Read More Hornet Hub gives Kennesaw State competition teams space to build, innovate September 18, 2026 Kennesaw State University celebrated a new chapter in hands-on learning with the official opening of the Hornet Hub on the Marietta Campus. The 12,000-square-foot facility provides student competition teams, which design and build projects for regional and national competitions, dedicated space and resources to bring their work from concept to completion. Read More Kennesaw State student developing robotic rehabilitation arm inspired by family experience September 08, 2026 Watching his grandfather lose mobility after a traumatic accident gave Kennesaw State University student Kai Clifford a firsthand look at how difficult everyday movement can become. Now, the senior mechanical engineering student is using robotics research to explore ways rehabilitation could become more comfortable and effective. Read More Mechatronics engineering student uses AI-powered system to keep waterways clean July 30, 2026 It is estimated that up to 23 million metric tons of plastic enter waterways each year, according to the United Nations Environment Programme. While harmful materials continue to plague governments around the world, a Kennesaw State University student is developing an artificial intelligence-powered system to detect litter before it reaches the ocean. Mechatronics engineering student Saam Grami is creating a system that detects, classifies, and tracks floating litter in rivers. Read More Kennesaw State professors use NSF grant to strengthen semiconductor education through interactive learning July 29, 2026 As the United States works to strengthen its semiconductor industry, Kennesaw State University researchers are helping prepare the next generation of engineers. Through a National Science Foundation-funded project, they are using interactive visualizations to make one of electrical engineering's most challenging subjects easier for students to understand. Kennesaw State names nursing simulation lab in honor of Katherine Scott October 06, 2026 Kennesaw State University has honored longtime donor Katherine A. Scott by naming a nursing simulation lab in recognition of her $1 million gift establishing the Katherine A. Scott Nursing Scholarship Endowment. Read More Kennesaw State student publishes study on alcohol's impact on Ugandan women September 10, 2026 Few undergraduates can add “lead author in a peer-reviewed journal” to their list of accomplishments. Kennesaw State University student and Harry S. Truman Scholarship finalist Allisa George is one of them. George, an Honors student double majoring in public health and biology, is the first author of a National Institutes of Health-funded study examining alcohol and mental health among women in Uganda recently published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. Read More Kennesaw State appoints Tracy Fasolino as associate dean, Wellstar School of Nursing director August 06, 2026 Kennesaw State University has named accomplished nursing educator and healthcare leader Tracy Fasolino, Ph.D., as associate dean and director of the Wellstar School of Nursing (WSON) and professor of nursing, effective Aug. 1. Read More From KSU Owl Network to FIFA World Cup, alumna builds sports media career July 08, 2026 In preparation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Kennesaw State University alumna Maddie Crews ’24 marked her calendar for 49 consecutive days of covering the competition for multiple media outlets. Read More Wellstar College launches first study abroad program to Amsterdam, providing a transformative global experience for KSU students July 02, 2026 Kennesaw State University's Wellstar College launched its first Amsterdam study abroad program, giving students immersive global public health experiences through research, cultural engagement, and experiential learning. Read More AOPA announces 2026 Howard R. Thranhardt Award recipients, including Kennesaw State's Dr. Mark Geil June 23, 2026 AOPA announces 2026 Howard R. Thranhardt Award recipients, including Kennesaw State’s Dr. Mark Geil Read More Twins who grew up at Kennesaw State graduate as nurses June 18, 2026 Katelyn Dockery remembers being pre-school age, sitting in her father’s office after school, coloring on a white board with markers. Her twin sister Taylor recalls going to Kennesaw State University basketball games and getting her face painted in the lobby at VyStar Arena. Their father, KSU Faculty Director of General Education in KSU’s Office of Academic Affairs Chris Dockery, remembers it all — basketball games, afternoons spent in his office with his daughters, taking them to lunch at The Commons, among other activities. And 21 years later, the Dockery family has cemented its legacy at KSU, with a pair of new graduates. Many have studied under the tutelage of faculty in the Department of Exercise Science and Sport Management, the latter integrating their personal research interests to set up students for success beyond the classroom. The opportunity to spend a semester in Japan during her junior year at KSU only grew her interest in the country. Today, thanks to earning a competitive scholarship from the Japanese government, Hackaday, a graduate of KSU’s School of Government and International Affairs , has now begun studying for a master’s degree in international affairs at Waseda University in Tokyo. “I’m incredibly honored to have been selected for this scholarship,” said Hackaday, who also minored in Japanese at KSU. “This is something I’ve been working toward for a couple of years, so having it confirmed was a strange feeling. It honestly didn’t sink in until I landed in Japan.” The Japan government’s MEXT Scholarship provides international students with an opportunity to study at Japanese universities, immersing them in Japanese society and language. It covers full tuition, airfare, and provides a monthly living stipend for international students. With support from KSU’s Education Abroad , Hackaday spent six months in a study-abroad program in Japan at Toyo University, learning even more about the culture and learning some Japanese along the way. “My semester abroad gave me the confidence and independence to take this next step,” she said. “After living and studying on my own in Japan for six months, I wanted to return for a longer period.” At Waseda, Hackaday hopes to strengthen her research skills, deepen her understanding of international education, improve her Japanese, and build relationships with faculty and students from around the world. She plans to research international higher education and how it can be used to benefit the global community. “I chose to study Japan as its aging population is a case study for policy challenges that many developed countries are beginning to face,” she said. Hackaday said her KSU journey provided a strong foundation in theory, critical thinking, academic writing, and research. She credits faculty members like Eric Castater, John Moran and Stephen Collins for encouraging her to always pursue more opportunities and knowledge. “Dr. Collins and especially Dr. Castater provided advice on my research proposal for Waseda University, which no doubt helped me build a stronger application,” she said. “I would not have the knowledge or academic confidence needed to pursue this scholarship without their influence.” For Ramazan Kilinc, director of KSU’s School of Government and International Affairs, Hackaday’s accomplishment is a proud moment. "Leah’s achievement is a source of great pride for KSU and SGIA,” Ramazan said. “Earning the prestigious MEXT Scholarship reflects her hard work, curiosity, and the transformative power of international education, which she took during her undergraduate studies. We look forward to seeing the impact she will make through her studies in Japan and future career in international affairs.” As Hackaday settles into her new life at Waseda, she is enjoying Japan’s food and culture while looking forward to all the adventures this next chapter will bring. “I’m nervous but excited beyond compare and very thankful to everyone who helped me achieve this goal,” she said. “Receiving this scholarship is a reminder not to doubt myself and never give up without trying.” – Story by Christin Senior Photo provided Related Stories Kennesaw State rises in U.S. News rankings of top universities KSU associate professor honored with 2026 Georgia Civic Excellence Award Kennesaw State students expand research horizons in India Kennesaw State architecture alumnus finds early career success A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State University offers undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral degrees to its more than 51,000 students. Leading the board as president is Wayne McGary (BS '99), vice president at Croy Engineering. Joining the executive leadership team are Ericka Bayonne (MS '97), chief communications officer for the State Road and Tollway Authority, serving as vice president, and Devon Faulk (BBA '93), selling partner services manager at Amazon, serving as secretary. Caric Martin (ABA '76), director of statewide engagement at Georgia's Own Credit Union, will continue serving as immediate past president, providing guidance and continuity to the board. Together, the officers will lead the Association's 24-member Board of Directors. The KSU Alumni Association’s mission is to strengthen connections between alumni and the university, recognize the achievements of Forever Owls, and inspire graduates to remain engaged with Kennesaw State for generations to come. From the Association’s annual Alumni Homecoming Tailgate to its annual support of Competition Teams, the KSU Alumni Association is continuously bringing Forever Owls together and supporting current students. Wayne McGary will serve a one-year renewable term as President. A graduate of Southern Polytechnic State University (SPSU), the parent of a Kennesaw State graduate, and a current KSU master's student, McGary brings decades of service and a deep connection to the university to his new leadership role. In addition to serving on the KSU Alumni Association Board, he is a member of the Southern Polytechnic College of Engineering and Engineering Technology Industry Advisory Board. His lifelong commitment to Kennesaw State, combined with his broad leadership experience, positions him well to serve as President of the Alumni Association. “As someone who was a nontraditional student balancing a full-time career while attending classes part-time, I know firsthand the value of a Kennesaw State education and the lifelong connections it creates,” said McGary. “I’m honored to serve as president of the KSU Alumni Association Board of Directors and look forward to working alongside my fellow board members to strengthen opportunities for alumni to stay connected and give back to the university.” “Kennesaw State’s alumni community is unique in its history, and the Alumni Association plays a vital role in strengthening lifelong connections of our Forever Owls,” said Frances Beusse, associate vice president of alumni & constituent engagement. “We are thrilled to have Wayne serving as President. His passion for Kennesaw State and his commitment to service will help build on that momentum as we continue creating new opportunities for alumni to stay connected and make an impact. The KSU Alumni Association Board of Directors also welcomed three newly elected at-large members who began their three-year terms on July 1. · Bethany Bagwell (BS ’11), Jefferson, Ga. · David Clarke (BS ’20), Douglas, Ga. · Oscelius Farrar III (BS ’17), Austell, Ga. The KSU Alumni Association works closely with university leadership and the Division of University Advancement to support programs, events, and initiatives that connect KSU and SPSU graduates across the region and around the world while advancing the University’s mission.
